jobs.description:
ABOUT US

Join us in inspiring everyone to express their unique beauty.

IPSY is the beauty industry’s most powerful platform, uniting brands, creators, and hyper-engaged consumers with unprecedented access to each other through the ultimate beauty membership. Home to sample-size subscription IPSY Original, full-size subscription IPSY Extra, and quarterly, limited-edition collection IPSY Ultimate, we curate beauty for millions of members so they can play, explore, and express their unique beauty every day.

We think self-discovery, self-expression, and confidence are beautiful. Agree? Then join us! Explore careers and learn more about our values, culture, and benefits across all our brands: IPSY Careers.

We're proud to be a remote-first company. Our fully remote team members have the chance to live and work where they want, because we believe work should fit into your life—not the other way around. We offer monthly virtual activities, company-wide offsites, professional development, and learning sessions, to help our team members stay connected, engaged, and impactful while working virtually.

United States Remote: Remote positions which may be performed in any of the states where IPSY has established a Business presence: Arizona, California, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Kansas, Massachusetts, Missouri, North Carolina, New York, New Jersey, Nevada, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Texas, Utah and Washington. California Privacy Notice

We don't ask for software downloads (except Zoom) and we will never ask for sensitive information (like SSN/bank info). Suspect fraud? Report it to law enforcement and recruiting@ipsy.com.

About the Role:

This role owns the design of IPSY’s printed collateral — the narrative and educational materials inside every subscription box — and provides creative support across IPSY’s event portfolio, from customer-facing activations to signature company events like the Brand & Creator Forum (IPSIES) and internal offsites. The role also supports packaging design for subscription boxes and related merchandise needs. It’s a role for a designer who can move fluidly between print-based editorial design and experiential/environmental creative, while maintaining IPSY’s brand standards across every touchpoint.

This position reports to the Sr. Manager, Art Direction and can be remote from any of the states that IPSY is authorized to hire.

What You’ll Be Doing:

Collateral Design

• Design and produce collateral across all monthly and quarterly subscription programs: (IPSY Original, Extra, Ultimate, Wellness) as well as ad hoc offerings like The Edit

• Ensure designs align with the monthly 360 creative direction

• Maintain IPSY brand standards across layout, typography, imagery, and color

• Collaborate on image selects from monthly photo shoots

Event Creative Support

• Partner with the Events Team, Producers, and other cross-functional stakeholders on creative needs across IPSY’s event portfolio — from smaller customer- and brand-facing activations to signature annual events like the Brand & Creator Forum (IPSIES) and company offsites

• Develop event mood boards, creative concepts, and overall visual direction/design systems in partnership with the Senior Manager, Art Direction and event leads

• Maintain consistency with IPSY's brand identity and visual standards across all packaging

What We Are Looking For:

• Strong print/editorial design skills, with experience designing for narrative or educational content, not just marketing collateral

• Experience in experiential, environmental, or event design — comfortable designing for physical spaces, not just screens or print

jobs.title: Thought Leader Liaison, Southwest Region
jobs.description:
Amylyx has an audacious mission to usher in a new era for treating diseases with high unmet needs. Where others see challenges, we see opportunities that we pursue with urgency, rigorous science, and unwavering commitment to the communities we serve. We are a clinical-stage company currently focused on post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH), Wolfram syndrome, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

Our mission is powered by our people. Our core values – be audacious, be curious, be authentic, be engaged, and be accountable – creating a culture of caring. Amylyx has assembled an experienced team ready to take action because the communities we serve have no time to wait. If you share our passion and are determined to tackle some of medicine’s toughest problems, we encourage you to read the opportunity below and apply.

The Opportunity

As a member of the marketing team, the Thought Leader Liaison, Southwest Region is a field-based individual contributor responsible for advancing Amylyx’s commercial objectives through strategic and compliant stakeholder engagement and insight generation across the assigned geography. The TLL cultivates professional relationships with key external stakeholders, delivers actionable market insights, and executes stakeholder engagement strategies that support brand performance, launch readiness, and organizational priorities. Working collaboratively across Marketing, Sales, Market Access, Medical Affairs, and Compliance, this role serves as a critical connector between external stakeholders and internal strategy, ensuring external stakeholder insights inform key business decisions. The TLL plays a critical role in elevating the voice of the healthcare community within Amylyx, helping ensure commercial strategies, educational initiatives, and engagement plans reflect evolving market needs and opportunities. This position reports to the Senior Director, Thought Leader Liaison Lead and serves as an extension of the U.S. Marketing team.

This opportunity is based in the Southwest and incumbents for this role should reside within the region: Arizona, California or Nevada

Amylyx may consider highly qualified candidates with more extensive and directly relevant experience for a Senior Thought Leader Liaison position.  The appropriate level will be determined based on the selected candidate’s qualifications, experience and demonstrated capabilities.

Responsibilities

• Serve as a strategic cross-functional partner to Marketing, Market Access, Sales Leadership, Medical Affairs, and Compliance, ensuring coordinated, compliant, and impactful stakeholder engagement.

jobs.title: Harness Design Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Radiant is seeking a Harness Design Engineer to support the design, build, and integration of electrical wire harnesses in a fast-paced startup environment. You’ll work alongside experienced mechanical and electrical engineers to solve challenging problems in system architecture, sensor/actuator selection, packaging, and system integration for advanced hardware. This role offers hands-on exposure to end-to-end hardware development from CAD and analysis through build, test, and validation.



RESPONSIBILITIES & DUTIES:

 - Own the design of the harnessing system from concept to integration, and serve as the subject matter expert on the interconnection between electrical and hardware systems.

 - Create harness drawings for manufacturing and act as the primary point of contact for the harness manufacturing team.

 - Support the creation of the reactor electrical schematics using Zuken E3 Cable and maintain the pinout tables throughout the design cycle.

 - Make decisions about conductor sizing, wire type, and shielding methods for low and high voltage using industry standards for guidance.

 - Use an understanding of electrical failure mechanisms, including voltage drop, thermal effects, and interference, to identify and mitigate risks.

 - Select materials, with support from the materials team, for harnessing in challenging environments across the reactor.

 - Support technicians with harness integration on the reactor as the system owner.

 - Work with the electrical team to commission the system and troubleshoot issues across the reactor.

 - Provide nonconformance solutions throughout the build and integration phases of development to limit program delays and maximize system uptime.

 


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a closely related field from an accredited institution.

 - 3+ Years of professional hands-on harness design or manufacturing experience.

 - Strong understanding of harnessing architecture, grounding schemas, power requirements, and shielding.

 - Strong understanding of electrical systems and the ability to interpret schematics.

jobs.description:
ABOUT ABRIDGE

Founded in 2018, Abridge is the first AI-native clinician intelligence platform organized around the patient, built for clinicians, and designed to help health systems coordinate the clinical, financial, and evidence-based decisions for every moment of care. Powered by purpose-built AI for healthcare, Abridge connects patients, providers, payers, and life sciences companies. This year, the platform will support more than 100 million patient-clinician conversations across more than 300 of the largest and most complex health systems in the U.S. With deep workflow integration, the Abridge clinician intelligence platform has been validated to support encounters in 28+ languages across specialties and care settings.

Abridge is setting the industry standard for the responsible deployment of Al across health systems with continual and transparent Al evaluation. Clinical decision support references and cites gold-standard sources of evidence, and features like Linked Evidence map AI-generated documentation to source data, helping clinicians quickly trust and verify the output.

Abridge was awarded Best in KLAS for Ambient AI in 2025 and 2026, in addition to other accolades, including TIME Best Inventions of 2024 and 2025, CNBC Disruptor 2025, and Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies 2025.

We are a growing team of practicing clinicians, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to transform healthcare. We have offices located in San Francisco, New York, and Pittsburgh.


THE ROLE




Abridge is looking for a People Operations Generalist to join our People team and keep our core People Ops work running smoothly: onboarding, benefits, workers’ comp, compliance, and HR support tickets. You’ll work closely with the Head of People Operations and the rest of the People team to keep things running smoothly and build processes that keep up as we scale.

This role suits someone who is proactive, moves fast, and brings solutions instead of questions. They’re resilient when priorities shift, comfortable with ambiguity, and have a bias for action. They enjoy owning the details, switching between tasks easily, and want to help scale People Ops at a fast-growing startup.




WHAT YOU’LL DO



HR Support & Systems

 - Triage and respond to employee questions in our HR ticketing system quickly and accurately, and escalate when needed.

 - Use Rippling day to day to manage employee data and pull reports. Spot data issues and fix them before they cause problems.

 - Find recurring ticket themes and turn them into self-serve resources or process fixes.

Onboarding & Employee Lifecycle

 - Own new hire onboarding from offer to first day, including paperwork, Rippling setup, and coordination with IT on devices and access.

 - Make sure every new hire has a smooth, well-organized experience, and keep improving the experience as hiring accelerates.

Benefits & Workers’ Comp

 - Administer employee benefits, including enrollments, qualifying life events, open enrollment, and renewals, and be the first point of contact for employee benefits questions.

 - Manage workers’ compensation claims from start to finish.

Compliance

 - Manage compliance programs, including audits, harassment prevention training, and other regulatory mandates.

 - Lead compliance reporting requirements such as EEO-1 and state-specific filings, making sure submissions are on time and accurate.

 - Maintain internal documentation (policies, calendars, audit trails) and build scalable processes that can flex with our team’s growth.

 - Support audits and respond to regulatory inquiries with thorough, organized documentation and clear processes.

Cross-Functional Partnership

 - Work with Payroll, Legal, Finance, and IT to give employees a seamless experience.

 - Jump in wherever there’s an operational gap, and help bring clarity and structure as we grow.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - 3–5 years of experience in People Operations, HR Generalist, or HR Coordinator roles.

 - Hands-on experience with an HRIS. Rippling is strongly preferred.

 - Experience administering benefits and managing workers’ comp claims.

 - Working knowledge of federal and multi-state compliance requirements, including reporting such as EEO-1 and required training mandates.

 - The ability to prioritize on your own in a fast-paced environment where priorities shift.

 - A proactive, solutions-first mindset. You notice gaps and fix them without waiting to be asked.

 - High attention to detail and strong organizational skills.

 - Excellent written and verbal communication. You can explain HR and compliance topics in a way employees understand.




This role is a hybrid position (Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays) based in San Francisco. 


WHY WORK AT ABRIDGE?

At Abridge, we’re transforming healthcare delivery experiences with generative AI, enabling clinicians and patients to connect in deeper, more meaningful ways. Our mission is clear: to power deeper understanding in healthcare. We’re driving real, lasting change, with millions of medical conversations processed each month.

Joining Abridge means stepping into a fast-paced, high-growth startup where your contributions truly make a difference. Our culture requires extreme ownership—every employee has the ability to (and is expected to) make an impact on our customers and our business.

Beyond individual impact, you will have the opportunity to work alongside a team of curious, high-achieving people in a supportive environment where success is shared, growth is constant, and feedback fuels progress. At Abridge, it’s not just what we do—it’s how we do it. Every decision is rooted in empathy, always prioritizing the needs of clinicians and patients.

We’re committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally. Whether it's flexible work hours, an inclusive culture, or ongoing learning opportunities, we are here to help you thrive and do the best work of your life.

If you are ready to make a meaningful impact alongside passionate people who care deeply about what they do, Abridge is the place for you.



HOW WE TAKE CARE OF ABRIDGERS:

 - Comprehensive Health Plans: Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage for all full-time employees and their families.

 - ... and much more!


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER

STAYING SAFE - PROTECT YOURSELF FROM RECRUITMENT FRAUD

jobs.description:
AI Engineering and Delivery is the customer-obsessed engineering group building the agentic AI and enterprise-scale search systems that power Now Assist, AI Agents, and the AI-driven experiences our customers rely on every day. We build AI as foundational platform infrastructure — prioritizing robustness, performance, safety, and real-world customer impact at scale.

About the Team

AI Engineering and Delivery is the customer-obsessed engineering group building the agentic AI and enterprise-scale search systems that power Now Assist, AI Agents, and the AI-driven experiences our customers rely on every day. We build AI as foundational platform infrastructure — prioritizing robustness, performance, safety, and real-world customer impact at scale.

Types of problems you’ll get to work on

You will design, build, and operate production-grade agentic AI systems embedded across ServiceNow's platform — autonomous agents that reason over real enterprise data, take action across workflows, and run safely at Fortune 500 scale.

Your core focus areas:

• Agentic architecture. Design and ship multi-agent systems — orchestration, tool use, planning loops, memory, and failure recovery — that operate reliably in production, not in notebooks.
• Enterprise-grounded reasoning. Build agents that leverage ServiceNow's data layer — CMDB, Workflow Data Fabric, and Knowledge Graph — to make decisions with context no frontier model has on its own.
• Trust, safety, and governance. Own the guardrails: observability, human-in-the-loop controls, and compliance infrastructure that make autonomous systems safe to deploy at scale.
• Retrieval and grounding. Work closely with our search team to ensure agents are grounded in accurate, low-latency retrieval — RAG pipelines, hybrid search, re-ranking, and evaluation — as a critical dependency of agentic quality.
• Model integration and evaluation. Integrate frontier models (Anthropic, Google, OpenAI) into the Sense → Decide → Act → Govern architecture; evaluate trade-offs across cost, latency, and capability for production use cases.
• Engineering leadership. Raise the technical bar through architecture decisions, code reviews, and coaching — particularly on agentic design patterns and production AI discipline.

To be successful in this role you have:

• To be successful in this role you have:
• 5+ years of software engineering with strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and distributed systems.
• Hands-on depth designing, shipping, and operating agentic systems in production — multi-agent orchestration, tool calling, planning loops, memory, and failure recovery. Not prototypes.
• Production-grade Python. Systems language (Go, Java, or C++) is a plus.
• Working experience with frontier AI SDKs (Anthropic, Google, or OpenAI) — prompt engineering, structured outputs, and model evaluation in production settings.

Why join us

With 100B+ workflows, 6.5T transactions a year, and 85% of the Fortune 500 on our platform, we are building the system that makes AI actually work inside the enterprise — Sense, Decide, Act, Govern. What's shipping as we speak: AI Specialists autonomously resolving cases across IT, CRM, HR, and Security. You'd work across three problem spaces at the frontier of what we do: Autonomous Enterprise: Self-driving business processes grounded in CMDB, Workflow Data Fabric, and Knowledge Graph — context no frontier lab can replicate, Omni-channel AI Resolution: Production voice, chat, and computer-use agents with generative UI, live with customers today, Super Intelligence Control Tower: Identity, entitlements, and audit-grade compliance for every agentic system in the enterprise — nobody else has this layer. You will build the substrate that connects all four: SENSE (any data) → DECIDE (any AI model) → ACT (any workflow) → GOVERN (identity + governance). The architectural inflection point is now.

jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff - Evaluations
jobs.description:
Role: Member of Technical Staff - Evaluations

Team: Post-Training

Location: San Francisco

Location Type: Hybrid

Employment Type: Full-time






ABOUT LIQUID AI

Spun out of MIT CSAIL, we build general-purpose AI systems that run efficiently across deployment targets, from data center accelerators to on-device hardware, ensuring low latency, minimal memory usage, privacy, and reliability. We partner with enterprises across consumer electronics, automotive, life sciences, and financial services. We are scaling rapidly and need exceptional people to help us get there.






THE OPPORTUNITY

Public benchmarks saturate and don't generalize to real-world tasks, so post-training risks overfitting to external scores. Every post-training decision at Liquid AI needs internal evals we trust: evals that track real-world behavior and are cheap and reproducible to run. This role sits in the Post-Training team and exists to make sure those decisions rest on exactly that kind of evidence.

You will work on the internal eval suite and infrastructure end to end working closely with the post-training researchers whose decisions depend on it and with other teams (audio and beyond) who need evals for their own models. Evaluating small edge models is an open problem, since nearly every public eval targets frontier models, and the evals you build here change the quality and capabilities of models we ship within weeks, not half a year.






WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We need someone who:

 - Proactive execution: You pick up use cases and come back with working benchmarks. You parallelize work, make progress visible, and finish without being chased.

 - White-box about evals: You volunteer where your own evals or scores were wrong and what you changed, and you present numbers with their caveats attached.






THE WORK

 - Work on the internal eval suite and infrastructure: keep it reliable, optimized, and reproducible at scale.

 - Design held-out evals for priority capabilities such as agentic workflows, computer use, and cybersecurity, with documented construction and contamination checks.

 - Build evals targeted at small edge models, where most public evaluations built for frontier models don't apply.

 - Read generated outputs to debug unexpected scores before anyone acts on them.

 - Turn customer and open-source feedback into environments usable for data, training, and evaluation, and partner with other teams to design evals for their specific needs.

 - Release open-source evals, write papers about them, and publish failure-mode reviews of popular evaluations.






EXPERIENCE & CAPABILITIES

What you'll need:

 - Eval design is where we need you to be unusually strong: you can take a high-level description of a capability and turn it into an evaluation that is accurate, general-purpose, separates good models from bad ones, and is hard to game.

 - Evals you have built before that we can recognize or check, and that hold up on coverage, reproducibility, contamination handling, and the signal they were meant to give. At least one built from scratch: a benchmark, an eval paper, or real contributions to lm-eval-harness, lighteval, OLMES, HELM, or Inspect.

 - Fluency with the fundamentals: contamination, saturation, judge bias, and variance.

 - Hands-on experience running and managing evals in a team, whether on an eval team, a training team, or in an engineering/DevOps role.

 - The habit of debugging unexpected scores by reading individual generated answers before believing the number.

 - Software engineering strong enough to own eval infrastructure and debug the inference and infra failures that surface when running evals at scale, without hand-holding.





Helpful, not required:

 - Model training experience.

 - Publications or research background (industry backgrounds are equally welcome).

 - Deep systems expertise.

 - Familiarity with what small edge models do and don't do well.

 - An eval-specific title is not needed: training-team or DevOps profiles who ran a lot of evals are a good fit.






WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (YEAR ONE)

 - Internal evals cover every main target capability and drive post-training decisions, so that model decisions in post-training cite an internal eval you built or hardened rather than an external benchmark.

 - The eval suite runs reliably at scale and is co-owned, with other teams coming to you for evals for their own models.

 - At least one open-source eval released with a paper, plus a failure-mode report on a popular evaluation, with Liquid's edge-model evals becoming an external reference.






WHAT WE OFFER

 - Evals are the job: You work on the whole eval function alongside one engineer, not one benchmark inside a large eval org, with real compute to run evals at scale and a hiring manager with a large public following who wants to open-source and publish the work.

 - Compensation & Equity: Competitive base salary plus equity, so you share in what we build. Final offers reflect skills, experience, and location.

 - Time Off: Unlimited PTO, plus company-wide Refill Days, long weekends when the whole company rests together.

 - Health & Wellbeing: Comprehensive health coverage, with details varying by location.

 - Paid Leave: Paid leave for pregnancy, parenting, medical needs, and caring for family.

jobs.title: Thought Leader Liaison, Southeast Region
jobs.description:
Amylyx has an audacious mission to usher in a new era for treating diseases with high unmet needs. Where others see challenges, we see opportunities that we pursue with urgency, rigorous science, and unwavering commitment to the communities we serve. We are a clinical-stage company currently focused on post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH), Wolfram syndrome, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

Our mission is powered by our people. Our core values – be audacious, be curious, be authentic, be engaged, and be accountable – creating a culture of caring. Amylyx has assembled an experienced team ready to take action because the communities we serve have no time to wait. If you share our passion and are determined to tackle some of medicine’s toughest problems, we encourage you to read the opportunity below and apply.

The Opportunity

As a member of the marketing team, the Thought Leader Liaison, Southeast Region is a field-based individual contributor responsible for advancing Amylyx’s commercial objectives through strategic and compliant stakeholder engagement and insight generation across the assigned geography. The TLL cultivates professional relationships with key external stakeholders, delivers actionable market insights, and executes stakeholder engagement strategies that support brand performance, launch readiness, and organizational priorities. Working collaboratively across Marketing, Sales, Market Access, Medical Affairs, and Compliance, this role serves as a critical connector between external stakeholders and internal strategy, ensuring external stakeholder insights inform key business decisions. The TLL plays a critical role in elevating the voice of the healthcare community within Amylyx, helping ensure commercial strategies, educational initiatives, and engagement plans reflect evolving market needs and opportunities. This position reports to the Senior Director, Thought Leader Liaison Lead and serves as an extension of the U.S. Marketing team.

This opportunity is based in the Southeast and incumbents for this role should reside within the region: Florida, Georgia or North Carolina

Amylyx may consider highly qualified candidates with more extensive and directly relevant experience for a Senior Thought Leader Liaison position.  The appropriate level will be determined based on the selected candidate’s qualifications, experience and demonstrated capabilities.

Responsibilities

• Develop and maintain professional relationships with key stakeholders (e.g., key opinion leaders) to advance commercial objectives.

• Identify and assess potential advisors, speakers, and thought leaders based on expertise, clinical experience, scientific contributions, and organizational needs.

• Execute thought leader engagement strategies aligned with national brand objectives, supporting identification, prioritization, and engagement planning.

• Support the planning and execution of advisory boards, speaker programs, congress activities, and other high-impact stakeholder initiatives to meet established business needs.

• Deliver regional marketing initiatives that strengthen brand strategy and address evolving educational and local market needs.

• Generate, synthesize, and communicate actionable stakeholder insights to inform commercial strategy, launch readiness, and organizational decision-making.

• Serve as a strategic cross-functional partner to Marketing, Market Access, Sales Leadership, Medical Affairs, and Compliance, ensuring coordinated, compliant, and impactful stakeholder engagement.

• Conduct all activities in accordance with applicable legal, regulatory, and company policies and procedures.

Required Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree required

• 8+ years of progressive experience in biotechnology or pharmaceutical commercial roles, including significant experience in thought leader engagement, sales, or marketing. Amylyx may consider highly qualified candidates with more extensive and directly relevant experience for a Senior Thought Leader Liaison position. The appropriate level will be determined based on the selected candidate’s qualifications, experience and demonstrated capabilities.

• Demonstrated success developing strategic thought leader partnerships and influencing stakeholder engagement within rare disease, endocrinology, or metabolic disease, preferably in launch or pre-launch environments.

• Proven ability to influence without authority, collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams, and communicate with clarity and impact across all levels of the organization.

jobs.description:
Are you an experienced Power BI Developer who enjoys transforming complex data into meaningful insights and intuitive reporting solutions? If you bring advanced dashboard development expertise, strong data validation skills, and the ability to design secure, reliable reporting environments while collaborating directly with business stakeholders, we'd love to connect with you!

About the role

The Senior Power BI Developer role is focused on designing, developing, and optimizing enterprise reporting solutions that turn complex data into accurate, accessible, and actionable business intelligence.

As part of FormativGroup's Data & Analytics Practice, you'll support the development of a stable, scalable Power BI Service environment, building advanced dashboards, custom visualizations, and reporting capabilities that support critical business operations and decision-making.

You'll work closely with business users, technical teams, and client leadership to gather requirements, validate data, improve reporting functionality, and establish best practices. This role combines hands-on Power BI development with technical leadership, documentation, training, and knowledge transfer.

What You'll Work On

As a Senior Power BI Developer, you will:

• Design, configure, and maintain a stable, secure, and reliable Power BI Service environment supporting enterprise reporting requirements.

• Develop and enhance interactive Power BI dashboards, reports, and data visualizations for business users and executive stakeholders.

• Build complex custom Power BI visualizations and user interfaces aligned with business and technical specifications.

• Perform comprehensive data validation, reconciliation, and quality assurance across multiple datasets to ensure reporting accuracy and consistency.

• Design and optimize data models, calculations, and reporting logic to support reliable business intelligence solutions.

What You'll Bring

You will likely be successful in this role if you have:

• 5+ years of advanced hands-on Power BI development experience, including enterprise dashboards, reporting solutions, and Power BI Service administration.

• Strong experience designing complex Power BI reports, interactive dashboards, and custom visualizations.

• Advanced knowledge of Power BI data modeling, DAX, Power Query, and reporting performance optimization.

• Experience integrating Power BI with Azure SQL Server and other enterprise data sources.

• Strong experience performing data validation, reconciliation, and quality assurance across multiple datasets.

• Strong technical documentation skills, including development specifications, reporting manuals, and knowledge transfer materials.

• Experience leading Power BI training, mentoring, and collaborative development sessions.

• Ability to communicate effectively with technical teams, business users, and senior leadership.

• Strong presentation and facilitation skills across both formal and informal stakeholder settings.

• Strong analytical thinking, troubleshooting abilities, and attention to detail.

• Experience managing deliverables, tracking milestones, and providing project status updates directly to clients.

How You Work

The ideal candidate will:

• Take ownership of reporting solutions from requirements gathering through development, validation, deployment, and ongoing optimization.

• Approach complex data and reporting challenges with analytical discipline, attention to accuracy, and a commitment to reliable business intelligence.

• Communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, including senior leadership.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer, Electrical Integration
jobs.description:
ABOUT RADIANT

Radiant is an El Segundo, CA-based company building the world's only mass-produced, transportable nuclear microreactors. The U.S. grid is under growing strain, with power demand accelerating, driving higher utility costs, rising carbon emissions, and interconnection backlogs. Radiant has a solution, transportable, on-site power. Our first reactor, Kaleidos, is 1 megawatt: small enough to be factory-built, transported by land, sea, or air, and deployed wherever power is needed. 1 MW can power 1000 homes for five years. Ship it back and we refuel for a 20 year operating life. We made energy a product that can be used for critical infrastructure like military bases, data centers, hospitals, and remote sites, as well as the commercial main street businesses that keep America running.  Founded in 2020, Radiant is under contract to deliver power to the U.S. Army, Navy and Air Force and has signed pre-order agreements with Equinix, with deployments beginning in 2028.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Radiant is seeking a Mechanical Engineer to support the design and integration of electrical components and subsystems in a fast-paced startup environment. You’ll work alongside experienced mechanical and electrical engineers to solve challenging problems in packaging, thermal management, structural design, and system integration for advanced hardware. This role offers hands-on exposure to end-to-end hardware development from CAD and analysis through build, test, and validation.

 


RESPONSIBILITIES & DUTIES:

 - Support the mechanical design and ownership of electrical components and subsystems, including:

 - Mechanical design of electrical assemblies such as control panels, enclosures, brackets, mounts, and supports.

 - Cable and wiring harness routing, retention, strain relief, bend radius compliance, and serviceability considerations.

 - Packaging of sensors, actuators, connectors, and electrical hardware within constrained assemblies.

 - 3D CAD modeling and 2D drawing creation using Siemens NX, including tolerance stack-ups and GD&T basics.

 - Perform first-order load calculations (static, shock, vibration) to support structural design decisions.

 - Conduct thermal analysis and heat-transfer assessments for electrical components, enclosures, and assemblies.

 - Support selection of materials, fasteners, and finishes appropriate for electrical, thermal, and environmental requirements.

 - Participate in system integration, troubleshooting, and validation activities alongside electrical and systems engineers.

 - Collect and interpret technical requirements and provide clear, constructive feedback across mechanical, electrical, software, and systems disciplines.

 - Perform trade studies and first-order analyses to evaluate design options and constraints.

 - Generate and maintain design documentation to support Design for Manufacturing (DFM), assembly, and serviceability.

 - Support subassembly design, coordinate with manufacturing, and assist with build and test schedules.

 


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS:

 - Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a closely related field from an accredited institution.

 - 3+ Years of professional hands-on mechanical design experience.

 - Experience using Siemens NX or similar 3D CAD tools.

 - Familiarity with mechanical design of electrical assemblies, including enclosures, brackets, and harness routing principles.

 - Basic understanding of structural mechanics, load paths, and first-order stress calculations.

 - Knowledge of thermal analysis, heat transfer, and thermal management concepts.

 - Ability to read and create mechanical drawings, including dimensions and tolerances.

 - Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate in a multidisciplinary engineering environment




DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS & SKILLS:

 - 5+ years of professional hands-on mechanical design experience.

 - Mechanical design for high-reliability or harsh environments (nuclear, aerospace, defense, or industrial), including thermal cycling, shock, vibration, or radiation exposure.

 - Experience with FEA or CFD tools for structural and thermal analysis beyond first-order hand calculations.

 - Hands-on experience supporting build, integration, and test on the floor, including design iteration based on manufacturing feedback.

 


ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

 - Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as necessary to accomplish our mission.

 - Must work 100% onsite at El Segundo HQ.




BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Stock: Substantial incentive stock plan for all full-time employees.

 - Medical: 100% up to base silver level plan for employee + 50% dependents, offers up to Platinum plans.

 - One Medical: Sponsored memberships for employees and their dependents.

 - Vision: 100% top tier plan coverage + 50% for dependents.

 - Dental: 100% top tier plan coverage, orthodontia extra, 50% for dependents.

 - Voluntary life, accident, hospital, critical illness, commuter and FSA/HSA are offered as employee contributed benefits.

 - 8-weeks of paid parental leave for all parents. Additional paid pregnancy leave for CA employees.

 - Nuclear Engineering Certificate Program: 100% covered educational program with Penn State University, for eligible employees, to rapidly upscale into nuclear.

 - Daily catered lunch. Free snacks and drinks.

 - Flexible PTO policy. Remote workday allocation.

 - Company and team-bonding events, happy hours and in-person camaraderie.

 - Beautiful El Segundo headquarters close to the Pacific Ocean.



Total Compensation and Benefits
Radiant compensates people for impact and invests in those who continue to raise the bar. Radiant’s full-time new hire compensation package includes base salary, substantial equity grants, and comprehensive health benefits. Total compensation and level are determined through a rigorous evaluation of interview performance, experience, education, and qualifications, and are designed to support continued growth as scope, responsibility, and impact expand at Radiant.

The best of today’s advanced reactor builders don’t wait for job postings. They join the winning team. If that’s you, contact us directly for immediate opportunities: recruiting@radiantnuclear.com.

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

This position involves access to technology that is subject to U.S. export controls. Any job offer made will be contingent upon the applicant’s capacity to serve in compliance with U.S. export controls.

jobs.title: Technical Support Specialist - Tier II
jobs.description:
The Position

CallRail is looking for a Technical Support Specialist (Tier II) to join our team. Tier II specialists act as our senior technical detectives—taking point on complex integrations, data attribution discrepancies, and advanced product workflows. You will bridge the gap between front-line support and core engineering, taking ownership of tricky technical issues to resolution while helping uplift our Tier I team.

What You'll Do

• Technical Escalations: Own end-to-end investigation for escalated tickets involving telephony (call routing), web script behavior (DNI), webhooks, API requests, and third-party integrations (e.g., Google Ads, GA4, Salesforce, HubSpot).

• Root-Cause Investigation: Use browser developer tools, server logs, API testing tools (like Postman), and database queries to isolate whether an issue stems from CallRail, a client's site code, or a third-party endpoint.

• High-Quality Handoffs: When identifying problem tickets or escalating issues to internal partners, thoroughly document identified failure points, reproducible test steps, payload logs, and diagnostic findings to ensure proper prioritization and solutioning for customers.

• Knowledge Sharing: Turn freshly solved complex cases into actionable notes to reduce repeat escalations.

• Technical Consultation: Assist customers via all channels and scheduled screen-share calls to guide them through complex setups or tricky technical troubleshooting.

• Stakeholder Communication: Provide calm, objective, and timely technical updates during high-priority incidents to leadership, Account Managers, and Sales, managing expectations with clarity and tact.

What You'll Need

jobs.title: Thought Leader Liaison, Central Region
jobs.description:
Amylyx has an audacious mission to usher in a new era for treating diseases with high unmet needs. Where others see challenges, we see opportunities that we pursue with urgency, rigorous science, and unwavering commitment to the communities we serve. We are a clinical-stage company currently focused on post-bariatric hypoglycemia (PBH), Wolfram syndrome, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

Our mission is powered by our people. Our core values – be audacious, be curious, be authentic, be engaged, and be accountable – creating a culture of caring. Amylyx has assembled an experienced team ready to take action because the communities we serve have no time to wait. If you share our passion and are determined to tackle some of medicine’s toughest problems, we encourage you to read the opportunity below and apply.

The Opportunity

As a member of the marketing team, the Thought Leader Liaison, Central Region is a field-based individual contributor responsible for advancing Amylyx’s commercial objectives through strategic and compliant stakeholder engagement and insight generation across the assigned geography. The TLL cultivates professional relationships with key external stakeholders, delivers actionable market insights, and executes stakeholder engagement strategies that support brand performance, launch readiness, and organizational priorities. Working collaboratively across Marketing, Sales, Market Access, Medical Affairs, and Compliance, this role serves as a critical connector between external stakeholders and internal strategy, ensuring external stakeholder insights inform key business decisions. The TLL plays a critical role in elevating the voice of the healthcare community within Amylyx, helping ensure commercial strategies, educational initiatives, and engagement plans reflect evolving market needs and opportunities. This position reports to the Senior Director, Thought Leader Liaison Lead and serves as an extension of the U.S. Marketing team.

This opportunity is based in the Central region and incumbents for this role should reside within the region. Colorado, Illinois, Michigan, Minnesota or Missouri

• Execute thought leader engagement strategies aligned with national brand objectives, supporting identification, prioritization, and engagement planning.

• Support the planning and execution of advisory boards, speaker programs, congress activities, and other high-impact stakeholder initiatives to meet established business needs.

• Deliver regional marketing initiatives that strengthen brand strategy and address evolving educational and local market needs.

• Serve as a strategic cross-functional partner to Marketing, Market Access, Sales Leadership, Medical Affairs, and Compliance, ensuring coordinated, compliant, and impactful stakeholder engagement.

jobs.title: Maintenance Technician
jobs.description:
ABOUT MARIANA MINERALS

Mariana Minerals is a software-first, vertically integrated minerals company on a mission to supply the critical minerals powering modern energy, AI, and defense technologies. We’re reimagining the minerals supply chain by combining deep industry expertise with advanced software, automation, and data-driven decision-making.

The Maintenance Technician, Mechanical  supports safe, reliable operation of our process and utility equipment at Lithium One in Joaquin, TX. In this role, you will perform preventive and corrective maintenance on pumps, motors, valves, conveyors, blowers, compressors, and other rotating equipment, then respond to unplanned breakdowns and trace problems to the root cause. You will play a critical role in keeping production steady and downtime low, and you will have a real hand in building our maintenance program from the ground up, including finding ways to simplify or automate repetitive maintenance tasks. As a startup, the first 6-8 months will include work beyond your mechanical specialty, such as electrical and instrumentation support, so the ideal fit is someone who loves variety and wants to build something.

Responsibilities

 - Perform preventive, predictive, and corrective maintenance on pumps, motors, valves, conveyors, blowers, compressors, and other rotating and process equipment

 - Troubleshoot and diagnose planned and unplanned equipment issues across the Lithium One plant, finding the root cause and making timely repairs

 - Keep production steady by minimizing downtime and completing work to manufacturer specifications and quality standards

 - Perform and document accurate inspections, calibration, and lubrication on process and utility equipment, and recommend equipment for inclusion in preventive maintenance programs

 - Read P&IDs, schematics, and blueprints, requisition parts and materials, and log work, parts used, and equipment condition in our in-house CMMS

 - Work with operations, engineering, and the electrical and controls techs to support start-up, shutdown, and change-out activities, and communicate potential hazards to engineers, electricians, and operators

 - Follow all OSHA and company safety procedures (including lockout/tagout, confined space, and traffic rules), actively participate in safety meetings, and immediately report hazards, near misses, or equipment damage while ensuring operations meet environmental and regulatory standards

Qualifications & Experience

 - Technical or trade school training in industrial maintenance or mechanical technology preferred (or equivalent experience)

 - Proven industrial maintenance experience, 3+ years

 - Hands-on experience with piping and with pump, motor, and valve rebuild and repair on rotating and process equipment

 - Experience in an oil & gas, water treatment, chemical processing, or similar industrial setting (oil & gas highly preferred; hydrometallurgy, mining, or battery materials experience is a plus)

 - Working knowledge of electrical and basic instrumentation systems, including motor starters and control circuits

 - Ability to read P&IDs, schematics, blueprints, and equipment manuals

 - Strong mechanical aptitude, with comfort using hand tools, power tools, precision measuring instruments, and basic rigging

 - Strong communication across shifts and good computer skills; CMMS experience preferred

 - Valid driver's license

Schedule
12-hour shifts (6am-6pm): Sunday-Tuesday plus every other Wednesday, or Thursday-Saturday plus every other Wednesday. A night rotation will be added in the near future.

Working Environment & Physical Requirements

 - Work in the processing plant and shop, in all weather conditions including extreme temperatures, with exposure to chemicals and other hazardous materials

 - Ability to lift a minimum of 50 pounds and to stand, walk, and work in confined or elevated spaces for extended periods

 - Ability to climb ladders and structures, with the manual dexterity to use hand and power tools

 - Must wear and use all required PPE


OUR CULTURE IS BUILT ON FOUR PRINCIPLES:



Everyone Gets Home Safe. We never put speed or cost ahead of people.

Extreme Ownership. We take full responsibility for outcomes, relentlessly driving toward solutions.

Engineer Out Requirements, then Automate. We simplify, optimize, and then automate for scale.

Share Your Legos. We collaborate openly, share knowledge, and empower each other to build bigger, better solutions.



Join us as we build the future of responsible mineral sourcing and supply!

Practice nursing with the autonomy, time, and patient connection that allows you to make a meaningful impact every day. jobs.title: Senior User Researcher
jobs.description:
About Formlabs:

A 3D printer is one of the most demanding machines you can build.

Lasers, optics, precision motion, thermals, airflow, materials handling, chemistry, sensing, controls, and software all have to work at micron-scale precision, for thousands of layers, with almost no tolerance for error. Making that work reliably is an extraordinary engineering problem.

That’s what we do.

At Formlabs, we’re building 3D printers that are changing the way things get made. We have the smartest minds across every engineering discipline, and the technology they’re building is deployed at more than 50,000 industry leaders worldwide, including Apple, Google, Tesla, New Balance, and NASA.

Your Impact:

We’re looking for a Senior Product Researcher to own how Formlabs understands its customers and markets. You’ll set the research agenda that shapes our roadmap, combining customer insight, competitive intelligence, and sales data into a clear point of view on where we should invest. Working directly with product leadership, R&D, and sales and marketing, you’ll lead the strategic studies behind our biggest product bets, build the systems that keep the company close to its customers, and turn evidence into decisions that leadership acts on.

If you’re energized by the idea of making the impossible happen, come join us as a Senior Product Researcher.

The Job:

• Own the product research roadmap. Partner with product and R&D leadership to identify the highest-stakes open questions, then design and run the studies that answer them

• Assist product managers in sizing markets, building business plans, and developing product strategy.

• Identify new areas of opportunity for Formlabs that are adjacent to what we are doing today. Propose product concepts that capture these new opportunities.

• Own the recurring insight programs, including NPS and CSAT, quarterly customer insights, feedback triage, and win/loss analysis.

• Lead alpha and beta programs for major launches. Recruit and manage customer cohorts and synthesize feedback into clear fix-before-launch recommendations.

• Track post-launch performance and market reception. Work with distributors and end customers to find out what’s working and what isn’t.

• Raise the research bar across the team. Mentor other researchers and PMs on research methods.

You:

• 7+ years of experience in product research, user research, market research, or product strategy, with a track record of research that changed what a company built.

• Fluency in both qualitative methods (interviews, field visits, contextual inquiry) and quantitative methods (survey design, segmentation, data analysis).

• Strong analytical skills, including Google Sheets or Excel. Experience with business systems for insights and reporting, such as Salesforce and Data Studio.

• Able to turn complex, ambiguous evidence into a clear recommendation and defend it.

• Comfortable owning research programs end to end and influencing teams you don’t manage.

Bonus skills

• Experience leading research for hardware or physical products, ideally in industrial, consumer, or medical markets.

• Background in high-growth B2B tech or hardware environments.

• Familiarity with manufacturing or 3D printing.

Our Benefits & Perks:

• Unlimited 3D printing with any Formlabs material on any Formlabs printer

• An equity program that will let you build wealth through RSUs

• Healthcare coverage (medical, dental, vision) that includes a totally free employee-only plan, effective starting on your first day on the job

• 401K matching with no vesting or tenure requirement

• Generous parental leave (fully paid up to 16 weeks)

• Flexible time off so you can take time when you need it

• Six-week fully paid sabbatical after hitting tenure milestones (with the option to take an additional six weeks after that)

• Free on-site parking & pre-tax commuter benefits

• Free on-site lunch, snacks, beverages, treats, beer kegs, and employee-favorite local coffee and espresso

• Self-driven professional development opportunities like conferences, trade shows, and hackathons

• One-of-a-kind activities and events like monthly socials, the annual weekend summer camp, a can’t-miss company hackathon, and lots of other social opportunities

You don’t need to check every box to apply for a role. If you love working with hardware, spending time with smart people, solving hard problems, and winning, we want to hear from you.

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company.  We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

Our Candidate AI Guidelines are available here. Please give them a read.

Compensation:

Equity is a big part of the compensation package at Formlabs - every employee receives equity because everyone contributes to building the company. We have a lot of confidence in the products we’re building and the impact we’re making, and you should too.

Base pay is the other part of our compensation package, and it is carefully determined based on your skills, experience, and expected impact. Equity and base pay combine to make up your total compensation package at Formlabs.

The annual base pay range for this role is:

$125,000—$155,000 USD

jobs.title: Program Cost Manager
jobs.description:
AST SpaceMobile and our global partners are building the first and only space-based cellular broadband network to be accessible by standard smartphones. Called SpaceMobile, this ultra-powerful network is being designed to provide connectivity at 4G/5G speeds everywhere on the planet – on land, at sea and in flight.

Position Overview

We are seeking a Program Cost Manager to build, implement, and manage the cost framework for a high-priority aerospace development program. This role is responsible for developing program budgets, forecasting costs, tracking financial performance, managing cost risks, and providing leadership with clear visibility into program expenditures, commitments, and financial outcomes.

The ideal candidate combines strong program cost management experience with a hands-on understanding of engineering, supply chain, and financial planning processes. This individual will partner closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Accounting, and FP&A teams while leveraging AI-enabled tools and automation to improve forecasting accuracy, reporting efficiency, and decision-making.

Key Responsibilities

• Develop and maintain the program cost framework, including materials, operating expenses, labor costs, and long-range financial planning

• Partner with Engineering teams to develop, maintain, and monitor bill of materials (BOM) budgets and cost projections

• Forecast supplier, engineering services, testing, manufacturing, and deployment costs throughout the program lifecycle

• Monitor actual spending against budgets, forecasts, commitments, and contracts while identifying variances and corrective actions

• Provide program leaders and executives with proactive visibility into cost risks, opportunities, and financial performance

• Perform cost trade studies and financial analysis to support key business decisions, including sourcing, procurement, and deployment strategies

• Design and maintain cost structures, work breakdown structures (WBS), cost codes, reporting hierarchies, and financial controls

• Prepare monthly cost reports, executive dashboards, forecasts, estimate-at-completion (EAC) updates, and leadership presentations

• Lead AI-driven initiatives that improve forecasting, variance analysis, spend management, contract review, and financial reporting processes

• Coordinate with FP&A and Accounting teams to support forecasting, accruals, capitalization, budgeting, and financial reporting requirements

• Establish and maintain program financial controls, approval processes, purchase order tracking, and contract change management activities

• Support strategic planning, funding requests, business cases, and executive decision-making processes

Qualifications

Education:

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field

• Master's degree in Finance, Business Administration, Engineering Management, or a related discipline preferred

Experience:

• Minimum 7 years of experience in program cost management, cost engineering, project controls, financial planning and analysis (FP&A), or related financial management roles

• Minimum 3 years supporting hardware development, manufacturing, engineering, aerospace, defense, or large-scale technical programs

• Experience building and maintaining program budgets, forecasts, and financial reporting structures

• Experience managing supplier costs, contracts, purchase orders, and program financial controls

• Demonstrated experience utilizing AI tools, automation platforms, or advanced analytics solutions within finance or operational environments

Preferred Qualifications:

• Aerospace, defense, satellite communications, manufacturing, or other complex engineering industry experience

• Experience building a cost framework for a new program, product line, or business unit

• Experience implementing AI-driven forecasting, contract analysis, spend analytics, or reporting automation solutions

• Experience supporting bill of materials (BOM) costing and should-cost analysis activities

• Familiarity with supplier contracts, engineering services agreements, milestone billing structures, and change order management

• Experience supporting capital-intensive programs and understanding capital expenditure (CapEx) versus operational expenditure (OpEx) planning

• Experience working in high-growth, fast-paced organizations with evolving processes and operational structures

Soft Skills:

• Strong ownership mindset and ability to build processes from the ground up

• Excellent analytical and financial problem-solving skills

• Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to collaborate across engineering, supply chain, finance, and executive leadership teams

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills

• Ability to translate complex financial information into clear, actionable recommendations

• Strong attention to detail and commitment to financial accuracy

• Ability to identify risks early and proactively recommend solutions

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines

• Continuous improvement mindset with enthusiasm for automation and emerging technologies

Technology Stack:

• Oracle NetSuite or comparable ERP systems

• Microsoft Excel (advanced modeling, forecasting, pivot tables, and scenario analysis)

• Microsoft PowerPoint

• Power BI or similar business intelligence platforms

• AI assistants and generative AI tools

• Microsoft Copilot

• ChatGPT

• Claude

• Python

• Power Automate

• Microsoft Teams

• SharePoint

• Outlook

• Product lifecycle management (PLM) and BOM management systems

• Microsoft Project, Primavera, or comparable project controls tools

Physical Requirements

• Ability to work in a standard office environment and use a computer for extended periods

• Ability to review financial reports, contracts, engineering documentation, and cost models

• Ability to participate in cross-functional meetings, business reviews, and executive presentations

• Occasional travel of approximately 10–20% to manufacturing, testing, supplier, and partner locations

• Ability to walk manufacturing floors, testing facilities, and operational sites while following required safety protocols

Benefits & Perks

At AST, we value our employees and offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, and work-life balance.

• Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance

• 401(k) Retirement Plan with Company Match

• Company-Paid Short-Term Disability (STD) and Long-Term Disability (LTD) Insurance

jobs.title: Contracts Manager
jobs.description:
HADRIAN - MANUFACTURING THE FUTURE

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.


Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.


Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.


If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.




THE ROLE:

The Contracts Manager owns the formation, negotiation, and administration of Hadrian’s agreements on both sides of the business: the agreements through which Hadrian sells to its customers, and the agreements through which it buys from its supply base. Hadrian’s contracting function is scaling alongside its factories. This seat will help design the workflows, systems, and controls that move agreements from intake to signature across sales and procurement, and is measured on the cycle time it removes.

 - Hadrian supplies precision components to the defense and aerospace primes and to commercial space and aviation customers. This seat negotiates and administers those customer agreements, including long-term supply agreements, master agreements, customer purchase orders, and Hadrian’s quote terms. Many arrive carrying FAR, DFARS, export control, and data rights requirements from the prime contract. The seat confirms Hadrian can perform them and flows them correctly 

 - Scaling Hadrian’s manufacturing footprint requires the purchase of machine tools, automation cells, raw material, castings and forgings, outside processing, tooling, and software. This seat owns Hadrian’s purchase order terms and the category addenda supporting them, adjudicates supplier markups, and serves as the contracts partner to Supply Chain and Procurement into its supply base.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own assigned customer and supplier agreements from intake through closeout: pre-award review, negotiation, award, acceptance, performance, modification, renewal, and closeout. Administer Hadrian’s subcontracts under prime contractor terms. Track deliverables, milestones, acceptance, and notice dates against each contract, and escalate noncompliance before it becomes a dispute.

 - Draft, revise, and interpret long-term supply agreements, master agreements, subcontracts, purchase orders, quote terms, non-disclosure agreements, statements of work, amendments, and change orders. Produce clear, defensible language on Hadrian’s paper and precise redlines on the counterparty’s.

 - Digest the FAR, DFARS, and customer-specific clauses the primes flow down to Hadrian through customer agreements and purchase orders. Determine which obligations Hadrian must carry, which must flow to its suppliers, and which do not apply. Apply them to the correct vendor agreements order by order and maintain the record of which clauses attached where. Challenge flowdowns that exceed what the prime contract requires or what a commercial supplier should reasonably accept.

 - Draft and administer Hadrian’s terms for subcontracts, suppliers, and capital equipment, including acceptance, warranty, title and risk of loss, and milestone payment structures. Verify that the correct Hadrian terms and category addenda attach to every order, screen order-face fields for the completeness downstream controls depend on, and confirm order terms do not conflict with the governing master agreement

 - Review customer terms, purchase orders, and long-term agreements from the primes against Hadrian’s established positions, and identify the pricing, liability, intellectual property, and data rights terms that require escalation. Adjudicate markups returned against Hadrian’s purchase order and quote terms under the playbook, and determine acceptance within delegated authority. Prepare the response setting out Hadrian’s position in terms the counterparty can act on.

 - Own the portfolio end to end across customers, suppliers, and prospective partners. Apply the review checklist to every inbound form, issue Hadrian’s standard redline, and distribute Hadrian’s form on request. Determine whether a mutual or unilateral instrument is appropriate and which party is protected. Approve deviations within the playbook, negotiate to closure, and track expirations.

 - Maintain the contract record in accordance with company and regulatory requirements. Define and enforce the contract file standard and naming conventions, own the central repository, and administer records retention. Drive discovery and reconciliation of legacy agreements to completion.

 - Own the contract lifecycle platform and serve as first-line support for its users. Build and maintain workflows, approval routing, templates, and form fields, and map approval chains to the delegation of authority. Direct the implementation partner through user acceptance testing and go-live. Own the enhancement backlog, integrations, permissions, and access reviews, and enforce the export control handling gate before any upload.


WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 - Bachelor’s degree in business administration, contracts management, supply chain management, finance, law, or a related field.

 - 5+ years in contract management, contract administration, or procurement contracting in aerospace, defense, or advanced manufacturing, including full lifecycle responsibility for customer and supplier agreements personally negotiated and administered.

 - Experience negotiating from the supplier’s side of the table with prime contractors or major OEMs, including long-term supply agreements, customer terms and purchase orders, and the pricing, delivery, and liability commitments behind them

 - Substantial experience administering purchase orders, supplier terms, and subcontracts in a manufacturing, industrial, or hardware environment, including capital equipment or major asset purchases and the acceptance, installation, and milestone payment structures behind them.

 - Working command of the FAR and DFARS clauses primes flow down to their suppliers. The candidate understands how prime-tier subcontracts and purchase orders are formed, administered, and modified, and how the prime’s contract type shapes the terms it flows down.

 - Demonstrated record of negotiating complex agreements to closure across price, terms, schedule, and risk allocation. The candidate has authored language issued under their organization’s name, not solely revised the work of others, across supply agreements, master agreements, basic ordering agreements, subcontracts, purchase orders, non-disclosure agreements, change orders, and license agreements.

 - A demonstrated record of building contracting infrastructure rather than inheriting it. The candidate has built or materially improved a playbook, position set, or clause library, established workflows and an intake process, and achieved measurable reduction in contract cycle time on both the sales and procurement sides.

 - Hands-on ownership of a contract lifecycle management system as an administrator, including workflow configuration, templates, permissions, and reporting, and advanced proficiency in Microsoft Word and Excel.

 - The candidate interprets legal language, assesses risk, and translates contractual requirements into guidance that engineering, program, and operations teams can act upon. The candidate has operated with delegated authority and recognizes when a matter falls outside the playbook.

 - Exceptional written work product. The record created in this seat is subject to customer audit, government review, and litigation, and a redline issued from it constitutes Hadrian’s position until corrected.

 - Exceptional organizational discipline under volume, comfort with ambiguity, and a bias toward decision.


WHAT WILL SET YOU APART

 - Master’s degree, MBA, JD, or graduate degree in business, law, or supply chain management.

 - Professional certification such as NCMA’s Certified Commercial Contracts Manager (CCCM), Certified Professional Contracts Manager (CPCM), or Certified Federal Contracts Manager (CFCM), or an equivalent World Commerce & Contracting credential.

 - Experience on the supplier side of defense, aerospace, or commercial space programs, including Navy, Air Force, Space Force, or Army platforms

 - Experience administering subcontracts under prime contractor terms and conditions at a tier-one or tier-two supplier.

 - Experience in a procurement, sourcing, or supply chain organization, or as the contracts partner embedded in one.

 - Experience running a contract lifecycle implementation or migration, including repository discovery, data cleanup, and cutover.

 - An active security clearance, or eligibility to obtain one.


COMPENSATION

For this role, the target salary range is $140,000 - $165,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.




BENEFITS FOR FULL-TIME EMPLOYEES

 - Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees 
   401k 

 - Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need. 

 - Flexible vacation policy 

 - Equity

 


ITAR REQUIREMENTS

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer
jobs.description:
About the Team

The Context Engine is ServiceNow’s platform for connecting enterprise data, knowledge graphs, and AI workloads into a single, governed context layer. We’re building the data infrastructure that AI agents and applications will depend on as enterprises move from pilots to production.

Types of problems you’ll get to work on

You’ll own the technical architecture of core components across the data lake (Iceberg, Polaris, Trino) and the Context Engine, taking them from early release to real adoption with customers.

Your core focus areas:

• Platform architecture. Lead design and implementation of lakehouse table services and context graph ingestion. Translate product requirements into scalable, observable plans with clear failure-recovery patterns.
• LLMs and ontologies. Design how large language models and enterprise ontologies work together in the Context Engine: ontology-grounded retrieval and reasoning for LLMs, and LLM-assisted ontology construction, mapping, and evolution. Make both production-grade, observable, and governed.
• 1.0 to adoption. Drive the full arc from early release to meaningful adoption. Learn from how customers actually use the platform, not only what they say, and build feedback loops that improve adoption over time.
• AI-native engineering. Set the bar for using AI in engineering itself, from AI-assisted code review and test generation to platform features that treat AI agents as first-class users.
• Engineering leadership. Run deep architecture reviews, raise the technical bar across the team, and represent the platform in technical and leadership forums.
• Cross-functional execution. Work with Product, Design, and partner engineering teams to align dependencies and ship coherent experiences.

To Be Successful in This Role

• 10+ years in software engineering, including shipping complex enterprise-grade data or SaaS products at scale.
• Hands-on experience building products from zero, with ownership of both code and architecture decisions. Not prototypes.
• Deep cloud-native architecture: multi-tenant design, large-scale API design (REST/gRPC), Kubernetes, observability, and multi-cloud platforms.
• Distributed systems and event-driven architecture expertise, with a focus on reliability, fault tolerance, and operational observability.
• Strong data modeling across relational, graph, columnar, and streaming systems, including open table formats such as Iceberg and query engines such as Trino.
• Hands-on experience with data platform technologies: Spark for large-scale data processing, Kafka for event streaming, and Iceberg and Polaris for lakehouse table management and catalog services.
• Production-grade Python, with hands-on experience building services with FastAPI.
• Hands-on experience building LangChain or LangGraph applications, and MCP servers that expose platform capabilities to AI agents.
• Hands-on experience running LLMs in production: prompt and context design, structured outputs, model evaluation, and cost and latency trade-offs.
• Working knowledge of ontologies and semantic modeling (such as OWL, RDF, or SKOS), including how they constrain and ground LLM outputs.
• Proficiency across the full engineering lifecycle, using AI daily to improve delivery velocity and software quality.
• Technical influence without formal authority, with a record of driving architecture decisions across teams through clear reasoning.

Nice to Have

• Knowledge graph or context graph experience, including entity resolution and graph query optimization.
• Experience building ontologies or semantic layers at enterprise scale, including ontology alignment and schema mapping across data sources.
• Experience fine-tuning or evaluating LLMs for entity extraction, classification, or relation extraction.
• Data governance, lineage, or catalog product experience, including auditability and access control.
• Production experience with data pipeline ingestion from SaaS sources.
• Familiarity with OpenAPI and other AI interoperability standards.
• Advanced degree in Computer Science, AI, or a related field.

Why join us

Intelligence is commoditizing. Context and execution are not. You’ll build the context layer that connects the whole stack: SENSE (any data) → DECIDE (any AI model) → ACT (any workflow) → GOVERN (identity + governance). You’ll report to the VP of Engineering, and the architectural inflection point is now.

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $221,200 - $387,100, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.

Work Personas

We approach our distributed world of work with flexibility and trust. Work personas (flexible, remote, or required in office) are categories that are assigned to ServiceNow employees depending on the nature of their work and their assigned work location. Learn more here. To determine eligibility for a work persona, ServiceNow may confirm the distance between your primary residence and the closest ServiceNow office using a third-party service.

Equal Opportunity Employer

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, national origin, age, disability, gender identity,  veteran status, or any other category protected by law. In addition, all qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with legal requirements.
