jobs.title: Data Analytics Engineer
jobs.description:
Veeam is the Data and AI Trust Company, specializing in helping organizations ensure their data and AI are fully understood, secured, and resilient to enable the acceleration of safe AI at scale. As the market leader in both data resilience and data security posture management, Veeam is built for the convergence of identity, data, security, and AI risk. Headquartered in Seattle with offices in more than 30 countries, Veeam protects over 550,000 customers worldwide, who trust Veeam to keep their businesses running. Join us as we go fearlessly forward together, growing, learning, and making a real impact for some of the world’s biggest brands.

About the Role

Reporting directly to the Director, Data Analytics, the Data Analytics Engineer contributes to the technical design, development, and enhancement of Corporate Metrics data products at Veeam, including Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR). The role implements the technical roadmap set by the Director for these data assets to drive data-driven decision making across the organization. The ideal candidate brings strong data architecture and dimensional modeling expertise, clear communication, strategic thinking, and the ability to translate business needs into scalable, reliable, and well-governed data assets.

This role is integral to the transformation of Veeam’s Corporate Metrics, which support both internal and external reporting and analytics. Responsibilities include architecture and technical design, building dimensional data models, understanding business processes, and driving execution to deliver accurate and scalable solutions aligned to a roadmap. The Data Analytics Engineer implements team processes and collaborates with partners and business stakeholders to translate requirements.

What You’ll Do

• Maintain Corporate Metrics Data Assets: Create and maintain the data pipelines, models, and storage solutions behind the Corporate Metrics data mart, including ARR, ensuring completeness, accuracy, and security.

• Corporate Metrics Semantic Layer: Build out a robust semantic layer enabling business users to access corporate metrics through AI Tools in natural language.

• Dimensional Data Modeling: Design and maintain dimensional models (star and snowflake schemas, conformed dimensions, fact tables, slowly changing dimensions) that serve as a consistent, reusable foundation for reporting and analytics across metric domains.

• Data Architecture & Transformation Job Development: Design and implement robust, scalable, and efficient Databricks jobs to support sources of truth for Corporate Metrics reporting and analytics.

• Data Quality & Governance: Collaborate and communicate requirements with the Data Quality and Governance team around data lineage, segmentation and sources of truth for Corporate Metrics data assets.

• Collaboration: Work closely with the Central Data Engineering, Revenue Intelligence, and Corporate Technology teams to align on metric definitions, requirements, and reporting needs.

• Communication: Act as the technical point of contact for Corporate Metrics data assets. Help translate business requirements into technical specs.

• Continuous Improvement: Identify opportunities to improve data processes, automation, and reporting capabilities.

• Release Management: Manage app changes through source control (e.g., GitHub or Azure DevOps), code review, and testing, following change processes that meet SOX and other compliance requirements.

Key Success Factors

• Understanding of Business Strategy and Processes related to Corporate Metrics:

• Grasp the definitions, calculations, and business impact of Corporate Metrics such as ARR and related SaaS, Sales, Finance, and Headcount metrics.

• Align data processes with business requirements and financial reporting standards.

• Technical Excellence:

• Demonstrate strong skills in data architecture, dimensional modeling, pipeline development, and integration.

• Ensure data quality, reliability, and scalability across all Corporate Metrics data systems.

• Take full responsibility for the lifecycle of Corporate Metrics sources of truth in Databricks: design, development, release, support, and troubleshooting.

• Use AI-assisted development responsibly, reviewing and testing generated code before release.

• Ownership & Accountability:

• Maintain the end-to-end lifecycle of Corporate Metrics data assets: design, implementation, maintenance, and troubleshooting.

• Proactively address issues, risks, and gaps in the data.

• Innovation & Continuous Improvement:

• Stay informed about advancements in analytics engineering, data modeling, cloud technologies, and AI-assisted development.

• Seek opportunities to automate, optimize, and enhance data processes.

• Security & Compliance:

• Ensure Corporate Metrics data assets and change processes comply with relevant security standards and regulations (e.g., SOX, GDPR)

What You’ll Bring

• Bachelor’s or master’s degree in Business Analytics, Computer Science, Engineering or a related quantitative field.

• 3+ years of experience in data analytics or analytics engineering, with significant experience on corporate reporting data projects.

• Strong SQL skills (DDL and DML)

• Hands-on experience designing and building dimensional data models (Kimball methodology, star schemas, fact and dimension tables, slowly changing dimensions).

• Proficiency with modern data engineering tools and platforms (e.g., Python, SQL, Databricks).

• Experience building semantic layers or metric stores (e.g., Databricks Metric Views/Genie, dbt Semantic Layer) and exposing data to AI or natural-language tools.

• Familiarity with DevOps processes and tools like Github or Azure DevOps

• Understanding of ARR and other SaaS and corporate metrics.

• Strong analytical skills and experience with AI-driven solutions.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities.

• Experience with external reporting needs for a public company.

Bonus Skills

• Familiarity with Claude Code, ChatGPT, or other AI/ML-driven development tools.

• Experience with Salesforce and Data Warehouse migrations or integrations.

• Knowledge of automated data quality testing frameworks

What You’ll Get

• Mental health support, therapy sessions, and digital wellness tools via SupportLinc EAP

• Professional training and education, including courses and workshops, internal meetups, and unlimited access to our online learning platforms (LinkedIn Learning, Athena, O’Reilly) and mentoring through our MentorLab program Please note: The position is based in San Jose, Costa Rica. If the applicant is permanently located outside of Costa Rica, Veeam reserves the right to decline the application. All applications must be submitted in English.

jobs.description:
Overview

You’re ready to shape the future of image analysis for the defense and intelligence community. You thrive on technical leadership, guiding teams through complex challenges and setting the vision for innovative GIS solutions. You enjoy mentoring others, influencing best practices, and making decisions that impact products across domains. You will design, test, document, and deploy innovative software solutions for the defense and intelligence communities that apply scientific principles in photogrammetry, remote sensing, and AI into innovative geospatial software capabilities.

Responsibilities

• Coordinate and contribute to the implementation of significant subsystems and applications within ArcGIS

• Provide technical leadership and vision, influencing design, use cases, testing, and deployment strategies

• Lead the articulation and realization of innovative designs for new GIS capabilities and user experiences

• Define and refine best practices for test case preparation, automation, and quality assessment

• Deliver advanced technical workshops at industry events and provide onsite support to users in critical situations

• Mentor and guide team members, managing project timelines, scope, and dependencies; may serve as Scrum Master or Product Owner

• Collaborate across teams to ensure high standards of software quality, usability, and performance

• Respond to high-priority technical support issues and develop new methods to address complex workflows

Requirements

• 8+ years of engineering experience working on COTS or GOTS software products, with a track record of technical leadership and innovation

• Recognized expertise in one or more aspects of product engineering, with significant contributions to subsystems, applications, or domains

• Demonstrated ability to lead the design, implementation, and validation of complex GIS software solutions

• Deep understanding of applied test methods, automation, and quality assessment for large-scale software releases

• Experience managing project timelines, scope, and dependencies, and providing technical leadership to project teams

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience leading technical workshops and presenting at industry events

• Able to work with controlled unclassified information (CUI)

• U.S. citizenship with the ability to obtain a U.S. Top Secret clearance with SCI access

• Bachelor’s degree in geography, engineering, remote sensing, photogrammetry, or a related field

Recommended Qualifications

• Master’s or PhD in geography, engineering, remote sensing, photogrammetry, or a related field

• Experience in the defense and/or intelligence communities

• Proficiency in modern development languages (Python, C#, etc.) for validating GIS functionality and developing advanced sample applications

• Hands-on imagery experience across multiple modalities

• Familiarity with the NITF, GeoTIFF, and CADRG formats and specifications

• Experience with ArcGIS Pro, ENVI, Socet GXP, Erdas, or RemoteView

• Experience as a Product Owner, Scrum Master, or System Engineer for major software projects

#LI-DV2

#LI-Onsite

Total Rewards

Esri’s competitive total rewards strategy includes industry-leading health and welfare benefits: medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance for employees (and their families), 401(k) and profit-sharing programs, minimum accrual of 80 hours of vacation leave, twelve paid holidays throughout the calendar year, and opportunities for personal and professional growth. Base salary is one component of our total rewards strategy. Compensation decisions and the base range for this role take into account many factors including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs.

A reasonable estimate of the base salary range is

$120,640—$193,752 USD

The Company

At Esri, diversity is more than just a word on a map. When employees of different experiences, perspectives, backgrounds, and cultures come together, we are more innovative and ultimately a better place to work. We believe in having a diverse workforce that is unified under our mission of creating positive global change. We understand that diversity, equity, and inclusion is not a destination but an ongoing process. We are committed to the continuation of learning, growing, and changing our workplace so every employee can contribute to their life’s best work. Our commitment to these principles extends to the global communities we serve by creating positive change with GIS technology. For more information on Esri’s Racial Equity and Social Justice initiatives, please visit our website here.

jobs.title: Nurse Practitioner (EST)
jobs.description:
Join the dynamic journey at Vynca, where we're passionate about transforming care for individuals with complex needs.

We’re more than just a team; we're a close-knit community. Our shared commitment to caring for each other and those we serve is what sets us apart. Guided by our unwavering core values: Excellence, Compassion, Curiosity, and Integrity, we forge paths of success together. Join us in this transformative movement where you can contribute to making a profound difference every day.

At Vynca, our mission is to provide comprehensive care for more quality days at home.




ABOUT THE JOB

Vynca is seeking a remote Nurse Practitioner to join our growing team! The Nurse Practitioner will serve as a vital member of the Clinical Care Delivery Team and will provide evidence-based, high-quality clinical care to an assigned panel of complex and seriously ill patients via telemedicine, with a focus on assessing patient needs, acting on what we find, and improving outcomes such as avoiding hospitalizations and supporting timely hospice transitions. A passion for this work and a love for patients is a must!



At this time we are only considering applicants in the following states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Nevada, North Carolina, Oregon, Texas, Utah, and Washington, with a strong preference for those based in the Eastern Time Zone.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

Remote care duties performed through HIPAA-compliant hardware and software:

 - Independently performs comprehensive and symptom management visits to address the individualized needs of the patient along with a plan of care oversight (as defined by state-specific law).

 - Assesses each patient’s symptoms, goals, and risks at every visit, acts on the findings with a clear plan of care, and follows up to confirm the patient’s condition and experience have improved.

 - Completes required assessments and documentation (e.g., ESAS, POLST, goals-of-care) in a timely manner and uses the results to adjust the plan of care.

 - Orders and interprets diagnostic and therapeutic tests relative to patient’s age-specific needs

 - Prescribes appropriate pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic treatment modalities

 - Interfaces with patients, families, caregivers, and clinical staff, to ensure a positive patient experience and strong clinical outcomes.

 - Partners with the RN, social worker, and other care team members through daily huddles and interdisciplinary team meetings to proactively identify at-risk patients and coordinate timely follow-up.

 - Works to reduce avoidable hospitalizations through proactive outreach, rapid response to changes in condition, and transition-of-care follow-up after hospital discharge.

 - Facilitates the patient’s transition within and between health care settings, e.g. admitting, transferring, and discharging patients.

 - Identifies patients who may benefit from hospice and leads compassionate, timely goals-of-care and hospice transition conversations.

 - Collaborates with multidisciplinary team members by making appropriate referrals.

 - Facilitates staff, patient, and family decision-making by providing educational tools.

 - Understands Medicare reimbursement and coding for all levels of service in addition to Medicaid and other regulatory requirements, and documents accurately to support appropriate billing.

 - Reviews individual and panel performance data regularly and acts on opportunities to improve quality, patient engagement, productivity, and outcomes.

 - Understands how clinical practice contributes to the organization’s financial sustainability, including revenue, care margin, and billable census.

 - Actively participates in any mandatory meetings of the organization.

 - Participates in after-hours on-call rotation.

 


YOUR EXPERIENCE AND  QUALIFICATIONS

 - Active, unrestricted Georgia RN and NP license, with the ability to obtain additional state licensure.
   
   - Additional Texas and/or New Jersey RN & NP licensure, highly preferred.

 - DEA licensure, or the ability to obtain

 - Graduate of an accredited nurse practitioner program

 - ANP, AGNP, or FNP Certification required

 - ACHPN certification or ability to obtain ACHPN certification required

 - 2+ years experience providing NP care to complex, seriously ill patients

 - Experience with, or interest in, outcomes-focused and value-based care, including working from data and scorecards

 - Strong communication skills for goals-of-care and hospice transition conversations

 - Ability to work in a remote environment, Monday-Friday 8:30am-5:00pm Eastern Time, with rotating evening/weekend on-call coverage

 


COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

 - Salary Range: $130-$160k annually. Pay for this position will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to: your prior experience and skills related to the position, geographic location, company needs, and current market demands.

 - Great humans deserve great benefits! At Vynca, full time employees are eligible for benefits such as: medical, dental, and vision insurance, income protection benefits, flexible PTO, company holidays, 401k, and access to other wellness benefits.

 - Continuing medical education reimbursement and company paid Malpractice, DEA, and Licensure.


ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

 - The hiring process for this role may consist of applying, followed by a phone screen, online assessment(s), interview(s), an offer, and background/reference checks.

 - Background Screening: A background check, which may include a drug test or other health screenings depending on the role, will be required prior to employment.

 - Job Description Scope: This job description is not exhaustive and may include additional activities, duties, and responsibilities not listed herein.

 - Vaccination Requirement: Employees in patient, client, or customer-facing roles must be vaccinated against influenza. Requests for religious or medical accommodations will be considered but may not always be approved.

 - Employment Eligibility: Compliance with federal law requires identity and work eligibility verification using E-Verify upon hire.

 - Equal Opportunity Employer: At Vynca Inc., we embrace diversity and are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace. We value all applicants regardless of race, color, religion, age, national origin, ancestry, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, disability, genetic information, citizenship status, or membership in any other protected group under federal, state, or local law.

 - Environmental Conditions and Physical Requirements: Works with Vynca patients/clients remotely and/or in-person. Successfully performs the essential duties and responsibilities of the position through the use of physical activities as described below:
   
   - Regularly requires sitting, standing, walking, talking, use of hands, listening, and observing.
   
   - Regularly requires working at a computer for an entire shift (with appropriate breaks).
   
   - Regularly requires use of laptop and video-conferencing technology.
   
   - Occasionally requires reaching, stooping, bending, kneeling, and lifting items weighing 25 pounds or less.
   
   - Occasional travel may be required to perform job duties, attend training, or company events.

jobs.title: Maintenance Technician
jobs.description:
Maintenance Technician

Join the team driving the future of Recycling! Triumvirate Environmental, one of the largest environmental services firms in North America, is seeking an Maintenance Technician for our Halifax recycling operation.  The pay range for this position is $20-$35/ hr. depending upon education and experience. The schedule is Monday-Friday 0800-1700.

In this role, you will do more than just turn a wrench, you will keep the heartbeat of our recycling facility running strong. From managing maintenance & production inventories to troubleshooting, repairing, and installing industrial equipment. From troubleshooting, repairing, and installing industrial equipment to maintaining inventories and performing proactive maintenance. You will play a hands-on role in ensuring that our advanced recycling machinery operates at peak performance.

If you are motivated, mechanically inclined, and ready to take ownership of both equipment reliability and operational excellence, we want to hear from you.

At Triumvirate, we are not just another employer; we are a growth company built on innovation, safety, and WOW-level service. We support higher education, life sciences, healthcare, and advanced manufacturing industries with sustainability at our core. Our dedication to sustainability and ethical standards drives our long-term success and strengthens relationships with stakeholders.  For more information, please click here:  https://www.triumvirate.com/social-responsibility.

Essential Responsibilities:

• Keep our operations running smoothly with proactive preventative maintenance/ repairs.

• Troubleshoot and solve mechanical and electrical issues that keep production moving.

• Inspect, service, and optimize extruders, conveyors, pumps, motors, and other key equipment.

• Install new equipment, calibrate machines, and continually improve uptime/ efficiency.

• Partner with operators, and managers to WOW both internal and external customers.

• Lead with safety to help foster a culture of innovation, and continuous improvement.

• Perform miscellaneous job duties as required.

Basic Requirements:

• At least 2 years of industrial maintenance experience (extrusion, electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, or hydraulic systems a plus).

• Ability to read and interpret manuals, blueprints, and work orders.

• Hands-on skills with power/hand tools, troubleshooting, and preventative maintenance.

• Knowledge of PLCs, Lean manufacturing, and 5S principles.

• A strong team mindset and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

• High school diploma or GED (trade school, associate's degree, or welding/fabrication skills preferred).

• Must be able to lift 50 pounds repetitively.

• Willingness to work

• Ability to work overtime when needed.

• This role is considered safety sensitive.

• Must be willing to consent to Motor Vehicle Record screening, criminal background check, pre-employment physical, and drug screen (inclusive of THC)

• Must have a reliable form of transportation.

• Maintain consistent and timely attendance.

• Must be eligible to work in the United States without future sponsorship.

Preferred Qualifications/Requirements:

• Experience with PLC troubleshooting/programing

• Skills in welding and metal fabrication

• Familiarity with hydraulic, pneumatic, or electrical systems

• Knowledge of industrial automation or robotics

• Background in mechanical repair, machine installation, or process improvement

Work Environment:

It’s important that candidates fully understand the environment they’ll be working in. This role is hands-on, fast paced, and critical to keeping our operation moving.

• Safety-First Culture: Hearing protection and other PPE are required. Safety isn’t optional; it’s the foundation of everything we do. All required PPE is provided by Triumvirate.

• Manufacturing Setting: You’ll work in a large, 100,000+-square-foot recycling facility that is always active with production, equipment movement, and inbound deliveries.

• Dynamic Conditions: Seasonal temperature changes, radio communication with operators and managers, and constant coordination across teams keep things moving quickly.

• Team-Oriented Atmosphere: You will be part of a 30+ employee operation where collaboration, communication, and accountability are essential.

• On Your Feet: Expect to be moving across large areas of the plant where the surface is concrete, responding to maintenance needs, and staying hands-on with equipment.

• Potential limited Travel: May be required to maintain offsite warehouse locations and training

• Be ready for change: Duties, responsibilities and activities may change as our operation grows

Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change, or new ones may be assigned at any time with or without notice.

#LI-Onsite

Besides Health, Dental and Vision Insurance, we contribute to a 401k, offer a generous tuition reimbursement program, TONS of safety training for some positions with opportunities for external trainings and certifications, Mentorship & Career Succession Planning, Relocation Opportunities, Auto/Home insurance discounts, pet assistance discount plans, discounted movie passes & more!

To learn more about our business, culture, and the exciting work that we are doing in the industry, find us on LinkedIn, Instagram (@triumvirateenvironmental), or our website!

Triumvirate Environmental is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. As an Equal Opportunity Employer (EOE), Triumvirate does not discriminate based on race, national origin, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, or other legally protected status. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Individuals with Disabilities and Protected Veterans are encouraged to apply.

If you have a disability and need accommodation during the application and hiring process, please contact us at https://www.triumvirate.com/contact or call us at 888-834-9697. jobs.title: R&D Sterile Compounding Technician
jobs.description:
Hims & Hers is the leading health and wellness platform, on a mission to help the world feel great through the power of better health. We are redefining healthcare by putting the customer first and delivering access to care that is affordable, accessible, and personal, from diagnosis to treatment to delivery. No two people are the same, so we provide access to personalized care designed for results. By normalizing health & wellness challenges and innovating on their solutions, we’re making better health outcomes easier to achieve. 



Hims & Hers is a public company, traded on the NYSE under the ticker symbol “HIMS.” To learn more about the brand and offerings, you can visit hims.com/about http://hims.com/about and hims.com/how-it-works http://hims.com/how-it-works . For information on the company’s outstanding benefits, culture, and its talent-first flexible/remote work approach, see below and visit www.hims.com/careers-professionals http://www.hims.com/careers-professionals.




ABOUT THE ROLE:

Hims & Hers is looking for a dependable, detail-oriented R&D Sterile Compounding Technician to support sterile product development. Working alongside our formulation scientists, you will prepare development and feasibility batches, execute experimental protocols in controlled environments, and capture the high-quality data that moves new sterile products forward.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys iterating and troubleshooting while respecting the discipline of GMP, aseptic technique, and approved protocols.



Hours: 

Standard Hours: Typically 7:00 AM – 3:30 PM.

 - Flexibility Required: Must be available for occasional early starts or late finishes (window of 6:00 AM – 6:00 PM) based on production mixes, business needs, and travel.




YOU WILL:

 - Prepare and compound sterile development, feasibility, and engineering batches according to approved protocols, SOPs, and batch records.

 - Perform dilution, concentration, and gravimetric/volumetric calculations accurately and verify them as required.

 - Operate and maintain laboratory and process equipment, including balances, pH meters, mixers, filtration systems, pumps, and semi-automated and automated filling equipment.

 - Perform aseptic processing, filtration, and filling in ISO 5-8 environments, including material transfer and in-process visual inspection of units for foreign matter.

 - Perform routine compounding operations, including measuring, compounding, and sterilizing labware and solutions, and verify steps as required.

 - Label, package, and ship development and feasibility samples in accordance with approved procedures.

 - Execute experimental plans, adapting technique as results change, within defined protocol boundaries.

 - Document all work in real time in lab notebooks, batch records, and Excel, following data integrity principles (ALCOA+). Complete controlled documents and assignments right the first time, with minimal errors and within the required timeline.

 - Promptly report unexpected results, deviations, and improvement ideas to the formulation scientist or supervisor through proper channels, rather than working around them. Support continuous improvement efforts.

 - Identify, communicate, troubleshoot, and help implement solutions for problems noticed in the cleanroom or during critical processes.

 - Assemble and organize experimental data and communicate status to R&D and cross-functional partners (Quality, Manufacturing, Analytical). Collaborate across teams to keep projects moving.

 - Prepare, clean, sterilize, and depyrogenate labware and equipment; clean and maintain cleanroom equipment; keep cleanroom suites and support areas organized and inspection-ready.

 - Complete required training (GMP, aseptic technique, safety) and maintain gowning and aseptic qualifications (e.g., media fill, gloved fingertip sampling), working within your qualified scope.

 - Step in flexibly as priorities and timelines shift, and help meet batch schedules and project targets.




YOU HAVE:

 - High school diploma or equivalent; [Associate’s/Bachelor’s in a scientific field] preferred.

 - Experience in a sterile compounding, pharmaceutical cleanroom, GMP, or laboratory formulation setting.

 - Strong aseptic technique, garbing, and cleanroom behavior.

 - Proficiency with pharmaceutical calculations (dilutions, concentrations, unit conversions).

 - Meticulous documentation habits and understanding of data integrity.

 - Deep understanding of why sterility matters, and of the differences between mechanical cleaning, sanitization, disinfection, and sterilization.

 - Hands-on experience with laboratory and process equipment (balances, pH meters, mixers, filtration, pumps).

 - Ability to work independently, understand objectives, and ask clarifying questions early to meet production and project targets with minimal supervision.

 - Strong organizational and communication skills.

 - Ability to stand for extended periods and work in gowned, controlled environments.




PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 - 1+ years of sterile compounding, cleanroom manufacturing, or pharmaceutical lab experience.

 - Working knowledge of USP <797>/<800>, cGMP, and GDP.

 - Experience with needle/syringe manipulation; media fill and gloved fingertip sampling qualification history.

 - Experience operating semi-automated or automated filling machines.




WHAT MAKES YOU SUCCESSFUL:

 - Experimental mindset: you troubleshoot proactively and treat unexpected results as information.

 - Calm and deliberate under pressure.

 - Self-directed but not unilateral: you act with a clear understanding of requirements and seek guidance when unsure. You are comfortable being wrong and unafraid to ask.

 - Organized and collaborative: you keep work tidy inside and outside the cleanroom and communicate clearly across teams.

 - Self-motivated and proactive: you notice problems early, raise them, and help solve them.

 - Dependable: teammates can count on you to follow SOPs and batch records exactly and to step in when needed.




OUR BENEFITS (THERE ARE MORE BUT HERE ARE SOME HIGHLIGHTS):

 - Competitive salary & equity compensation for full-time roles

 - Unlimited PTO, company holidays, and quarterly mental health days

 - Comprehensive health benefits including medical, dental & vision, and parental leave

 - Employee Stock Purchase Program (ESPP)

 - 401k benefits with employer matching contribution

 - Offsite team retreats







We are committed to building a workforce that reflects diverse perspectives and prioritizes ethics, wellness, and a strong sense of belonging. If you're excited about this role, we encourage you to apply—even if you're not sure if your background or experience is a perfect match.



Hims considers all qualified applicants for employment, including applicants with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the California Fair Chance Act, and any similar state or local fair chance laws.



It is unlawful in Massachusetts to require or administer a lie detector test as a condition of employment or continued employment. An employer who violates this law shall be subject to criminal penalties and civil liability.



Hims & Hers is committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, please contact us at accommodations@forhims.com and describe the needed accommodation. Your privacy is important to us, and any information you share will only be used for the legitimate purpose of considering your request for accommodation. Hims & Hers gives consideration to all qualified applicants without regard to any protected status, including disability. Please do not send resumes to this email address.



To learn more about how we collect, use, retain, and disclose Personal Information, please visit our Global Candidate Privacy Statement https://www.hims.com/global-candidate-privacy-statement.

jobs.title: Construction Engineering Technician (CET)
jobs.description:
Copper River Technologies is seeking a highly motivated Construction Engineering Technician (CET) to support NAVFAC Mid-Atlantic construction projects in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Construction Engineering Technician serves as a key member of the construction management team by providing quality assurance inspections, construction oversight, safety monitoring, contract administration support, and technical assistance throughout all phases of federal construction projects. The ideal candidate will have extensive experience supporting NAVFAC or USACE construction projects while ensuring contractor compliance with quality, safety, and contractual requirements.

Responsibilities (include but are not limited to):

Quality Assurance & Construction Oversight

• Coordinate and monitor the Contractor's Construction Quality Management (CQM) Program throughout project execution.

• Review contractor Quality Control (QC) Plans and provide recommendations for Government approval.

• Attend Preparatory, Initial, and Follow-Up Quality Control meetings to verify compliance with contract requirements.

• Inspect construction activities, materials, equipment, and workmanship to ensure compliance with plans, specifications, and applicable codes.

• Verify installed quantities, materials, and completed work prior to invoice approval.

• Witness testing and commissioning of mechanical, electrical, HVAC, roofing, fire protection, utility, and life safety systems.

• Maintain project photographs and detailed construction documentation throughout project execution.

Safety & Compliance

• Monitor contractor compliance with EM 385-1-1 Safety & Health Requirements and OSHA regulations.

• Review Activity Hazard Analyses (AHAs), Accident Prevention Plans (APPs), and site-specific safety documentation.

• Participate in safety inspections, stand-downs, accident investigations, and corrective action reviews.

• Review crane lift plans and observe critical lift operations in accordance with NAVFAC P-307 requirements.

• Ensure contractors conduct required toolbox safety meetings and submit required safety documentation.

Project & Contract Support

• Assist the Construction Manager with reviewing construction drawings, specifications, Requests for Information (RFIs), and contractor submittals.

• Participate in pre-bid site visits, preconstruction conferences, partnering meetings, and project progress meetings.

• Review contractor schedules, three-week look-ahead schedules, daily reports, and progress documentation.

• Assist with environmental compliance reviews, utility coordination, permits, and temporary construction facilities.

• Support contract modifications, Government estimates, proposal reviews, and contractor performance evaluations.

• Assist with project closeout activities, including punch list inspections, as-built drawings, warranties, Operations & Maintenance (O&M) manuals, and final acceptance documentation.

• Perform additional duties as assigned.

Essential Job Qualifications and Requirements:

• Clearance

• Active Secret Security Clearance required

• Education and Certifications:

• Ability to pass the USACE EM 385-1-1 Safety & Health Examination within 15 days of onboarding

• Required Experience and Skills: Minimum 5 years of experience as a Quality Control Manager supporting NAVFAC or USACE construction projects OR Minimum 10 years of experience as a Foreman in Concrete, Mechanical, Electrical, Masonry, or Carpentry on commercial, industrial, or military construction projects Construction Quality Management (CQM) for Contractors certification prior to start or the ability to obtain it within 60 days of hire OSHA 30-Hour Construction Safety certification or ability to obtain within 30 days of hire Thorough understanding of construction quality management, contractor quality control procedures, and federal construction contract requirements

• Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Strong understanding of federal construction quality assurance and inspection practices Ability to interpret construction drawings, specifications, shop drawings, and technical documentation Knowledge of construction scheduling, testing, commissioning, and project documentation Excellent organizational and documentation skills Strong problem-solving and analytical abilities Ability to communicate effectively with contractors, engineers, architects, contracting officers, and Government representatives Ability to work independently while managing multiple priorities on active construction sites

Preferred Qualifications

• Previous experience supporting NAVFAC or USACE military construction programs

• Familiarity with NAVFAC Business Management System (BMS)

• Experience reviewing testing and commissioning documentation

• Knowledge of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and federal construction contracting processes

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description:
As a Staff Software Engineer on the Design System team, you will build and evolve the engineering surface of the design system: the theme system, the design tokens, and the tooling that lets engineers, designers, and product teams apply it correctly. You will work in close partnership with design and product counterparts, and your decisions will ripple across internal product teams and external customers, so systems thinking and a working command of accessibility are as important as your front-end craft.

Roles and responsibilities

• Evolve the theme system and its design token architecture, covering token taxonomy, platform transforms, theming APIs, and the guardrails that keep themes accessible.

• Engineer tooling that makes the design system easy to adopt: theme builders, linting and audit rules, codemods, Figma to code workflows, and local development aids.

• Build AI skills and tooling that put the design system to work for engineers, designers, and product partners, so prototypes and production code generate on-system by default.

• Partner closely with design system designers and product managers, weighing design intent, customer need, and engineering cost in every decision rather than optimizing for one.

• Trace the downstream impact of every change across consuming teams and customer instances, and manage versioning, deprecation, and breaking-change communication accordingly.

• Hold the system to WCAG 2.2 Level AA, including contrast, forced colors, focus visibility, and reflow, and build automated checks that catch regressions before release.

• Collaborate with component authors and the component engine team on API contracts, token consumption, and release sequencing.

• Maintain the enablement surface for the system, including API documentation, usage guidance, and migration paths.

• Support adopters directly: triage issues, unblock teams, and feed recurring friction back into the roadmap.

• Raise the bar through technical design review, code review, and mentorship across the design system and consuming teams.

• 8+ years of professional front-end engineering experience, including significant time building or operating a design system used by multiple teams.
• Advanced TypeScript and modern JavaScript, with deep command of the browser platform: DOM, events, Custom Elements, and Shadow DOM.
• Hands-on experience with design tokens: schema design, transform pipelines such as Style Dictionary, and multi-platform or multi-brand distribution.
• Expert CSS, particularly theming at scale with custom properties, cascade layers, modern layout, container queries, and forced colors mode.
• Current working knowledge of WCAG 2.2 Level AA and how to apply it to tokens, themes, and components, with hands-on screen reader and keyboard testing.
• Fluency applying AI tooling in your own engineering practice, including agentic coding tools, and sound judgment about where generated output needs human review.
• Strong front-end build, release, and versioning skills across tooling such as Vite, Rollup, or Webpack, plus semantic versioning in a monorepo.
• Demonstrated systems thinking: you reason about cascading impact across dependent teams and customers, and you plan migrations instead of shipping surprises.
• Proven track record of collaborating as a peer with designers and product managers, and of influencing technical direction across teams without direct authority.
• Clear technical writing, with experience documenting APIs and guiding other engineers through adoption.

Nice to have

• Experience building AI tooling for other engineers, designers, or product partners to use, such as agent skills, MCP servers, or prompt-driven UI generation.
• Experience building developer-facing documentation or enablement sites.

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $149,800 - $262,200, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. jobs.title: Staff Validation Engineer, Electrical Systems
jobs.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is hiring a Staff Validation Engineer, Electrical Systems to join our Electrical & Software Test organization. In this role you will be the technical lead for system-level testing of electrical, software, and control systems on test assets that deliver learnings on our Power Conversion Systems (DC/DC, inverter, etc.) and Network Systems (plant-level communications, etc.). These assets are a cornerstone of our validation strategy.



You will be deeply accountable for identifying, planning, and executing system-level tests that deliver learnings to our Power Conversion Systems and Network Systems teams, and for turning those learnings into design changes, requirements, and product-readiness decisions. The ideal candidate pairs rigorous technical depth and first-principles thinking with the leadership required to align cross-functional teams and mentor growing engineers and technicians.



This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the scaling of our battery technology and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!



Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Identify the system-level tests, test assets, and operating conditions needed to retire the highest-risk electrical, software, and control system unknowns.

 - Architect comprehensive test plans and procedures that validate Power Conversion Systems (DC/DC, inverter) and Network Systems (plant-level communications) behaviors across electrical, software, and control layers.

 - Act as the primary technical bridge between design teams (electrical hardware, software, controls), test engineering, and product management to translate high-level requirements into executable validation strategies.

 - Partner closely with Site Operations and Facilities teams to manage the infrastructure footprint, power requirements, safety protocols (hazard reviews, FMEA), and continuous uptime of test assets.

 - Lead the day-to-day execution of test campaigns. When anomalies occur, spearhead root-cause analysis (RCA) and triage across electrical hardware, software, controls, and test infrastructure.

 - Synthesize complex test data into clear, actionable engineering reports and leadership dashboards to gate product milestones.

 - Act as a force multiplier by coaching, mentoring, and leveling up junior engineers and test technicians.

 - Champion a culture of safety, cleanliness, 5S, and rigorous documentation within the testing lab environment.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - 8+ years of experience in systems validation, integration testing, or hardware test engineering (ideally within power electronics, grid storage, renewables, electric vehicles, or aerospace).

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, Controls, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

 - Deep familiarity with power conversion hardware (DC/DC converters, inverters, rectifiers), high-voltage power distribution, protection, and control architectures.

 - Experience with high-power industrial systems, grid-tied equipment, or power electronics at utility or industrial scale.

 - Proficiency with test automation frameworks (e.g., Python, LabVIEW, MATLAB/Simulink) and data analysis pipelines for high-rate electrical data.

 - Familiarity with network protocols standard to industrial, grid, and automotive systems (CAN, Modbus, Ethernet, EtherCAT, DNP3, IEC 61850).

 - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving hardware startup environment; able to carve out a path forward when requirements are fluid.

 - Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work cross-functionally and present test findings to design, controls, and leadership audiences in a fast-paced environment.

• Run cross-team workflow and coordination so work moves cleanly between teams

The focus is on domestic health care programs, including topics such as Medicare, Medicaid, and other public health insurance programs; health plan performance and quality measurement; regulatory science and evidence-based policy; and clinical trial and patient advocacy.

Founded in 1946 and headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, the American Institutes for Research (AIR) is a nonpartisan, not-for-profit organization that conducts behavioral and social science research and delivers technical assistance to address some of the most pressing challenges in the United States and globally. jobs.title: Behavioral Health Lead (LICSW)
jobs.description:
Akido builds AI-powered doctors. Akido is the first AI-native care provider, combining cutting-edge technology with a nationwide medical network to address America’s physician shortage and make exceptional healthcare universal. Its AI empowers doctors to deliver faster, more accurate, and more compassionate care.

Serving 500K+ patients across California, Rhode Island, and New York, Akido offers primary and specialty care in 26 specialties—from serving unhoused communities in Los Angeles to ride-share drivers in New York.

Founded in 2015 (YC W15), Akido is expanding its risk-bearing care models and scaling ScopeAI, its breakthrough clinical AI platform. Read more about Akido’s $60M Series B. More info at Akidolabs.com.

The Opportunity

RIPCMG is seeking an experienced Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker (LICSW) to serve as its Behavioral Health Lead. This is a working clinical leader role. About 80–85% of the week is direct patient care, The remaining 15–20% is spent leading the RIPCPC Integrated Behavioral Health team of LCSW and LICSW clinicians, running the behavioral health program day to day, and serving as the organization’s point person for behavioral health regulatory and payor contract matters.

The Behavioral Health Lead practices in two modes. The first is longitudinal care: carrying a panel of patients who need ongoing psychotherapy. The second is integrated behavioral health: working inside the primary care team through warm handoffs, same-day consults, brief interventions, and the Collaborative Care Model (CoCM). The right candidate is comfortable moving between a scheduled therapy hour and a hallway handoff in the same afternoon, and knows how to decide which patients belong in which model.

Although employed by RIPCMG, the Behavioral Health Lead works across both organizations: practicing in the medical group, supervising the IPA’s behavioral health clinicians, and making sure behavioral health services meet state requirements and the terms of each health plan contract. This person will shape how behavioral health is built into a growing organization: the workflows, the referral criteria, the measurement, the team, and the contracts that pay for it. It is a chance to build a program, not just join one.

What you’ll do

• Carry a longitudinal panel of children, adolescents, and adults who need ongoing treatment, including diagnostic evaluation, treatment planning, and individual, family, and group psychotherapy using evidence-based approaches.

• Deliver integrated behavioral health in the primary care setting: accept warm handoffs, provide same-day consults and brief interventions, and help primary care clinicians manage behavioral health needs within the visit.

• Serve as behavioral health care manager for patients enrolled in Collaborative Care. Engage patients, administer validated measures (such as PHQ-9, GAD-7, and age-appropriate tools), track every patient in the registry, treat to target, and bring the caseload to weekly review with the psychiatric consultant.

• Communicate psychiatric consultant recommendations to the treating primary care clinician and follow through on changes to the care plan.

• Conduct suicide and safety risk assessments, develop safety plans, and coordinate with crisis resources such as BH Link, Kids’ Link RI, and mobile crisis services when needed.

• Coordinate referrals to higher levels of care and community services, and move patients between longitudinal therapy, brief intervention, and Collaborative Care as their needs change.

• Meet productivity expectations of [15-18] billable encounters per week plus an active Collaborative Care caseload of about [25–30] patients, adjusted for supervision load.

• Complete timely, compliant documentation for psychotherapy and Collaborative Care, including accurate time logs, so that minutes are never counted toward two services.

Team leadership and supervision

• Provide clinical supervision to the RIPCPC Integrated Behavioral Health team of LCSW and LICSW clinicians, including case consultation, documentation review, and oversight of high-risk cases.

• Provide licensure-track supervision to LCSWs working toward the LICSW, consistent with Rhode Island Board of Social Work Examiners requirements, and complete supervised-experience verification for the Board.

• Lead a weekly team huddle and caseload review. Assign new referrals by acuity and fit to longitudinal therapy, integrated care, or Collaborative Care.

• Provide clinical input on hiring, onboarding, training, coverage, and performance for RIPCPC clinicians, in partnership with RIPCPC leadership and Human Resources, which retain employment authority.

Program operations and quality

• Own behavioral health workflows across RIPCMG sites: referral intake, warm handoffs, Collaborative Care consent and enrollment, registry management, step-up and step-down criteria, and crisis response.

• Track and report access (time to first appointment), caseload, productivity, and outcomes, including PHQ-9 response and remission and HEDIS behavioral health measures such as depression screening and follow-up, depression remission or response, and follow-up after emergency department visits for mental illness.

• Partner with billing and compliance on payor coverage for psychotherapy and Collaborative Care services, documentation standards, and periodic chart audits.

• Educate primary care clinicians and staff on referral criteria, warm handoffs, and how to work with the behavioral health team.

• Represent behavioral health in RIPCMG and RIPCPC leadership meetings and with community partners.

Regulatory and payor contract lead

• Serve as the point person for behavioral health regulatory questions across RIPCMG and RIPCPC, including Rhode Island licensure and supervision rules, state Medicaid and health plan requirements, confidentiality rules for behavioral health and substance use records, and mental health parity.

• Track changes in federal and state behavioral health rules and payor policies, including coverage and billing rules for psychotherapy, Collaborative Care, and behavioral health integration services. Translate changes into workflow, documentation, and training updates.

• Serve as the behavioral health subject matter expert for payor contracting. Review proposed contract terms, fee schedules, and quality requirements for behavioral health services before signing, and flag operational or financial risks.

• Act as the named behavioral health contact for health plans on credentialing questions, behavioral health quality programs, delegated oversight, and audits. Prepare policies, evidence, and corrective action responses as needed.

• Partner with Credentialing to keep behavioral health clinicians enrolled with each payor, and confirm which services each license type can bill under each contract.

Who you are

Required

• Master of Social Work (MSW) from a program accredited by the Council on Social Work Education.

• Active, unrestricted Rhode Island LICSW license at time of hire.

• Five or more years of post-master’s clinical experience, including at least two years in integrated primary care, Collaborative Care, or another medical setting.

• Experience providing clinical supervision to licensed clinicians, and eligibility to provide licensure-track supervision under Rhode Island regulations.

• Working knowledge of behavioral health billing, payor coverage rules, and Rhode Island regulatory requirements for behavioral health services.

• Clinical experience treating children, adolescents, and adults.

• Skill in both brief, solution-focused interventions and longitudinal, evidence-based psychotherapy.

• Experience with measurement-based care, suicide risk assessment, and safety planning.

• Comfort with electronic health records, registries, and basic performance reporting.

Preferred

• Formal Collaborative Care training (for example, through the University of Washington AIMS Center) and experience as a behavioral health care manager in an operating CoCM program.

• Experience launching or expanding an integrated behavioral health or Collaborative Care program, including workflow design and billing setup.

• Pediatric and adolescent integrated behavioral health experience.

• Training in modalities such as CBT, TF-CBT, DBT, motivational interviewing, or parent-child interventions.

• Experience supporting payor contracting, credentialing, delegated audits, or regulatory compliance for behavioral health services.

• Working knowledge of the Rhode Island behavioral health system, including crisis services and Medicaid managed care.

• Bilingual English/Spanish.

Physical Demands: Mostly sedentary work duties require exerting up to thirty pounds of force occasionally and/or small amounts of force frequently. Sedentary work typically involves sitting most of the time but may involve walking or standing for brief periods.

Salary range

$105,000—$125,000 USD

jobs.title: Data Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
At Trella Health, our mission is simple: empowering meaningful change in healthcare.

We are building AI-enabled intelligence and workflows that help healthcare organizations make smarter decisions, strengthen operations, and support healthier outcomes for patients. Our platform connects health systems and post-acute providers through actionable intelligence and connected workflows that improve how care is coordinated across the healthcare continuum.

That work starts with our people. Trellavators are collaborative, curious, and committed to doing meaningful work that makes a measurable impact. We move quickly, support each other, keep our commitments, and continuously look for better ways to serve our customers and one another.

If you are excited by the opportunity to grow your career while helping shape the future of healthcare intelligence, workflows, and outcomes, we would love to meet you.

Position Overview:

We’re looking for a Data Engineering Manager who still likes getting their hands dirty. You’ll lead our Data Engineering team and help build a healthcare data platform that’s fast, scalable, and ready for whatever we throw at it next.

Your job: design, build, and tune the pipelines and platforms that turn diverse healthcare data into analytics and insights people actually use. You’ll lead the team and roll up your sleeves alongside them, putting best-in-class architecture and governance in place while keeping us HIPAA and SOC 2 compliant.

The toolkit includes Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS. The problems are big, the data is complicated, and that's what makes it an exciting challenge to tackle.

Location: This role is remote with a strong preference for candidates within commuting distance of Atlanta, GA; Philadelphia, PA. We will also consider applicants based in other U.S. locations.

Reports to: CTO

As a Data Engineering Manager at Trella, you will:

• Lead and scale a high-performing data engineering team through hands-on technical leadership, mentorship, and the establishment of best practices that drive innovation, collaboration, and continuous improvement

• Architect, build, and evolve a centralized, cloud-native data platform supporting diverse healthcare datasets, including medical and Rx claims, EHR, CCLF, and BCDA data sources

• Design, implement, and operate scalable data pipelines for ingestion, transformation, and normalization to support analytics, machine learning, and GenAI use cases

• Implement flexible data ingestion patterns, including batch processing, streaming services, and FHIR-based APIs, to ingest data into the data lake

• Optimize data platforms and pipelines for performance, reliability, scalability, and cost efficiency

• Lead the design and enforcement of data governance standards, access controls, and encryption to meet HIPAA and SOC 2 compliance and certification requirements

• Develop and maintain clear, comprehensive documentation covering data platform architecture, ETL/ELT processes, data lineage, and metadata

• Partner cross-functionally with data science, QA, software engineering, product, and business stakeholders to deliver trusted, timely, and high-quality data assets

• Collaborate with DevOps to enable automated, scalable deployment of data pipelines and platform components using CI/CD and infrastructure-as-code practices

• Stay current with emerging trends and best practices in data engineering, healthcare data management, and advanced analytics, applying learnings to continuously improve the platform and team

This job might be a fit for you if you have:

• 8+ years of experience in data engineering, with demonstrated success coaching and developing technical talent and leading the design, delivery, and operation of cloud-based data platforms in production environments

• Deep proficiency in Python, SQL, and modern ETL/ELT frameworks for building reliable, production-grade data workflows

• Hands-on experience with Databricks, Snowflake, and AWS services (e.g., S3, Glue, Lambda, EMR), along with modern data platform technologies and transformation tools such as dbt or SQLMesh

• Strong ability to design scalable, modular codebases that promote maintainability, reuse, testing, and cross-team collaboration

• Experience implementing and leveraging data lineage to understand dependencies, assess upstream and downstream impact, and support governance and change management

• Solid understanding of data governance, data quality, and data security principles, including their application in regulated environments

• Proficiency in data modeling, database design, and data warehousing concepts for analytical and operational use cases

• Ability to partner effectively with DevOps to define and align on deployment standards, environment management, and operational best practices for data platforms and pipelines

• Working knowledge of healthcare data interoperability standards and APIs

About Trella Health

Trella Health is the AI-powered intelligence and workflow platform helping health systems and post-acute providers turn fragmented healthcare data into decisive action. We bring together market intelligence, referral workflows, patient discharge automation, and care coordination tools so healthcare organizations can make smarter decisions, strengthen business and clinical operations, and deliver high-quality, cost-efficient care.

Powered by billions of data points across claims, referrals, patient discharge, and clinical data, Trella Health gives customers the intelligence and workflows they need to understand their markets, build stronger referral relationships, coordinate patient care transitions, and grow with confidence.

Since launching our first product in 2016, Trella Health has continued to grow our team, our platform, and our impact across healthcare. Today, we support more than 17,000 customers, including leading post-acute providers and health systems, and more than 63,000 users across the care continuum.

Trella Health is headquartered in Atlanta, with a growing presence in Philadelphia and team members located across the country.

Join Us

At Trella Health, you will have the opportunity to do meaningful work with people who are focused on outcomes, committed to continuous improvement, and supportive of one another. We believe great work happens when team members feel trusted, connected, and empowered to grow.

Our culture is built on transparency, accountability, partnership, and the belief that better healthcare starts with better decisions. Trellavators work hard, move fast, celebrate wins, and have fun along the way.

We offer competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support team members inside and outside of work, including:

• Health, dental, vision, and voluntary benefits

• Competitive salary, incentive compensation, and equity shares

• 401(k) retirement savings

• Flexible PTO and 10 paid holidays

• Flexible work hours

• Paid leave programs

• Marketplace for discounted retail and entertainment

At Trella Health, you can grow your career while helping build technology that strengthens healthcare operations, improves care coordination, and supports healthier outcomes for patients.

Equal Opportunity Employer

Trella Health is an equal opportunity employer. All persons will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, national origin, marital status, age, disability, handicap, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected status as recognized by federal, state, or local laws.

jobs.title: Customer Solutions and Support
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Customer Support team is the front line for every Sift customer who runs into a question or a problem. We troubleshoot, triage, and resolve issues across Sift's Digital Trust & Safety products, working closely with Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, and Engineering to make sure customers get fast, accurate answers. We're the team customers remember when something goes right in a moment of frustration — and we take that responsibility seriously. We're also always looking for smarter ways to work, including using AI tools to help us respond faster and more consistently.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

We're looking for a Customer Support Specialist who's excited to learn a complex product and build real troubleshooting skills from the ground up. You're naturally curious about how things work, patient with customers who are frustrated, and comfortable asking questions when you don't know the answer yet. With guidance from senior teammates, you'll build the product knowledge and judgment that let you solve problems independently over time.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Responding to customer inquiries: Answer incoming support tickets and questions via our support channels, with guidance from senior Support team members on anything unfamiliar or complex.

 - Troubleshooting product issues: Learn to diagnose common issues in Sift's platform, using documentation and escalation paths to work through problems you haven't seen before.

 - Documenting and tracking cases: Keep clear, accurate records of customer issues and their resolutions in our support tools, so the next person helping that customer has full context.

 - Escalating appropriately: Recognize when an issue is beyond your current scope and loop in the right teammate or team, rather than guessing.

 - Contributing to our knowledge base: Help identify gaps in internal documentation and contribute notes or suggested edits as you learn.

 - Building product expertise: Develop a working understanding of Sift's product and the fraud landscape it operates in, growing your ability to solve problems independently.
   
   


WHAT WOULD MAKE YOU A STRONG FIT

Must-haves:

 - 1–3 years of experience in a customer-facing support, service, or help-desk role, or equivalent practical experience

 - Strong written communication skills — clear, empathetic, and precise, especially under a frustrated customer's pressure

 - Comfortable learning new software tools and systems quickly

 - Experience leveraging AI/LLM tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Cowork) for day-to-day work, and general fluency with AI-assisted workflows

 - A genuine curiosity about how things work, and a willingness to ask for help when you need it



Nice to have:

 - Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience

 - Experience with support ticketing tools (e.g., Zendesk, Salesforce)

 - Exposure to SaaS products or basic familiarity with APIs and SQL

 - Interest in fraud, payments, or trust & safety
   
   


OUR TYPICAL INTERVIEW PROCESS

 - Recruiter conversation: 30–45 minutes with a recruiter to discuss your background and the role.

 - Hiring manager screen: 30–45 minutes with the hiring manager to explore your fit for the position.

 - Interview loop with the team: covering a customer scenario walkthrough, written communication exercise, and values & behavior.
   
   


BENEFITS AND PERKS

 - Competitive total compensation package

 - 401k plan

 - Medical, dental and vision coverage

 - Flexible lifestyle wallet

 - Learning & development reimbursement

 - Flexible time off

 - Company Mental Health Days



Let’s build it together:

At Sift, we are intentionally building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace. We believe that diversity drives innovation, equity is a fundamental right, and inclusion is a basic human need. We envision a place where all Sifties feel secure sharing their authentic selves and diverse experiences with their teams, their customers, and their community – ultimately using this empowerment and authenticity to build trust and create a safer Internet.

This document provides transparency around how Sift handles the personal data of job applicants: https://sift.com/recruitment-privacy

A little about us:
Sift is the AI-powered fraud platform securing digital trust for leading global businesses. Our deep investments in machine learning and user identity, a data network scoring 1 trillion events per year, and a commitment to long-term customer success empower more than 700 customers to grow fearlessly. Global brands rely on Sift to unlock growth and deliver seamless consumer experiences. jobs.title: Senior DTx Quality Engineer
jobs.description:
Who We Are:

Click Therapeutics, Inc., develops, validates, and commercializes software as prescription medical treatments for people with unmet medical needs. As a leading innovator of Digital Therapeutics™, Click delivers accessible, clinically proven, FDA-regulated prescription treatments to the smartphone in your hand. Click’s treatments are defined by a commitment to applying technical and scientific rigor and patient-centric design to the development process. This results in uniquely engaging experiences that achieve compelling clinical outcomes for patients seeking new treatment options. Click Therapeutics continuously expands and refines its platform with novel cognitive, behavioral and neuromodulatory mechanisms of action and advanced data-driven tools such as artificial intelligence and machine learning. The digital therapeutics under development on Click’s platform address diverse areas of therapeutic need, including indications in psychiatry, neurology, oncology, immunology, and cardiometabolic diseases. Consistently named a best place to work, Click fosters an inclusive, diverse workforce of innovators, clinicians, scientists, researchers, designers, technologists, engineers and more, united in a common mission to provide patients everywhere access to safe and effective prescription digital therapeutics. For more information, visit www.clicktherapeutics.com and connect with us on LinkedIn.

About the Role:

The Senior DTx (Digital Therapeutic) Quality Engineer has a key role in the development of Click’s Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) products. This position works alongside the Product Management, Software Engineering, and Testing teams and drives the day-to-day product quality activities while implementing Quality Management System (QMS) procedures in alignment with evolving FDA and international medical device regulations. The Senior DTx Quality Engineer reports to the Associate Director, Regulatory & Quality and has a direct role in bringing Click medical device software to the market.

This position is based out of Click’s headquarters located in Tribeca, NYC, at the center of one of the fastest-growing digital health communities. We have a hybrid working model that consists of at least 4 days in office each week.

Responsibilities:

• Drive product development processes, from a quality perspective, to ensure product development compliance with regulatory and quality standards throughout the Software Development Lifecycle.

• Drive on-going process improvements and collaborate with the technical teams to enhance implementation of procedures in an Agile framework.

• Lead product risk management activities to establish product risk assessments and trace the implementation of risk controls. Actively monitor for product risks, manage/mitigate where possible and communicate/escalate as needed.

• In coordination with the technical teams, develop and review design documentation including product requirements, design specifications, verification/validation test plans and reports, and traceability tables. Maintain records as part of the products’ Design and Development File.

• Manage post-production activities including complaint handling, data analysis, and defect tracking.

• Enable clear communication, prioritization, and decision making across multiple teams using post-production data to inform product updates and enhancements while implementing change control.

Qualifications:

At Click, we aren't just looking for talent; we are looking for the next evolution of the modern professional. To us, AI is not a future possibility, it is a present-day prerequisite. We expect every Click colleague to have seamlessly integrated AI into their professional workflow and personal productivity, using it as a force multiplier to move faster, think deeper, and deliver superlative results that were previously out of reach. If you do not yet view AI as an essential partner in your daily pursuit of excellence, you will find it impossible to keep pace with our mission. High performers who harness AI technology to transcend traditional boundaries and set new benchmarks for professional excellence will thrive at Click.

• Bachelor’s Degree, preferably in engineering 1-5 years of experience working in a medical device, software, or other technology field

• Ability to oversee quality management activities within multiple simultaneous projects

• Strong verbal and written communication skills to translate procedures into practice and effectively work with interdisciplinary teams and stakeholders

• Attention to detail and ability to generate clear technical documentation/records (i.e., protocols, reports, test methods, justifications)

Click Preferred Qualifications:

• Experience working with software products through full lifecycle with knowledge of iterative agile planning, development and delivery

• Proficiency in medical device quality system regulation and standards including ISO 13485.

• Familiarity with relevant SaMD standards and methodologies such as IEC 62304, IEC 14971, AAMI TIR 45

Compensation:

The base salary range for this position is between $120,000 - $142,000. The final base salary will be dependent upon skills, experience and location. In addition to the base salary, Click Therapeutics offers an annual performance-based cash bonus and a generous equity package.

Benefits:

The role includes great benefits and is an excellent wealth-building opportunity at a fast-growing pre-IPO company in a nascent and extremely exciting space.

Equal Employment Opportunity:
