jobs.location: Boston, Massachusetts, United States; Las Vegas, Nevada, United States; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, United States; Remote U.S.
jobs.description:
Motional is a leading autonomous driving company on a mission to make driverless vehicles a safe, reliable, and accessible reality. Backed by Hyundai Motor Group, Motional is at the forefront of the physical AI revolution. Motional isn't just building first-of-its-kind technology; we are transforming transportation to create safer streets and more sustainable mobility options.

The Systems Readiness and Performance team is the crucial bridge between software development and real-world deployment. We are responsible for driving system design, for verifying and validating the autonomy stack, and for defining, measuring, and validating system performance targets. We work closely with stakeholders in autonomy, vehicle platform, safety, infrastructure, and operations to build the safety case for our fully driverless IONIQ 5 robotaxis in Las Vegas and to shape the vehicle platform that comes next.

Mission Summary:

We are seeking a Principal Engineer to lead driverless readiness evaluations. In this role, you will analyze test results from commercial-grade software builds to identify, evaluate, and prioritize operational risks, collaborating closely with the safety team to define and implement necessary mitigations.

What You'll Be Doing:

• Oversee the testing: We evolve the system testing process with each iteration. So it is important to ensure any improvements or customizations are appropriately integrated during testing. This role works with those that execute the tests to ensure the assessment meets the intended scope.

• Analyze the results: While many of the tests are automatically executed and analyzed, the correctness of the results need to be ensured. Differing results may occur between different test modalities. Any differences need to be investigated and reconciled so the appropriate outcome is reported. This role ensures consistent and correct outcomes are reported.

• Identify the risks: This role organizes and identifies the risks resulting from the test analysis. These risks are further analyzed with the safety group for assessment and mitigation The risks are communicated to the different stakeholders including company leadership.

• Collaborate cross-functionally: We don’t work in a silo. As we find issues, we immediately collaborate with the developers to better understand the root cause. As appropriate, these issues are immediately communicated to the stakeholders, depending on the severity.

• Autonomy Roadmapping: This work places us in a great position to understand what features and improvements are needed from the autonomy stack. We work closely with the TPM and Commercial teams to support maintaining the appropriate autonomy development roadmap. Motional has the challenge of improving performance within the existing ODD while also expanding and scaling in new ones.

• Create and maintain tooling: We work with large data sets. Tooling is established for us to analyze this data. However, it needs to be maintained and evolved as we improve our processes. This role is responsible for the tooling to do the job.

What We're Looking For:

• Bachelor's degree in Systems Engineering, Computer Science, Aerospace Engineering, Robotics, or a related field; a Master's degree is preferred.

• 7+ years of engineering experience; experience with an ADAS or automated driving system is preferred.

• Strong understanding of modern software development principles and production best practices.

• Experience with database querying and visualization such as SQL, Looker.

• Experience with agentic based software development and data analysis

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, particularly in the context of complex system performance evaluation and data analysis.

• Proficient with Git and standard version control workflows.

• Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to effectively communicate technical concepts and results to diverse audiences (engineers, product managers, leadership).

• Proven ability to work both independently and effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team.

• Strong attention to detail and a commitment to data quality, accuracy, and rigorous testing.

• Comfortable working in a fast-paced, agile, continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) environment.

Physical Demands:

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit, talk, or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand and at times for long periods; walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms. The employee must occasionally lift and move up to 50 pounds.

Travel Requirements (up to 20%):

Expected to travel for 1-2 weeks each quarter visiting all of our testing sites - mostly to LV, but also domestically as needed for the business.

Working Environment:

The work environment characteristics described here represent those a team member encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The team member is regularly exposed to mechanical and computer parts. The team member is occasionally exposed to fumes and/or airborne particles. The noise level in the environment is low to moderate.

Higher purpose, greater impact.

jobs.description:
Chainguard is the trusted source for open source. By delivering hardened, secure, and production-ready builds of all the open source software engineers and AI agents rely on, Chainguard helps organizations build faster, stay compliant, and eliminate risk.

Our customers include Fortune 500 enterprises and global industry leaders, including Anduril, Canva, Fortinet, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, OpenAI, Snap Inc., and Snowflake.

Chainguard is venture-backed by leading investors, including Amplify, IVP, Kleiner Perkins, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Mantis VC, Redpoint Ventures, Sequoia Capital, and Spark Capital.

The role, in a nutshell:

We’re looking for a Senior Technical Support Engineer who’s equal parts problem-solver, translator, and customer hero. You’ll be the go-to person when customers hit snags with Chainguard Images, digging into technical mysteries, keeping folks informed, and partnering with Engineering to squash bugs before they cause chaos. This isn’t just “reset the password and move on” support: you’ll work on real, complex issues with modern tools (Docker, Kubernetes, GitHub, Helm charts, Terraform, etc.), make customers feel like superheroes themselves, and help shape how Chainguard delivers world-class support. About Us

We live and breathe our company values:

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Loan Management System
jobs.description:
DAVE VS. GOLIATH. WE’RE DAVE.

Dave is a financial app on a mission to build products that level the financial playing field. It is redefining the financial landscape by leveraging technology to create an affordable, transparent, and user-centric access to liquidity for millions of Americans. As a leading innovator in the U.S. financial services sector, Dave’s digital financial platform offers products designed to meet the credit needs of those underserved by traditional financial institutions. Dave’s offerings include its flagship ExtraCash product, providing members up to $500 within minutes. The company is on track to launch several new product offerings in 2026, including a Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) option.



Dave is focused on serving Americans who are financially vulnerable or living paycheck to paycheck. Dave is leading the charge in creating a new era of credit products that prioritizes speed, affordability, and accessibility, making it the go-to financial partner for those who need it most.



Flex card is Dave's newest and most ambitious product, a pay-in-4 card built for the millions of members living paycheck to paycheck who've never had fair access to credit. Behind every purchase it makes is the system that turns a balance into a loan, casts it into installments, services it, and collects it. That system is the loan management system (LMS), and it's what this role owns.

This is a senior individual-contributor role at the foundation of Flex and every loan product that comes after it. You'll own the LMS and the systems of record end-to-end: the ledger, loan casting, servicing, collections, and the compliance tooling around them. And you'll take it from a single-product build to a scalable platform, so that when Dave launches its next loan product, it runs on what you've built instead of starting over.

If you like real ownership, hard systems problems, and building the infrastructure that makes fair credit possible at scale, this role is for you.




WHAT YOU'LL BUILD & OWN

 - Own the loan management system: Lead the LMS and core systems of record: the ledger, loan casting at billing, the pay-in-4 installment structure, participation and installment fees, repayment, and collections.

 - Build the platform, not just the product: Lead the build-vs-buy decision and the migration off our current loan-servicing platform onto a foundation that makes Flex faster, more reliable, and easier to iterate on. From there, evolve it from a single-product integration into a multi-product platform that future loan products reuse instead of rebuild.

 - Ship the mechanics members feel: installment schedules aligned to paycheck dates, early payoff, and decline and failure handling.

 - Own the numbers: Define and track system health, payoff rates, and loss performance, and use them to prioritize where to invest.

 - Enable flawless execution: Work closely with Risk, Legal/Compliance (LECO), Data Science, Engineering, and Operations, and coordinate external partners (Coastal, LoanPro) on anything that touches casting, collections, or compliance.


THE IMPACT

The LMS is where Flex's unit economics are won or lost. Payoff rates, loss performance, and whether members can repay on a schedule that fits their paycheck all run through the system you'll own and small improvements compound across every loan.

You'll be building this foundation at its most formative stage. Get it right and Dave launches its next loan product in a fraction of the time, on infrastructure that's already compliant, auditable, and proven. The problems are real, the stakes are high, and your fingerprints will be all over how Dave lends for years to come.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Experience

 - 8 + years of product management experience, with meaningful time in lending, credit, or financial systems

 - Direct experience across the lending lifecycle (origination, underwriting, servicing, repayment, collections) and the risk and compliance considerations throughout

 - A track record building internal platforms or systems of record, ideally through a single-product-to-platform transition

 - Comfort setting direction in ambiguous, greenfield areas and driving execution across functions without formal authority

 - Strong analytical skills; comfortable using data to inform decisions

 - Proven ability to use AI tools as a force multiplier for speed, quality, and impact

Bonus

 - Experience with BNPL, installment, or pay-over-time products

 - Hands-on experience with third-party loan-servicing systems (LoanPro or similar)

 - Experience coordinating with bank or sponsor partners like Coastal

 - Familiarity with adverse action notices, Reg B / FCRA, and consumer-lending compliance

 - Experience with ledger or servicing migrations, or standing up a second product on shared infrastructure




WHY YOU'LL BE SUCCESSFUL HERE

You thrive where the architecture is still being written. You take ambiguous, high-stakes systems problems and turn them into clear plans that ship, making smart trade-offs between speed, resilience, and long-term flexibility. You're rigorous about correctness and controls, but you never lose sight of the member repaying on the other end.

You're steady when the stakes are high and the systems are load-bearing. You build trust with engineers, risk, and compliance partners by being clear, prepared, and decisive. You're motivated by real responsibility, welcome visibility with senior leaders, and see hard infrastructure work as the highest-leverage thing you can do.




WHAT TO EXPECT

Real autonomy over foundational infrastructure. High visibility and real accountability. You'll have direct influence over the system that determines how Dave lends, today and for every loan product that follows.




WHY JOIN DAVE

 - Mission with scale: Tangible impact for millions of members — not theoretical

 - Product at the core: Product is central to how Dave grows and wins

 - Strong partners: Collaborative teams who care about building the right thing

 - Meaningful ownership: Competitive compensation, meaningful equity in a public company (NASDAQ: DAVE), comprehensive benefits, 401(k) matching, and flexible PTO



Ready to build for the underdog?

Reports to: Senior Director, Product Management



Don’t let imposter syndrome get in the way of an incredible opportunity. We’re looking for people who can help us achieve our mission and vision, not just check off the boxes. If you’re excited about this role, we encourage you to apply. You may just be the right candidate for this or other roles.



Why you’ll love working here: 

At Dave, our people are just as important as our product. Our culture reflects the values that guide who we are, how we work, and what we aspire to be. Daves are member-centric, helpful, transparent, persistent, and better together. We strive to create an environment where all Daves feel valued, heard, and empowered to do their best work. As a virtual-first company, team members can live and work anywhere in the United States, except Hawaii. 



A few of our benefits & perks:

💚 Opportunity to tackle tough challenges, learn and grow from fellow top talent, and help millions of people reach their personal financial goals

💻 Flexible hours and virtual-first work culture with a home office stipend

🏥 Premium Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance plans

👶 Generous paid parental and caregiver leave

 💰 401(k) savings plan with matching contributions

📈 Financial advisor and financial wellness support

🏖️ Flexible PTO and generous company holidays, including Juneteenth and Winter Break

🎉 All-company in-person events once or twice a year and virtual events throughout to connect with your team members and leadership team


Dave Operating LLC is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity employer and is dedicated to cultivating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We will consider for employment all qualified applicants and do not discriminate on any basis protected by federal, state, or local law, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance relating to an applicant's criminal history.

• Turn that internal build into external proof. Case studies, joint points of view, and stage time that position Huge as the model for transformation on Google Cloud.

• Partner across Growth, Product, and the Google account team to keep the alliance strategy aligned with where Huge is headed.

What you should have

• 10+ years in alliances, partnerships, or technology consulting, with genuine depth in Google Cloud specifically and meaningful exposure to at least one other major platform ecosystem (Optimizely, Contentstack, Shopify, Anthropic).

jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineering Intern (Summer)
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

Every vehicle REGENT builds will eventually need to prove it's safe and sound to the standards of real certification — and that proof starts with the verification framework underneath it. As an Embedded Software Engineering Intern, you'll work directly in C++ and Python to help build Squire, the verification framework being developed as the test baseline for Viceroy's VCS software. You'll write test harnesses that hook directly into embedded flight control code, build out the tooling around it — generating test cases, parsing results, automating runs — and help lay groundwork for hardware-in-the-loop testing down the line. Because Squire is still taking shape, you won't be handed a fixed spec to execute; you'll be building something real while its architecture is still being defined, which means your judgment and your code both matter.

You'll sit within the Engineering & Technology team's Software Engineering group, contributing directly into the same codebase the rest of the embedded team works out of. This isn't peripheral test-writing — it's infrastructure work that will let the whole team eventually verify Viceroy's software against a certifiable standard, work that's foundational to getting SEAGLIDERS safely out of the water and into real coastal routes. You won't be expected to arrive knowing certification standards or verification framework architecture inside and out; the team will teach you that as you go. What matters is that you can write solid embedded code, build useful tooling around it, and stay comfortable figuring things out as the target evolves. If you're someone who gets energized by building the thing that makes everything else provable, you'll find real purpose in this work.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build Embedded Test Harnesses: You'll write C++ test harnesses that hook directly into Viceroy's VCS software, giving the team a real way to exercise and validate flight control code rather than just scripting around its edges.

 - Develop Verification Tooling: You'll write Python to generate test cases, parse results, and automate test runs, building out the tooling that makes Squire actually usable as a framework rather than a one-off script.

 - Design Requirements-Traceable Tests: You'll build tests that trace cleanly back to requirements, laying groundwork for a test environment that can eventually hold up against certification-grade scrutiny.

 - Contribute To A Shared Codebase: You'll commit directly into the same repository the embedded team works out of, writing clean, reviewable code that merges in rather than living off to the side.

 - Work Hands-On With Hardware: You'll work with electronic hardware, including microprocessors, as part of exercising and validating the software you're testing against.

 - Help Shape Squire As It's Built: You'll make real calls about how the framework should work as its architecture is still being defined, adapting your approach as Viceroy's design evolves alongside it.

 - Lay Groundwork For HIL Testing: You'll work toward supporting hardware-in-the-loop testing, building the pieces that will eventually let the team verify software against real hardware behavior.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Strong C++ Fundamentals: You're comfortable reading and writing embedded C++ well enough to build real test harnesses against it, not just work around the margins.

 - Practical Python Scripting: You can write solid Python to stitch together tooling — generating test cases, parsing output, automating runs — and use it to move a framework forward quickly.

 - A Requirements-Minded Approach To Testing: You understand how test design, unit testing, and traceability map back to requirements, and you think that way naturally rather than treating tests as an afterthought.

 - Comfort In A Shared Codebase: You're used to working with git and standard review workflows, writing commits and branches that are easy for a team to review and merge.

 - Hands-On Hardware Experience: You're able to work with electronic hardware, including microprocessors, as part of your day-to-day engineering work.

 - Ease With Ambiguity: You can take a rough direction, make reasonable calls, and adjust as you go, rather than waiting for a fully specified plan before you start building.

 - Bonus Experience, Not Required: Exposure to CI/CD pipelines, simulation or hardware-in-the-loop testing, or certification standards like DO-178C will help you ramp up faster, but none of it is expected on day one.
   
   


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

 - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

 - Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation

 - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team

 - Daily, free catered lunches

 - Learning & professional development opportunities

 - Meaningful projects that make an impact

 - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

Equal Opportunity Employer

REGENT is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.title: Marketing & Comms Intern (Spring Co-Op/Summer)
jobs.description:
At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.


ROLE OVERVIEW

REGENT is reinventing maritime mobility with Seagliders, and our marketing and communications is how we share that story with the world. As our Marketing team grows, we're looking for an aspiring strategic communications professional who wants to see how a brand really comes together. You'll work across the full marketing function, from shaping the assets and systems that power our storytelling to supporting the conferences and visits that put our mission in front of the world, while contributing your own content ideas along the way.

You'll sit within our Marketing & Communications team, working alongside the people who shape how REGENT shows up in the world, with a mentor guiding you as you take on real ownership from day one. You'll leave with a portfolio of content you created, tangible systems you managed, and hands-on experience in how a fast-moving company brings a new category to life. If you're someone who gets genuine satisfaction from bringing order to chaos and wants hands-on experience across the full range of marketing operations, we'd love to meet you.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own Our Marketing Asset Inventory: You'll keep track of the materials that represent REGENT in the field, from conference displays to SWAG, so the team always knows what we have and where it is.

 - Manage Our Photo and Video Library: You'll create a consistent naming and tagging system in our digital asset management tool, making it easy for the whole team to find and use the content that tells our story.

 - Support Conferences and Visits: You'll help coordinate logistics for conferences and visits, getting an inside look at how REGENT shows up in front of customers and partners.

 - Contribute to Content Across Channels: You'll bring your ideas and creativity to content for our website, social media, and beyond, from drafting posts to capturing photos and video.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - Meticulous Organization: You have a natural eye for detail and consistency, which will keep inventories, file names, and asset libraries clean and easy to navigate.

 - Clear, Proactive Communication: You collaborate well with others and keep people in the loop without needing to be asked, sharing updates as a matter of habit.

 - Strong Time Management: You can juggle multiple projects and deadlines at once, moving fluidly between operational work and creative contributions.

 - Creativity and Initiative: You bring fresh ideas to the table and aren't afraid to pitch content concepts or suggest better ways of doing things.

 - Comfort With Digital Tools: Experience with digital asset management and website platform is a plus, though we'll teach you our specific systems.

 - A Creative Toolkit: Basic writing, social media, or photo and video editing skills are a welcome bonus.
   
   


WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

 - Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

 - Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

 - Innovative Mindset: You're driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You're passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive compensation

 - Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team

 - Daily, free catered lunches

 - Learning & professional development opportunities

 - Meaningful projects that make an impact

 - Mentorship & guidance from experienced team members

If you’re ready to take on an exciting challenge, grow with us, and make a lasting impact, we want to hear from you. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, but you see yourself contributing to our mission, we encourage you to apply! We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

jobs.title: Manager, Signage
jobs.description:
LA28 does not provide relocation assistance for any positions. If you are based outside the Los Angeles area, we still welcome your application — we value talent from all geographic backgrounds and want to hear from you if you are able to work on-site in LA.

Role Purpose

You will build the wayfinding and signage plan for your venue cluster from the ground up, shaping how spectators, athletes and workforce move through every competition and non-competition venue. As Manager, Signage, you will scope requirements, create dot plans and artworks, and guide contractors and cluster venue managers through planning, installation, Games-time operations and de-rig. Working with Venue Management, Functional Area leads, city authorities and transport partners, you will keep every sign accurate, on brand and ready for each sport configuration.

Key Responsibilities

· Scope wayfinding and Functional Area signage requirements for competition and non-competition venues across your cluster.

· Develop signage dot plans and artworks in approved software, aligned with brand and terminology standards.

· Validate sign locations on venue site visits with Venue Management, Functional Area leads, contractors and transport partners.

· Direct contractors and cluster venue managers on specifications, permits, installation and de-rig against readiness milestones.

· Lead Games-time signage operations, managing sport transitions, escalations and wayfinding adjustments for a seamless spectator journey.

Required Competencies

· 5+ years of experience in wayfinding and signage planning, or in signage delivery for major games or tournaments.

· Familiarity with signage artwork production, signage scoping and signage-specific software across multiple venues.

· Strong project management skills, balancing multiple venues, sports and competing priorities against tight deadlines and changing requirements.

· Strong understanding of venue operations, spatial planning and spectator movement from Olympic and Paralympic Games or large global sporting events.

· Excellent communication and coordination skills with venue teams, functional areas, contractors and public agencies in a multi-venue, multi-stakeholder environment.

Valued Experience

· ADA accessibility training or certification in signage and environmental design.

· Multi-venue or multi-sport operations at major international events.

· Experience within an event organising committee or venue team.

· Coordinating with transport operators and city authorities on wayfinding.

· Signage planning, asset management or wayfinding software experience.

What We Offer

· A historic opportunity to guide millions of visitors through the LA28 Games.

· Visible ownership of the signage every spectator, athlete and partner will follow.

· Broad exposure to venue, transport, brand and operations teams across the Games.

· Teammates who share optimism, excellence, co-creation and pride in Los Angeles.

What This Role Means for the Games

Clear signage is the first thing a visitor relies on. Your plans will help spectators, athletes and workforce move confidently between transport hubs and venues, turning complex multi-sport sites into a welcoming Olympic and Paralympic experience.

Physical Requirements & Working Conditions

· Available to work onsite in our Downtown Los Angeles-based office.

· The majority of work will be conducted in an office setting, requiring extended periods of time using computers, phones, and other office equipment.

· The LA28 office is an open floorplan working environment; employees must be able to work efficiently in an open cubicle environment.

· Hours of work may vary, including evenings, weekends, and holidays, especially during peak event periods.

· Perform other duties as required; the role will evolve over time and may include operational responsibilities during the Olympic and Paralympic Games.

· Increasing on-site work at venues as the Games approach, through installation, Games-time operations, sport transitions and de-rig, with local and regional travel.

· Comfortable navigating construction areas, multi-level venues, outdoor conditions, long walking distances and crowds.

Compensation

The annual base salary range for this position is $88,000 - $115,000. The pay scale provided is the range that LA28 reasonably expects to pay as starting base compensation for this role. All LA28 compensation remains subject to final determination based on individual candidate qualifications, experience, or other reasonable criteria consistent with LA28's operational business needs and applicable law.

LA28 is an equal opportunity employer. To read our full Equal Opportunity and Accommodation statements, please visit LA28 Careers Page.

jobs.title: Senior Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.



We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.



We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.



If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.



About This Role:

We are seeking a Software Engineer to join Crusoe’s Hardware Systems Engineering team and build the tools, automation, and data platforms that let our hardware engineers debug, validate, and support high-performance compute systems at scale. In this role, you will own the software that supports the full hardware lifecycle, from prototype bring-up through large-scale production, accelerating issue resolution and improving reliability across Crusoe Cloud’s GPU- and CPU-based infrastructure.

You will work closely with hardware engineers to understand their debugging and validation workflows, then turn them into automatable workflows. You will also work with cross-functional teams to integrate tools with the production environment. A particular focus will be provisioning, hardware health monitoring, test framework, and data collection. Your work will directly improve Crusoe’s ability to deploy and operate sustainable, AI-first compute systems with world-class performance and reliability.



What You’ll Be Working On:

 - Design, build, and maintain software tools and frameworks that support the hardware development and sustaining lifecycle, including bring-up, validation, deployment, and ongoing production support.

 - Develop automated test, diagnostics, and health-monitoring frameworks that run across fleets of servers, enabling continuous reliability improvements.

 - Build tooling, monitoring and logging systems that help hardware engineers triage and root-cause issues across different hardware platforms.

 - Create automated validation and characterization workflows for GPU, CPU, and high-performance compute platforms, including result collection, analysis, and reporting.

 - Build and operate data pipelines, dashboards, and analytics that surface hardware failure trends, performance regressions, and reliability metrics.

 - Support E2E integration and solution testing by developing test harnesses and CI/CD workflows that ensure Crusoe Cloud products meet performance, reliability, and scalability expectations.

 - Evaluate and introduce new tools, testing methods, and automation approaches that improve engineering efficiency and support Crusoe’s sustainability goals.

 - Provide data-driven insights from tooling and telemetry to influence Crusoe’s hardware roadmap and reliability strategy.



What You’ll Bring to the Team:

 - 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, ideally building internal tools, infrastructure software, provisioning, test automation, or systems software.

 - Strong proficiency in Python and at least one systems language (Go, C/C++, or Rust), plus Shell scripting.

 - Experience designing and implementing automation and test frameworks, including workflow engines, for hardware or large-scale infrastructure.

jobs.title: Marketing and Communications Manager
jobs.description:
Marketing and Communications Manager

Location: Remote, US Based, EST
Employment Type: Full-time

About the Role

Over the past year, Underscore has built the foundation for a stronger marketing and new business engine, including a refreshed brand and positioning, a redesigned website, a defined ideal client profile, HubSpot infrastructure, an earned media program, and a growing portfolio of events and experiences designed to connect us with leaders across biopharma.

Now we’re looking for a Marketing and Communications Manager who can execute on that foundation to deliver a consistent, high-performing marketing and communications program.

The Marketing and Communications Manager will own the day-to-day execution of Underscore’s efforts across content, thought leadership, case studies, digital marketing, events, PR, sales enablement, and internal communications. This person will work closely with our leadership, subject matter experts, Sales Enablement, and external marketing and PR partners to make sure great ideas become great content and, ultimately, business opportunities.

This role will also help shape experiences. This includes our Rare Company Dinner series, which will be held at least four times in 2027. The manager will work on invitations, follow-ups, venue management, and ensuring we deliver premium, valuable experiences for senior leaders in biopharma.

Internally, this person will help lead the communications that keep our people informed, connected, and engaged. This includes managing our monthly Town Halls and maintaining our online communication hub.

This is a hands-on role for someone who is equally comfortable developing a content calendar, interviewing a media expert for a case study, building a HubSpot campaign, preparing a Town Hall, supporting an industry event, and looking at performance data to determine what we should do next.

What You’ll Do

Content & Thought Leadership

• Own and execute Underscore’s editorial calendar across the website, LinkedIn, email, and other marketing channels.

• Develop and manage the Rare Company newsletter, creating relevant and compelling content for biopharma leaders and prospective clients. The source of this information will be Underscore’s subject matter experts. The Marketing and Communications Manager will shape the story and language.

• Turn the expertise that already exists across Underscore into compelling content, including conference takeaways, partner insights, industry perspectives, media and analytics thought leadership, and emerging trends.

• Maintain Underscore’s voice and strengthen our position in the healthcare and biopharma marketplace.

• Keep the Underscore website current with new team members, company news, events, awards, thought leadership, and other relevant updates.

• Route leads that come through the site for our Rare Company Dinners, as well as general leads, to the right resources for follow-up. The approach and executional requirements will be outlined in our 2027 plan.

Internal Communications & Company Meetings

• Own the planning and execution of Underscore’s monthly Town Halls, partnering with leadership to shape agendas, gather content, coordinate presentations and speakers, and ensure employees hear the information that matters most.

• Partner with leaders across the company to translate company updates, milestones, and organizational news into communications that are clear, engaging, and relevant to employees.

• Help create a consistent internal communications cadence so employees understand what is happening across Underscore, where the company is going, and how their work connects to it.

• Bring the same storytelling, clarity, and attention to Underscore’s internal communications that we bring to our external brand.

Case Studies & Credentials

• Build and maintain a strong library of Underscore case studies, with a goal of developing approximately two new case studies per quarter.

• Partner with account leads, media teams, analytics, and other subject matter experts to identify compelling stories and results.

• Own the case study process from beginning to end, including interviews, results gathering, writing, internal review, client approval, publishing, and inclusion in the sales library.

• Navigate client confidentiality and healthcare industry requirements to develop compelling blinded case studies when necessary.

• Ensure our capabilities decks, credentials, team bios, case studies, RFP content, and other sales materials remain current and easy to access.

HubSpot & Sales Enablement

• Serve as a day-to-day marketing partner to Sales Enablement and the broader growth team.

• Support marketing activity within HubSpot, including getting content to fuel custom messages designed to engage the client and get a conversation going.

• Deliver tailored communications and content strategies for different prospect audiences and stages of the new business journey. This will be structured by audience so we can test and learn what works and what doesn’t.

• Maintain a consistent cadence for timely lead follow-up following conferences, events, campaigns, and other business development activities. These standards will be agreed upon as part of our 2027 plan.

• Participate in the preparation of monthly reporting that gives leadership visibility into pipeline sources, campaign performance, content engagement, and marketing effectiveness.

PR & Awards

• Support Underscore’s external PR agency by providing company information, executive bios, subject matter expertise, quotes, images, approvals, and other materials needed to support earned media.

• Own the annual awards calendar and coordinate submissions from initial opportunity through final deadline.

• Help execute and continuously improve the playbook for major industry moments such as Fierce Pharma Week.

What We’re Looking For

Required

• 4–6 years of B2B marketing agency experience, ideally with at least three years working in or with healthcare, biopharma, pharmaceutical companies, or healthcare agencies.

• Exceptional writing and editing skills. You can interview a subject matter expert and turn the conversation into content that a senior biopharma marketer would genuinely want to read.

• Strong understanding of HubSpot, including best practices for relationship management.

• Demonstrated experience owning and consistently executing against an editorial or content calendar.

• Strong project management skills, with the ability to move multiple initiatives from idea to execution without losing momentum.

• Comfortable working directly with senior leaders and subject matter experts to turn their expertise into accessible, differentiated content.

• A strong sense of ownership and follow-through. You see something that needs to get done and know how to move it forward.

• Strong PowerPoint skills required.

Preferred

• Internal communications experience is a plus.

• Agency experience, particularly within media, digital marketing, healthcare communications, or a related environment.

• Experience developing pharmaceutical or healthcare case studies and navigating client legal, regulatory, or confidentiality requirements.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first year, success in this role will mean:

• Underscore has a consistent editorial calendar that is being executed across channels.

• The Rare Company newsletter has become a recognizable and valuable communication for our target audience.

• New case studies are being developed and added to our credentials library each quarter.

• Leads from events, campaigns, and other marketing activity have clear ownership and timely follow-up.

• The website and sales enablement materials remain current rather than being updated reactively.

• Strong ideas and insights from across Underscore are consistently turned into useful, market-facing content.

• Leadership has clear monthly visibility into marketing activity, engagement, lead sources, and pipeline contribution.

• Monthly Town Halls are thoughtfully planned and executed, with clear, relevant content that helps employees understand what is happening across the company.

Who Will Thrive Here

You’re a doer.

You like taking something from idea to finished product. You know how to pull a good story out of people who may not think of themselves as storytellers. You care about the quality of the writing, but you also care whether someone opened it, responded to it, understood it, or wanted to have a conversation because of it.

You understand that good communication matters on both sides of the company. You can help tell Underscore’s story to the market while also helping our people understand where we’re going, what matters, and how they are part of it.

You’re comfortable working in an environment where there are plenty of ideas and opportunities, and part of your value is bringing the structure, discipline, and follow-through that turns those ideas into a real marketing and communications program.

At Underscore, you’ll have access to deep expertise across media, analytics, strategy, and healthcare. Your job is to help make sure both our people and the market see it.

Interested?
Apply by submitting your resume and a brief note outlining your healthcare or media experience.

Underscore Marketing is a woman-owned, independent agency specializing in life sciences. Since 2002, we've helped clients gain a competitive edge through bold, data-driven promotional strategies that deliver measurable results.

Our team comprises media, strategy, and omnichannel analytics experts who thrive on collaboration, innovation, and results. When you join Underscore, you become part of a dynamic environment where your ideas matter, your growth is supported, and your work helps elevate brands in a competitive healthcare landscape.

If you're passionate about making a difference and want to be part of a team that values integrity, creativity, and results, if that sounds like you, we invite you to share.

Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Underscore is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We believe that diversity drives innovation and success, and we welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.title: Senior Optical Systems Validation Engineer - Optical Circuit Switch (OCS)
jobs.description:
PsiQuantum's mission is to build the first useful quantum computers: machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries.

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry, including partners like GlobalFoundries, we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don't feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.

That approach has since been tested at the highest level of scrutiny the U.S. government applies to emerging technology, and it has held up. In 2025, PsiQuantum closed a $1 billion funding round that valued the company at $7 billion. In 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce signed a $100 million Letter of Intent under the CHIPS and Science Act, followed by a $125 million agreement with DARPA under Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, PsiQuantum's most valuable U.S. government agreement to date. This year, we also broke ground on our utility-scale quantum computer in Brisbane, Australia, and continued building out our Chicago site. Victor Peng, our CEO, and co-founder Jeremy O'Brien, now Executive Chairman, lead a team and board that reflects how seriously the world is taking this build, joined this year by Intel's Lip-Bu Tan and Atomico's Niklas Zennström.

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies, including Airbus, Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical, to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact.

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift, and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we now have the funding, the government validation, and the sites under construction to make it real.

Job Summary:

We are seeking a Senior Optical Systems Validation Engineer to lead the validation of optical switching technology in representative data-center communication systems.

Working closely with photonics, hardware, firmware, and systems engineering, you will own the bring-up of optical link and bit-error-rate setups, define validation plans, and quantify performance under customer-relevant operating conditions. Your work will provide the evidence needed for product readiness, design decisions, and customer demonstrations, and help establish the team’s test capabilities, qualification methods, and technical approach to optical link validation.

This is a hands-on technical role for an engineer with relevant experience and a track record of independently building and debugging communication test systems.

Responsibilities:

• Translate customer requirements into optical link validation plans, including test configurations, coverage, operating conditions, acceptance criteria, and appropriate test durations.

• Select, bring up, and automate test setups using BER equipment, optical transceivers, evaluation platforms, and relevant communication endpoints.

• Build representative link configurations based on intended customer architectures, including relevant scale-up and scale-out applications.

• Measure link error performance and remaining optical power margin under steady-state and dynamic operating conditions, comparing reference links with links incorporating our switching subsystems.

• Investigate link failures and performance limitations, distinguish subsystem effects from transceiver, electrical-interface, firmware, and test-setup behavior, and coordinate investigations with the relevant engineering teams.

• Develop repeatable demonstrations and produce clear reports describing measured performance, limitations, and readiness for customer evaluation.

Experience/Qualifications:

• Degree in Electrical Engineering, Photonics, Physics, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

• Relevant experience (5+ years preferred) in high-speed optical communications or interconnect validation, including independent ownership of hardware bring-up and qualification.

• Hands-on experience building and debugging optical link test setups using BER equipment, optical transceivers, and relevant optical or high-speed electrical instrumentation.

• Understanding of optical link budgets, receiver sensitivity, high-speed modulation, receiver synchronization, equalization, and forward error correction.

• Proficiency in Python or a comparable language for instrument control, test automation, and data analysis.

• Ability to translate link requirements into measurable, reproducible tests, critically interpret results, and communicate findings across engineering teams.

Preferred qualifications

• Experience validating optical switching systems or data-center optical interconnects.

• Experience with transient measurements, receiver synchronization, or link recovery testing.

• Experience with Ethernet, InfiniBand, or other relevant high-speed interconnect interfaces.

• Experience building network testbeds and using traffic generators to measure throughput, latency, and packet loss.

• Experience supporting customer evaluations or reproducing integration issues in the laboratory.

jobs.title: Analytics Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
About Us

Health is the most important thing in life, and the American healthcare system is completely broken - poor outcomes, high cost, bad patient experience. We're building a new system from the ground up.

Our mission is to improve people’s health by making it easy to live a healthy lifestyle.

Nourish is the country's largest dietitian-led metabolic health clinic. We’re an AI-native digital health system matching patients with 10,000+ Registered Dietitians, physicians, medications, lab testing, and AI agents to deliver insurance-covered care across all 50 states. Founded four years ago, we've completed millions of appointments, tripled year-over-year, and partnered with health plans covering 200M+ Americans across 250+ health systems.

In 2026 we raised a $100M Series C, bringing total funding to $215M. The round was led by Menlo Ventures, with participation from Thrive Capital, Index Ventures, J.P. Morgan Growth Equity Partners, Maverick Ventures, Y Combinator, BoxGroup, Atomico, Daybreak, and Operator Partners.

Learn more about our Series C here: Nourish Blog, Bloomberg, Fierce Healthcare, Digital Native, The Pulse Podcast.

This is not a job for everyone. We hold an extremely high bar because we believe talent density is our biggest competitive advantage. We're looking for people who actively choose hard, ambiguous problems, who run toward unglamorous work, give and receive candid feedback, and bring relentless resilience without the ego. Our work is important, but we are not self-important. We do this because we’re solving one of the hardest problems in the world, and the problem matters. If that's you, we disproportionately reward it.

About the Role

We're scaling quickly, and data is a critical lever to growing our business and improving patient outcomes. As Manager, Analytics Engineering you'll lead the strategy and execution of a team of analytics engineers working across a multitude of domains, partner with leadership on critical business questions, and drive the vision for the future of Analytics at Nourish.

This role combines analytics engineering, business insights, and people management to support domains ranging from supply and demand to marketing, and operations. You'll work closely with Operations, Engineering, and Product to build reliable data foundations and help teams answer their most important questions. You'll define and execute Nourish's analytics roadmap alongside other Data leads.

Our Data team is based in NYC and goes into the office 2-3 days a week. While this isn't a strict requirement, we are looking for people who would be excited to be part of that culture.

Key Responsibilities:

• Lead and develop a team of Analytics Engineers: lead planning and prioritization; provide technical and analytical guidance; hold the bar on execution; help hire new team members.

• Define and deliver the analytics roadmap across data modeling, business intelligence, and AI-enabled analytics. Establish technical standards that help the team scale.

• Deliver high-impact insights: lead analyses of ambiguous problems; proactively identify opportunities; partner with leadership on solving complex and impactful analytics questions.

• Build and maintain a robust data foundation: Partner with Engineering to validate and optimize pipelines, ensuring our data infrastructure is accurate, scalable, and supports a trusted single source of truth.

• Champion a data-first culture: Guide teams to interpret and act on data, write clear documentation, and lead by example in driving evidence-based decisions.

We’d love to hear from you if:

• Have 5+ years of relevant experience owning analytics end to end at a fast-paced, high-growth company.

• Have 2+ years of leadership experience leading not only your team day to to day, but also setting and driving the technical vision to support business growth.

• Are an unstoppable problem-solver taking complex and highly ambiguous asks and turning them into structured and thoughtful roadmaps to be rolled out to a lean team.

• Have deep domain expertise in analytics engineering: You write clean, performant SQL, have hands-on experience with tools like dbt and Fivetran, and have a strong grasp of the fundamentals of data modeling, ETLs, and infrastructure.

• Are curious, strategic, and outcome-oriented: You proactively shape the right questions, translate complex data into clear, actionable insights, and balance speed with depth to drive clear, high-impact decisions across the business

• Are a builder who thrives on ownership and impact: You take pride in designing clean, scalable systems from scratch, and are excited to take end-to-end ownership - filling gaps, creating structure, and becoming the go-to person others rely on for clarity.

• Communicate complex ideas with clarity: You distill deep analysis into crisp, actionable takeaways, whether writing a Notion doc or presenting to leadership, and you earn trust across cross-functional teams by speaking the language of both operations and engineering

• Are motivated by impact and mission: You believe in the power of food as medicine to transform healthcare and are excited to improve lives at scale by contributing to Nourish’s mission.

You will design, develop, and manage cloud infrastructure using Terraform, build and maintain GitLab CI/CD pipelines, and deploy and support Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) environments that enable reliable and secure mission operations. Working as part of a small, experienced technical team, you will collaborate directly with federal stakeholders to identify opportunities for improvement, implement scalable cloud solutions, and strengthen platform performance, security, and reliability. This position requires working onsite at the customer’s location in Washington, DC, four days per week, providing opportunities for direct customer engagement and collaboration. This is a hands-on role where your technical expertise, initiative, and ability to deliver practical solutions will have a direct impact on mission success.

We know that you can’t have great technology services without amazing people. At MetroStar, we are obsessed with our people and have led a two-decade legacy of building the best and brightest teams. Because we know our future relies on our deep understanding and relentless focus on our people, we live by our mission: A passion for our people. Value for our customers.

If you think you can see yourself delivering our mission and pursuing our goals with us, then check out the job description below!

What you’ll do:

• You will be responsible for the day-to-day operation, maintenance, and modernization of Microsoft Azure infrastructure supporting a mission-critical federal program.

• You will design, deploy, and manage cloud resources, including virtual machines, networking, storage, identity services, and platform services, while developing and maintaining Terraform infrastructure as code and GitLab CI/CD pipelines to automate provisioning, configuration, and deployments.

• You will administer and optimize Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD) environments, including host pools, session hosts, FSLogix profiles, and Microsoft 365 integrations, ensuring reliable performance and availability for mission users.

• Your daily responsibilities will include troubleshooting infrastructure and connectivity issues, monitoring system health using Azure Monitor and Log Analytics, implementing automation through PowerShell and Bash scripting, and maintaining secure cloud operations aligned with NIST, RMF, FedRAMP, and agency-specific requirements.

• Working directly with engineering, cybersecurity, and program stakeholders, you will identify opportunities for improvement, resolve technical challenges, and deliver secure, scalable, and reliable cloud solutions that improve operational efficiency and support evolving mission requirements.

What you’ll need to succeed:

• Active Secret clearance with the ability to obtain an Interim Top Secret clearance.

• 3+ years in cloud engineering, DevOps, or systems engineering, with substantial hands-on Azure work.

• Demonstrated depth with Microsoft Azure core services and architecture — you've implemented and run real environments, not just studied for the cert.

• Strong familiarization with Terraform. This is the one we weight most heavily.

• PowerShell scripting ability for automation and system configuration.

• Working experience troubleshooting CI/CD pipelines in GitLab.

• Hands-on experience with Azure Virtual Desktop in a production environment — host pools, session hosts, and FSLogix.

• Experience supporting Azure networking: VNets, routing, NSGs, and VPN/ExpressRoute.

• Familiarity with federal cloud security frameworks such as FedRAMP, NIST, and RMF.

• Have troubleshooting instincts and the communication skills to explain your reasoning to engineers and non-engineers alike.

• Ability to work onsite in downtown Washington, DC four days per week.

SALARY RANGE: $110,000 - $140,000

The salary range for this position is determined based on qualifications, skills, and relevant experience. The final salary offered will be determined based on several factors including:

• The candidate's professional background and relevant work experience

• The specific responsibilities of the role and organizational needs

• Internal equity and alignment with current team compensation

• This role is also eligible for additional compensation, subject to the terms and policies of MetroStar, which may include:

• Performance-based bonuses

jobs.title: Wastewater Treatment Plant Operator
jobs.description:
Coho Technology Solutions is seeking a Wastewater Treatment Plant Operator that will be responsible for the safe, efficient, and compliant operation of a multi-stage wastewater treatment facility in accordance with National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) permit requirements. This position supports continuous plant operations by monitoring processes, operating treatment equipment, performing sampling and testing, adjusting chemical treatment, responding to alarms, and conducting routine operator-level maintenance. The operator will work rotating shifts in coordination with government personnel to ensure uninterrupted wastewater treatment operations.

Location: Mainside Wastewater Treatment Plant, Quantico, VA
Schedule: 12 hour rotating shifts (days/nights, weekends, holidays)

Responsibilities:

• Operate and monitor a wastewater treatment plant providing pretreatment, primary, secondary, and tertiary treatment in compliance with NPDES permit conditions.

• Operate pumps, valves, gates, feeders, flocculators, clarifiers, filters, UV disinfection systems, and related process control equipment.

• Collect influent, intermediate, and effluent samples; perform required testing and analysis (e.g., pH, temperature, settleable solids, flow rates).

• Adjust chemical feed rates and treatment processes based on test results and operational requirements.

• Perform tertiary treatment operations, including chemical mixing, polymer and chemical feed systems, gravity sand filtration, phosphorus and nitrogen removal, and UV disinfection.

• Respond to plant alarms and telemetry notifications; investigate issues and take corrective actions as needed.

• Make operational decisions during assigned shifts, including serving as Operator in Charge when required and determining appropriate actions during abnormal or emergency conditions.

• Operate sludge handling and disposal equipment such as centrifuges, vacuum coil filters, or belt filter presses.

• Perform operator-level preventive maintenance, including lubrication, minor repairs, adjustments, and calibration of equipment in accordance with SOPs, TPMs, and manufacturer manuals.

• Maintain accurate logs, records, flow charts, calibration records, and operational documentation.

• Work under the general direction of the Wastewater Treatment Plant Supervisor while exercising independent judgment within established procedures.

• Support continuous shift coverage and work mandatory overtime when required.

Requirements:

Experience

• Experience operating a wastewater treatment plant with multiple stages of treatment, including tertiary processes.

• Hands-on experience with wastewater treatment equipment, chemical treatment systems, and process monitoring.

• Experience working rotating shifts in a continuous operations environment preferred.

Skills and Knowledge

• Proficiency in the operation, purpose, and capabilities of wastewater treatment equipment and systems.

• Knowledge of safe handling and application of wastewater treatment chemicals, including sulfuric acid, sulfur dioxide, aluminum sulfate, ferric chloride, polymers, sodium hydroxide, lime, and related compounds.

• Knowledge of tertiary wastewater treatment processes, chlorination and dechlorination, and nutrient (phosphorus and nitrogen) removal.

• Understanding of ultraviolet (UV) disinfection system operation and maintenance.

• Ability to read and interpret digital and analog gauges, meters, and alarms.

• Ability to read, interpret, and apply technical manuals, SOPs, and regulatory documentation.

• Strong written and verbal communication skills.

• Basic computer proficiency, including use of Windows-based systems and operational software.

Education and Certification

• Must possess and maintain a Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation (DPOR) Wastewater Treatment Plant Operator Certification, Class I or Class II.

• High school diploma or equivalent required.

• Technical or vocational training in wastewater treatment or a related field preferred.

Physical Requirements

• Ability to safely wear all required personal protective equipment, including respiratory protection.

• Ability to perform physical tasks including prolonged standing and walking, climbing ladders and stairs, and lifting objects weighing up to 45–50 pounds (occasionally more).

• Ability to work rotating shifts, including nights, weekends, holidays, and overtime as required.

Compensation range: $50 - $54 per hour.

jobs.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

About the role:

We are looking for interns for the Winter 2027 Season. You will contribute to the development and optimization of Skydio's embedded hardware in the loop (HIL) system. Including the Python test framework, its CI integration, the fleet of physical test stations, and the devices on them. You'll help guide its technical direction, keep it reliable as the number of products and tests grows, and make it easy for other teams to add tests.

An ideal intern candidate is a junior, senior, or MS-level college student with industry experience developing test infrastructure with familiarity of device-level embedded software or firmware.

About the team:

The Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) team is responsible for the development and maintenance of HIL infrastructure. This ranges from cloud infrastructure for continuous integration (CI) validation, internal tooling for developer use, as well as development with the physical hardware products Skydio builds; from drones and docks to radios and accessories. We work closely with both the hardware team and the rest of the software organization, creating the foundation for the rest of the Skydio software teams to build upon.

 - We work closely with both the hardware team and the rest of the software organization, to bridge the gap between software development and hardware validation.

How you'll make an impact:

 - Contribute to the architecture and roadmap of the HIL test framework and its integration with CI

 - Design and build new test stations and fixtures and bring new products onto the HIL

 - Partner with firmware, platform and product teams to turn their validation needs into reliable automated tests

 - Develop new critical use cases to expand hardware validation and development to more broad teams

 - Triage failing runs, separate infrastructure problems from product regressions, and route real bugs to the right team

What makes you a good fit:

 - Strong Python, with clean, well-tested code and sensible abstraction boundaries

 - Software engineering experience, including building or owning test or CI infrastructure

 - Solid Linux systems skills: networking, USB/udev, systemd, Docker, shell

 - Hands-on embedded Linux experience: flashing, bootloaders and recovery modes, serial consoles, debugging boards that don't boot

 - Clear communicator who can support many engineering teams

 - Experience / interest in hardware bring-up and system debugging

 - Obtaining FAA Part 107 certification within the first 60 days of employment is strongly encouraged for all Skydio employees and required for certain positions.
   
   Compensation: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Graduate students, and $70/hr for PhD students*. Interns are eligible to receive the following benefits: Paid vacation time, sick leave, holiday pay and 401K savings plan. jobs.title: Sales Strategy and Operations | Channel Programs Specialist
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation, more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries.

Overview

Verkada is a 100% channel-driven business. Our partners are foundational to our growth strategy and to delivering exceptional customer experiences. As Verkada continues to scale, we are launching a new Partner Program to deepen our alignment with our most strategic partners.  In this role, you will be part of the team responsible for ensuring the success of our Partner Program while driving operational and process improvement initiatives.

Additionally, as a member of Sales Strategy and Operations, you’ll be part of the team at the nexus of strategic decision-making in Verkada’s 1,000-person sales organization. You will have an integral role in driving the insights and operations that enable Sales to run better, faster, and smarter.

Responsibilities

• Ensure the integrity of our partner-sourced business. One of the key ways our partners enhance our growth is through Deal Registration - leads that our partners bring to us. In your role as Channel Programs Specialist, you will own the audit and compliance function for our Deal Registration process, ensuring that our partner-sourced business is a reliable source of revenue for Verkada.

• Support ongoing data accuracy and cleanliness. Own our Deal Registration process from a data accuracy standpoint and run point on all data integrity efforts including data audits, recategorizations, and backfills. Work closely with the Channel Operations team to measure partner compliance with our Partner Program membership criteria, including tracking of all key performance indicators.

• Collect and analyze data on our Channel organization. Run ad-hoc reporting and analyses to understand trends in our Channel business. Prepare summary presentations for Sales Operations and Channel leadership.

• Implement and reinforce Channel policies. Partner closely with our Channel leadership team to implement policies that enhance growth and scalability of our Channel organization and execute policy compliance.

• Design and implement streamlined operations processes. Partner with Verkada’s Channel Operations team and developers to configure, test, and implement new workflows that integrate critical Channel data into our CRM and Partner Portal.

Requirements

• Ability to work in a fast paced, often-changing environment.

• Outstanding interpersonal skills. You work well on teams and are comfortable speaking with stakeholders of all backgrounds.

• Extreme attention to detail.

• Excellent organizational skills with an ability to tackle large volumes of data review with efficiency and accuracy.

• Experience building out future-proof processes, procedures, and workflows.

• Exceptional written, presentation, and verbal communication skills.

• Strong Excel skills with experience using formulas (lookups, index match, countifs, sumifs, etc.) Google Sheets experience is a plus.

• 1-3 years of professional experience in a quantitative role such as accounting, tax, or audit. Bachelors in Accounting, Business, Economics, Finance, or other quantitative fields preferred.

US Employee Benefits

Verkada is committed to fostering a workplace environment that prioritizes the holistic health and wellbeing of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive wellness perks, benefits, and resources. Our benefits and perks programs include, but are not limited to:

With that in mind, we carefully consider a number of factors to determine the appropriate starting pay for an employee, including their primary work location and an assessment of a candidate's skills and experience, as well as market demands and internal parity.
