jobs.description:
HPC/GPU DATA CENTER NETWORK ENGINEER 
- MEMBER OF TECHNICAL STAFF

Location: Hybrid | Bellevue, WA Area
Multiple Levels and Roles available



BUILD THE NETWORK FOUNDATION FOR NEXT-GENERATION AI INFRASTRUCTURE



ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

A well-funded, rapidly growing AI infrastructure company is building a next-generation cloud platform designed to power the full lifecycle of artificial intelligence. The organization is developing a comprehensive AI infrastructure, platform, and services portfolio that supports the full spectrum of AI workloads, including large-scale compute, model training, fine-tuning, inference, and emerging agentic AI applications.



Backed by significant long-term investment, the company combines the speed, ownership, and innovation of a startup with the stability and resources of an established parent organization. Engineering teams are intentionally lean, highly collaborative, and AI-native, leveraging modern automation and tooling to build world-class infrastructure capable of supporting the industry's most demanding AI workloads.



We're seeking a Principal Data Center Network Engineer to architect and build the networking foundation for a multi-tenant AI cloud platform. This is a greenfield opportunity to define the network architecture supporting GPU clusters, tenant isolation, security, and high-performance connectivity across next-generation AI infrastructure.

 
 


THE OPPORTUNITY

As one of the earliest networking engineers on the infrastructure team, you'll own the design, automation, and evolution of the data center network that powers a rapidly expanding AI platform. You'll work across a multi-vendor networking environment, partnering closely with infrastructure, hardware, platform, and cloud engineering teams to deliver secure, resilient, and high-performance networking at scale.



This is a highly visible Principal-level individual contributor role offering significant technical ownership and influence over the long-term networking strategy of the organization.

 
 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design, build, automate, and operate data center networking supporting large-scale GPU clusters, AI workloads, and multi-tenant cloud services.

 - Develop secure tenant isolation architectures that ensure performance, scalability, and security across customer environments.

 - Design resilient, highly available network architectures across compute, storage, and infrastructure services.

 - Work across multiple networking platforms and vendors, including technologies from Arista, Juniper, HPE, and other enterprise networking providers.

 - Partner closely with hardware, infrastructure, virtualization, and platform engineering teams to optimize networking for AI training and inference workloads.

 - Build infrastructure automation to simplify deployment, configuration management, monitoring, and operational excellence.

 - Define networking standards, architecture documentation, and engineering best practices as the infrastructure organization grows.

 - Evaluate emerging networking technologies and help shape the long-term evolution of the company's AI networking platform.

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Significant experience designing, deploying, and operating large-scale data center networks within hyperscale cloud, AI infrastructure, HPC, or enterprise environments.

 - Deep expertise across multiple enterprise networking platforms, with demonstrated experience supporting at least two major vendors such as Arista, Juniper, HPE, Cisco, or equivalent technologies.

 - Strong understanding of multi-tenant networking, segmentation, tenant isolation, and network security architecture.

 - Experience designing highly available, scalable, and automated networking solutions supporting mission-critical production environments.

 - Strong automation mindset with experience implementing Infrastructure as Code, network automation, or programmable networking.

 - Ability to operate independently in a fast-paced, early-stage environment where architecture, standards, and processes are being built from the ground up.

 


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

jobs.title: Fulfillment Planning Analyst
jobs.description:
Fulfillment Planning Analyst

About Carvana
At Carvana, we’re changing the way people buy and sell cars. With an ambitious vision and a fundamentally different approach designed to be fun, fast, and fair, Carvana became the fastest-growing automotive retailer in history. We expanded nationally, went public on the New York Stock Exchange, sold our 1 millionth car, and reached the Fortune 500, all in just eight years.

Today, with 4 million retail customers and counting, Carvana is both the fastest-growing and the most profitable public automotive retailer, and we’re just getting started. We continue to raise the bar for our customers as we tackle the enormous opportunity still ahead in the largest consumer vertical.

Working here means being part of a team that embraces change, celebrates creative problem solving, and always strives to be better. At Carvana, you’ll have the opportunity to take on meaningful challenges, learn quickly, and help shape the future of automotive retail. If you’re driven to grow and make an impact as part of a collaborative team, you’ll fit right in. Learn more about what it’s like to work here from the people that already do.

About the team and position
This is an individual contributor position in Fulfillment Strategy & Analytics. The analyst plans and optimizes Carvana's middle-mile network: the movement of vehicles between inspection centers, logistics hubs, and last-mile markets. You will forecast vehicle flow and capacity, evaluate routing and operational changes, and deliver frequency plans to labor schedulers.

This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

This is a fully on-site position, Monday through Friday, at our corporate HQ in Tempe, Arizona.

What you’ll be doing

• Build demand forecasts and frequency plans for the middle-mile logistics network.

• Combine sales demand, trip execution, site capacity and headcount data to forecast network volume and capacity.

• Update forecasts and demand models as actual results, capacity changes and demand constraints come in.

• Evaluate network changes such as new lanes, meet points, and operating hours. Quantify their effect on load factor, third-party trip use, headcount needs and speed to the customer.

• Identify demand trends and the network capacity they require, including site overflow and rerouting needs.

• Communicate promptly with stakeholders when changes to the network plan affect operations, and coordinate the response to capacity and demand constraints.

• Own your analyses from the initial question to the final recommendation.

• Present findings to stakeholders, with the definitions, date ranges and caveats behind the numbers.

• Use AI tools daily for analysis, querying and drafting.

• Build and maintain sheets, dashboards and planning tools.

What you should have/know

• Bachelor's degree, or 6+ years of equivalent work experience, in a quantitative discipline such as supply chain, engineering, operations or another STEM field.

• 2+ years of experience in network, transportation or supply chain planning.

• Hands-on experience with AI deeply integrated into your analytical workflow, including writing queries, building analyses, drafting findings, and automating recurring work.

• Advanced skill in Excel and/or Google Sheets.

• Familiarity with SQL, or the ability to learn it quickly.

• Hands-on experience with at least one of the following: scheduling software, demand modeling, transportation management systems, geographic information systems.

• Clear, concise written and verbal communication.

• Ability to manage several requests at once, set priorities, and deliver accurate work on tight timelines.

• Ability to work through complex problems with incomplete information.

• Sound judgment and discernment, including the ability to spot when a number, data source or AI-generated answer is wrong, incomplete or conflicts with another source.

• Ability to work on-site at our Tempe headquarters, with extensive use of computers.

It would be great if you also have

• Experience with Snowflake or another data warehouse.

• Experience with BI and dashboard tools such as Tableau.

• Background in logistics, fleet or transportation operations.

• Experience with routing, optimization or network design models.

Don't Meet 100% of the Qualifications?
At Carvana, we value diverse backgrounds and experiences. We encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't fit every single bullet point. Give it a shot—we'd love to hear from you!

What we’ll offer in return

• Full-Time position with a competitive salary.

• Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits.

• 401K with company match.

• A multitude of perks including student loan payments, discounts on vehicles, benefits for your pets, and much more.

• A great wellness program to keep you healthy and happy both physically and mentally.

• Access to opportunities to expand your skill set and share your knowledge with others across the organization.

• A company culture focused on high performance and bar-raising, with vast opportunity to learn and grow.

Other requirements
To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

• Must be able to read, write, speak, and understand English.

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

Legal stuff
Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check.  This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

Carvana is an equal employment opportunity employer.  All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law.  Carvana also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories.

- MEMBER OF TECHNICAL STAFF

Multiple roles available





DESIGN THE HARDWARE POWERING THE NEXT GENERATION OF AI INFRASTRUCTURE

This role is ideal for an engineer who enjoys translating vendor reference architectures into highly optimized, production-ready systems that maximize performance, reliability, serviceability, and cost efficiency.

 
 


THE OPPORTUNITY

As one of the earliest infrastructure engineers on the team, you'll own the physical design of GPU servers and rack-scale systems that form the foundation of a rapidly expanding AI platform. Working closely with GPU vendors, ODMs/OEMs, data center engineering, networking, and operations teams, you'll drive hardware architecture from concept through deployment while influencing future infrastructure strategy.

 - Comfortable operating as a senior technical leader within a fast-moving, high-growth engineering organization.

 


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

jobs.title: Senior/Staff Systems Engineer, Autonomy Verification
jobs.description:
Who We Are

Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. Safer streets, more time for what matters, and easier access to the world around us, that’s why we’re building a universal autonomy platform: self-driving for all roads and all rides.

Founded in 2016, Nuro is a physical AI company developing Level 4 autonomous driving technology for a wide range of vehicles, use cases, and markets. Powered by the Nuro Driver™, our universal autonomy platform enables the global mobility ecosystem to deploy autonomy at scale, from robotaxis and logistics fleets to personal vehicles.

With years of real-world deployment experience and a flexible, partner-led business model, Nuro is working toward a future where millions of autonomous vehicles powered by our technology help make everyday life safer, easier, and more connected.

Nuro has raised over $2B in capital from Uber, NVIDIA, Google, Softbank, Fidelity, T. Rowe Price, and other leading investors.

About the Role

As a Senior/Staff Systems Engineer working on Autonomy Verification, you are responsible for verifying that the Nuro Driver is safe to deploy in our target ODD and complies with the rules of the road. This requires prior experience with the development or validation of autonomous systems, and a collaborative nature to work closely with a variety of teams across Nuro: Autonomy Software, Simulation, Product, and Operations. You will have end-to-end ownership from requirements definition, metrics design, and test strategy development.

About the Work

• Create requirements for an autonomous system, ensuring safe operation within its ODD and compliance with the rules of the road.

• Design generalizable metrics and acceptance criteria to verify that the autonomous system satisfies these requirements, leveraging safety standards and methodologies.

• Propose and leverage diverse test strategies - synthetic and log simulation, on-road logs, closed-course testing, third-party accident reconstructions - to verify requirements.

• Collaborate closely with Behavior, Perception, Data Science, Product, Legal, and Public Trust teams to develop acceptance criteria for metrics and tests.

• Partner with simulation infrastructure and test integration teams to set up automated verification workflows.

• Quantify coverage of the tests for our ODD, ensuring simulation realism and relevance for deployment. Link the results from the tests as evidence to support the Autonomy Safety Case.

About You

• 5+ years of technical work experience in a relevant area with 3+ years of experience with development or validation of autonomous vehicles/robotic systems.

• Experience creating behavior requirements for SAE L2, L3, or L4 autonomous systems or other robotic systems to operate safely within its ODD.

• Experience with simulation and real-world testing of autonomous systems.

• Strong understanding of the autonomy architecture - how sensing, localization, perception, prediction, behavior, and control modules interact.

• Hands-on software experience, with the ability to code in Python or C++.

• Highly collaborative in nature, with strong abilities to think and communicate analytically and effectively.

Bonus Points

• Background in autonomous vehicles ideally with L4 AV deployment.

• Prior experience building computational models for driving behavior or ML based metrics for behavior evaluation.

• Familiarity with safety standards and methodologies like STPA, ISO-21448, ISO 8800.

• Experience developing a safety case or compiling evidence supporting a safety case in a structured manner.

At Nuro, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. For this position, the reasonably expected base pay range is between $176,400 and $319,720 for the level at which this job has been scoped. Your base pay will depend on several factors, including your experience, qualifications, education, location, and skills. In the event that you are considered for a different level, a higher or lower pay range would apply. This position is also eligible for an annual performance bonus, equity, and a competitive benefits package.

At Nuro, we celebrate differences and are committed to a diverse workplace that fosters inclusion and psychological safety for all employees. Nuro is proud to be an equal opportunity employer and expressly prohibits any form of workplace discrimination based on race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, genetic information, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristics. #LI-DNP

jobs.description:

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

This role is built for someone who has built motion systems in fast-moving environments, cares deeply about craft, and brings an AI-first mindset to how creative work gets made. You'll join the Brand Studio, the team behind the brand across the entire SpaceXSI ecosystem (from Grok and Grok Bot to X), and help define both the motion language of the brand and how it comes to life in our campaigns and products. COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

Annual Salary:

$172,000 - $250,000 USD

jobs.title: Virtualization & Orchestration Engineer - Member of Technical Staff
jobs.description:
VIRTUALIZATION & ORCHESTRATION ENGINEER 
- MEMBER OF TECHNICAL STAFF

Location: Hybrid | Bellevue, WA (downtown)
Multiple levels and roles available





BUILD THE PLATFORM LAYER POWERING NEXT-GENERATION AI INFRASTRUCTURE



ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

A well-funded, rapidly growing AI infrastructure company is building a next-generation cloud platform designed to power the full lifecycle of artificial intelligence. The organization is developing a comprehensive AI infrastructure, platform, and services portfolio that supports the full spectrum of AI workloads—including large-scale compute, model training, fine-tuning, inference, and emerging agentic AI applications.



Backed by significant long-term investment, the company combines the speed, ownership, and innovation of a startup with the stability and resources of an established parent organization. Engineering teams are intentionally lean, highly collaborative, and AI-native, leveraging modern automation and tooling to build infrastructure capable of supporting the industry's most demanding AI workloads.



We're seeking Virtualization & Orchestration Engineers to build the platform layer that enables customers to reliably consume GPU compute at scale. This team is responsible for designing and operating the virtualization, Kubernetes, provisioning, and orchestration systems that power large-scale AI workloads across next-generation data center infrastructure.

 
 


THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a foundational engineering role within the company's largest infrastructure engineering organization. You'll help design and build the systems that make GPU capacity available, scalable, secure, and reliable across a multi-tenant AI cloud platform.



You'll work at the intersection of virtualization, Kubernetes, distributed systems, GPU infrastructure, and high-performance computing, solving complex challenges around workload scheduling, resource allocation, cluster management, and infrastructure automation.



This opportunity is ideal for engineers who enjoy building large-scale platforms from the ground up and owning critical infrastructure systems end-to-end.

 



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and build virtualization infrastructure supporting GPU-intensive AI and HPC workloads.

 - Develop and operate Kubernetes-based orchestration systems for GPU cluster provisioning and workload scheduling.

 - Build automated provisioning systems that enable GPU capacity to be allocated, scaled, and reclaimed efficiently across multiple tenants.

 - Design solutions for workload placement, resource management, and cluster lifecycle operations.

 - Partner closely with hardware, networking, infrastructure, and AI platform teams to ensure orchestration systems align with real-world cluster architectures and constraints.

 - Improve the reliability, security, scalability, and operational maturity of the orchestration platform.

 - Build tooling and automation that simplifies infrastructure management and improves developer and customer experiences.

 - Contribute to architectural decisions, engineering standards, and best practices as the platform evolves.

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong hands-on experience with Kubernetes and container orchestration in production environments.

 - Experience designing, building, and operating large-scale infrastructure platforms.

 - Background with virtualization technologies supporting cloud, HPC, GPU, or distributed computing environments.

 - Understanding of GPU cluster provisioning, workload scheduling, and resource management.

 - Experience with Linux-based infrastructure and distributed systems concepts.

 - Ability to independently own complex systems from design through production operation.

 - Comfortable working in a fast-moving environment where architecture and processes are being established.

 


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience with GPU scheduling technologies such as Slurm, Kubernetes device plugins, NVIDIA GPU Operator, or similar frameworks.

 - Experience supporting AI infrastructure, machine learning platforms, HPC environments, or GPU cloud providers.

 - Background building multi-tenant infrastructure platforms for cloud providers or large-scale compute environments.

 - Experience with infrastructure automation, Infrastructure as Code, and platform engineering practices.

 - Familiarity with high-performance networking and GPU cluster architectures.

 


COMPENSATION

 - Competitive base pay for Bellevue market

 - Certain roles are eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, annual bonus, and long term incentives. These awards are allocated based on individual performance  

 - U.S. based employees have access to medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401(k) plan and company match, employees also receive per calendar year, paid holidays

 


LOCATION

 - Hybrid role based in the Bellevue, WA area.

 - Approximately three days per week in the office.

 - Candidates elsewhere in the U.S. who are open to relocation are encouraged to apply.

 - U.S. work authorization is required. Visa sponsorship is not currently available.

 


WHY JOIN?

 - Build the orchestration platform powering one of the industry's most advanced AI infrastructure environments.

 - Work directly on GPU clusters, Kubernetes platforms, and large-scale distributed systems.

 - Solve complex infrastructure challenges across virtualization, scheduling, resource management, and automation.

 - Join early enough to influence architecture, engineering practices, and platform strategy.

 - Collaborate with a highly experienced team building the foundation for next-generation AI applications.

 - Enjoy the ownership and technical impact of a startup environment backed by significant long-term investment.

jobs.title: Senior Cryogenic System Engineer
jobs.description:
PsiQuantum's mission is to build the first useful quantum computers: machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries.

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry, including partners like GlobalFoundries, we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don't feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.

That approach has since been tested at the highest level of scrutiny the U.S. government applies to emerging technology, and it has held up. In 2025, PsiQuantum closed a $1 billion funding round that valued the company at $7 billion. In 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce signed a $100 million Letter of Intent under the CHIPS and Science Act, followed by a $125 million agreement with DARPA under Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, PsiQuantum's most valuable U.S. government agreement to date. This year, we also broke ground on our utility-scale quantum computer in Brisbane, Australia, and continued building out our Chicago site. Victor Peng, our CEO, and co-founder Jeremy O'Brien, now Executive Chairman, lead a team and board that reflects how seriously the world is taking this build, joined this year by Intel's Lip-Bu Tan and Atomico's Niklas Zennström.

PsiQuantum also develops the algorithms and software needed to make these systems commercially valuable. Our application, software, and industry teams work directly with leading Fortune 500 companies, including Airbus, Lockheed Martin, Mercedes-Benz, Boehringer Ingelheim, and Mitsubishi Chemical, to prepare quantum solutions for real-world impact.

Quantum computing is not an extension of classical computing. It represents a fundamental shift, and a path to mastering challenges that cannot be solved any other way. The potential is enormous, and we now have the funding, the government validation, and the sites under construction to make it real.

Job Summary:

The Senior Cryogenic System Engineer is responsible for the design, analysis, verification, validation, integration, and operational support of cryogenic systems that enable PsiQuantum's quantum computing infrastructure.

This role focuses on system integration of cryostats, cryogenic distribution systems, cryoplants, and related technologies, applying strong engineering judgment across thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, and structural mechanics.

The role supports the full engineering lifecycle from requirements definition, detailed design, analysis, vendor coordination, fabrication, installation, integration, testing, commissioning, and troubleshooting. The Senior Cryogenic System Engineer also provides technical leadership in ambiguous situations and helps establish robust processes, documentation practices, and verification methods for complex cryogenic systems.

The ideal candidate combines strong cryogenic systems engineering expertise with practical mechanical design experience, analytical rigor, and hands-on execution. They are comfortable leading technical work across design, analysis, verification, vendor coordination, installation, commissioning, and troubleshooting while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary teams.

Responsibilities:

• Lead integration of cryostat components, including mechanical hardware, sensors, valves, and instrumentation.

• Lead integration of cryogenic equipment, including cryostats, cryogenic distribution systems, vacuum systems, cryoplants, and cryogenic storage.

• Apply thermodynamics, heat transfer, fluid mechanics, and structural mechanics to develop cryogenic system designs.

• Perform detailed design, analysis, and testing of cryogenic system components and assemblies.

• Coordinate technical activities across multiple disciplines and provide hands-on guidance during fabrication, installation, integration, and operations.

• Lead the development of verification and validation test plans for cryogenic mechanical systems and evaluate test results.

• Select, support, and direct vendors during design, manufacturing, and testing.

• Analyze field issues related to cryogenic design and provide technical solutions where required.

• Participate in multidisciplinary project teams through all phases of product development to ensure successful execution of innovative, best-in-class designs.

Experience/Qualifications:

• B.Sc., M.Sc., or Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Physics, or a related discipline.

• 3–5+ years of experience applying engineering principles to solve complex problems related to thermal-fluid systems and/or cryogenics.

• Experience with cryogenic mechanical systems, including cryostats, cryogenic distribution systems, valve boxes, and/or cryoplants.

• Experience with requirements management, materials and component selection, FMEA, tolerance analysis, and test planning.

• Ability to provide technical leadership in ambiguous situations.

• Demonstrated analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience with software tools such as Mathcad, SINDA/FLUINT, Thermal Desktop, SINAPS, ANSYS APDL, ANSYS Workbench, SolidWorks, SpaceClaim, LabVIEW, and MATLAB.

• Experience working with cryogenic systems, cryostats, cryocoolers, cryogenic distribution systems, vacuum pumps, and cryoplants.

• Experience coordinating technical activities during construction, installation, or commissioning of large-scale scientific or industrial facilities.

• Experience applying best practices to the design, fabrication, and assembly of cryogenic equipment.

• Experience with material performance, design constraints, and manufacturing constraints under cryogenic conditions.

• Hands-on experience with fabrication methods such as machining, welding, brazing, soldering, and forming.

• Hands-on experience performing lab testing and data acquisition.

• Understanding of Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing per ASME Y14.5.

jobs.title: Head of Business Operations & Finance
jobs.description:

ABOUT FLOX

We’re building Flox to make Nix practical for teams operating at enterprise scale — giving developers and AI agents a reproducible foundation to build and run software without environment drift.



We recently raised a $25M Series B led by Addition, NEA, and D. E. Shaw. We’re still early, but we’re already working with companies including NVIDIA, Microsoft, CoreWeave, Morgan Stanley, D. E. Shaw, Resolve AI, and PostHog.

You’ll own our financial model, planning, forecasting, and core finance operations, while also working directly with the CEO on the questions that matter most to the company: where we invest, how quickly we hire, how we price, how we measure the business, and which strategic opportunities we pursue.



We’re looking for someone who likes being close to the details but can zoom out quickly. One day you may be preparing for a Board meeting or updating our operating model; the next you may be evaluating a strategic partnership, acquisition opportunity, major customer investment, or new market initiative.



You’ll have significant ownership from day one and the opportunity to grow into a key member of our leadership team.



What You’ll Own

 - Finance and planning: Own our operating model, budget, forecasts, cash planning, runway, and long-range scenarios.

 - Company performance: Build the metrics and reporting that help us understand how the business is performing and where we should invest.

 - Board and fundraising: Lead the financial side of Board preparation, investor reporting, fundraising, and diligence.

 - Corporate development: Evaluate strategic partnerships, acquisitions, investments, and other inorganic opportunities, including financial analysis, diligence, and transaction support.

 - Finance operations: Oversee accounting, tax, treasury, compliance, and financial reporting, working with external partners where appropriate.

 - GTM economics: Partner with the commercial team on pricing, packaging, revenue forecasting, deal economics, and sales capacity.

 - Business operations: Take on important cross-functional problems, improve how we operate, and build the systems and processes we’ll need as the company scales.




WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

You may come from IB, PE, strategic finance, corporate development, consulting, or a high-growth technology company. Finance experience is strongly preferred, and experience evaluating strategic transactions, partnerships, or acquisitions is a plus.



You’ll likely be a strong fit if you:

 - Are excellent with financial models and comfortable making decisions with imperfect information.

 - Understand how venture-backed technology companies operate and what changes as they scale.

 - Can evaluate both organic and inorganic growth opportunities, moving comfortably between strategy and execution.

 - Have worked closely with founders, executives, Boards, or investors.

 - Communicate clearly and can turn complex analysis into a simple point of view.

 - Enjoy building from scratch rather than inheriting mature systems and processes.

 - Want a role where the scope will evolve as quickly as the company does.



Experience with enterprise software, developer tools, cloud infrastructure, AI infrastructure, or usage-based businesses is helpful but not required.

jobs.description:
COMPANY DESCRIPTION

Today, when you go to your doctor and get referred to a specialist, your doctor sends out a referral and tells you, “They’ll be in touch soon.” So you wait. And wait. Sometimes days, weeks, or even months. Why? Because too often providers are overwhelmed with the painstakingly tedious work required to get paid by insurance companies. Powered by proprietary models, Tennr handles the complex paperwork that gets patients through the door and providers paid, helping operators get patients the right care, at the right time, in the right setting.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

As an Implementation Engineer, you’ll build, test, and support automation solutions for Tennr’s most complex customers: large-scale health systems, national provider groups, and strategic partners. This is a hands-on, highly technical, customer-facing role that demands strong judgment, quality discipline, and the ability to deliver on committed timelines.

You’ll work alongside an Embedded Solutions Engineer who owns solution design, while you own the build, the testing, and the health of the account after go-live. You’ll pressure test designs before you build them, ship work that holds up under real operational load, and keep multiple build threads moving at once.

This role sits within Embedded Solutions and works directly with Solutions Engineers, Account Partners, Product, and Engineering.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Build, test, and optimize customer workflows on Tennr’s platform against the Solutions Engineer’s architecture

 - Pressure test designs up front and flag logic gaps, edge cases, and downstream effects with a proposed fix

 - Run multiple concurrent build threads while keeping timelines and status clear for internal stakeholders

 - Test your own work end to end, including edge cases and failure scenarios, and prevent regressions on live enterprise deployments where a bug has immediate operational impact

 - Own post-go-live support for your accounts, handling customer communication and issue resolution

 - Stay with the customer past go-live to build on top of the core workflows, expand automation into new areas, and evolve the build as their business changes

 - Write well-scoped product tickets and collaborate with Product and Engineering to improve the platform

 - Work in an agile cadence (sprints, grooming, estimation) and give an accurate forward read on capacity and at-risk dates
   
   


QUALIFICATIONS

 - 3+ years building, testing, and deploying software integrations for external, enterprise customers

 - A degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, Information Systems, or Industrial/Operations Engineering is preferred. Equivalent experience is welcome

 - Comfortable working directly in code across APIs, data workflows, and system integrations, and able to debug your way through an unfamiliar system

 - Fluency with agentic and AI-assisted workflows

 - Strong QA discipline: you test your own work thoroughly and catch issues at build time

 - Clear communicator with customers and internal teams

 - Experience running work in an agile cadence (sprints, grooming, estimation)

 - Able to manage several concurrent workstreams and own a date

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and fast-paced, high-ownership environments

 - Based in New York City area (or open to re-location) and able to work on-site 4 days/week
   
   


NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience with healthcare systems and data, such as EHR integrations, HL7/FHIR, revenue cycle, or referral and authorization workflows

 - Experience with enterprise go-lives

 - Advanced fluency with agentic and AI-assisted development. Coding agents are a core part of how you work, you know how to scope and direct them through non-trivial builds, and you can spot when the output is wrong before it ships

 - Familiarity with workflow automation, RPA, or enterprise integration platforms (e.g., Workato, UiPath)
   
   


WHY TENNR?

 - Drive Impact: one of our company values is Cowboy, meaning you set the pace. You won’t just talk about things, you’ll get them done. And feel the impact.

 - Develop Operational Expertise: learn the inner workings of scaling systems, tools, and infrastructure

 - Innovate with Purpose: we’re not just doing this for fun (although we do have a lot of fun). At Tennr, you’ll join a high-caliber team maniacally focused on reducing patient delays across the U.S. healthcare system.

 - Build Relationships: collaborate and connect with like-minded, driven individuals in our Hudson Square office 4 days/week

 - Free lunch! Plus a pantry full of snacks.
   
   


BENEFITS

 - Beautiful new office at 345 Hudson Street

 - Unlimited PTO

 - 100% paid employee health benefit options

 - Employer funded 401(k) match

 - Competitive parental leave

Salesforce Certified Developer / Architect – Public Sector - Minnesota
jobs.description:
Are you a certified Salesforce Developer / Architect who enjoys turning complex government requirements into secure, scalable solutions that make a meaningful impact? If you bring strong hands-on Salesforce development experience, expertise across multiple Salesforce Clouds, and the ability to bridge architecture, development, and business needs, we'd love to connect with you!

About the role

The Salesforce Certified Developer / Architect role is focused on designing, developing, integrating, and enhancing enterprise Salesforce solutions that support critical Public Sector operations.

As part of FormativGroup's Salesforce Practice, you'll contribute to Salesforce modernization and implementation initiatives supporting government organizations, working across Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, and Government Cloud.

You'll combine hands-on technical development with architecture and solution design, collaborating closely with Enterprise Architects, Business Analysts, Project Managers, QA teams, and business stakeholders. This role requires the ability to translate business requirements into Salesforce solutions, support system integrations, streamline processes, and guide technical execution throughout the Agile delivery lifecycle.

What You'll Work On

As a Salesforce Certified Developer / Architect, you will:

• Design, develop, configure, and enhance Salesforce solutions to support complex Public Sector business requirements.

• Contribute to Salesforce architecture and technical design while remaining actively involved in hands-on development and implementation.

• Develop solutions across Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, and Government Cloud using Salesforce development and configuration capabilities.

• Design and implement integrations between Salesforce and external enterprise applications, ensuring secure and reliable data exchange.

• Create, enhance, and maintain Salesforce automation using Flows, workflows, and declarative configuration tools to improve business processes and operational efficiency.

• Partner with Business Analysts and business stakeholders to gather, analyze, and translate requirements into technical designs and development deliverables.

• Collaborate with Project Managers to define project scope, timelines, deliverables, dependencies, and implementation plans.

• Work with Enterprise Architects, Business Analysts, and QA teams to develop test scenarios, validate functionality, and support User Acceptance Testing (UAT).

• Participate in Agile delivery activities, including requirements refinement, sprint planning, development, testing, and release readiness.

• Assess and document change requests, evaluate technical and delivery impacts, and support formal change approval processes.

• Create and maintain technical documentation, solution designs, configuration records, and implementation materials.

• Provide knowledge transfer to technical teams, administrators, and business stakeholders to support ongoing platform maintenance and adoption.

• Apply Salesforce architecture, security, integration, and development best practices to support scalable and maintainable solutions.

What You'll Bring

You will likely be successful in this role if you have:

• Minimum 7 years of hands-on Salesforce design and development experience.

• Active and valid Salesforce certifications in the following areas: Salesforce Certified Application Architect Salesforce Certified Platform Developer Salesforce Certified Agentforce Specialist Salesforce Certified Advanced Administrator (Administrator II)

• Minimum 2 years of experience with Salesforce Sales Cloud.

• Minimum 2 years of experience with Salesforce Service Cloud.

• Minimum 2 years of experience with Salesforce Experience Cloud.

• Minimum 2 years of experience with Salesforce Government Cloud.

• Strong experience designing, developing, and integrating Salesforce solutions within enterprise environments.

• Experience translating business requirements into scalable Salesforce configurations, technical designs, and application functionality.

• Experience creating and maintaining Salesforce automation, workflows, and business process improvements.

• Understanding of Salesforce architecture, integrations, security, data models, and platform best practices.

• Experience collaborating across Agile delivery teams, including architects, developers, business analysts, QA resources, and project managers.

• Experience supporting testing, UAT, implementation planning, documentation, and knowledge transfer.

• Strong communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across business and technical stakeholders.

How You Work

The ideal candidate will:

• Combine hands-on Salesforce development expertise with architectural thinking, balancing technical execution with long-term solution scalability.

• Take ownership of assigned work, applying sound technical judgment to complex development and integration challenges.

• Collaborate effectively with Enterprise Architects, Business Analysts, Project Managers, QA teams, and government stakeholders.

• Navigate changing requirements, project dependencies, and delivery priorities while maintaining a strong focus on quality and accountability.

• Communicate technical concepts clearly, document solutions thoroughly, and support effective knowledge transfer across teams.

Bonus Points If You Have

• Scaled Agile Certified SAFe Practitioner certification.

• Salesforce Certified Data Architect certification.

• Salesforce Certified Sharing and Visibility Architect certification.

• 5+ years of Salesforce Administrator experience.

• Experience using Azure DevOps (ADO) for project tracking, development coordination, or release management.

• Experience supporting technology initiatives for state or federal government agencies.

• Experience delivering technology solutions within the mortgage, housing finance, or real estate industries.

• Experience supporting complex government Salesforce implementations involving multiple Clouds, integrations, and regulatory requirements.

What Success Looks Like

• Salesforce solutions are designed and developed in alignment with government business requirements, technical architecture standards, and implementation objectives.

• Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Experience Cloud, and Government Cloud capabilities are configured and integrated effectively to support business operations.

• Automated workflows, system integrations, and platform enhancements improve operational efficiency and reduce manual processing.

• Technical documentation, testing support, UAT coordination, and change management activities contribute to predictable, high-quality delivery.

• Business stakeholders, architects, and project teams benefit from clear communication, dependable technical execution, and effective collaboration.

• Knowledge transfer and solution documentation support long-term platform sustainability and ongoing enhancement opportunities.

Why Join FormativGroup

FormativGroup is a PE-backed technology consulting and implementation partner helping organizations modernize complex business platforms, improve delivery outcomes, and scale technology solutions that support long-term growth. We partner with clients across strategy, solution design, implementation, and ongoing support to help move critical initiatives from vision to execution. Our teams bring deep technical expertise, delivery discipline, and a collaborative approach to every engagement.

At FormativGroup, you'll work with people who are practical, collaborative, and focused on solving meaningful business and technology problems. We're growing, which means you'll have opportunities to contribute ideas, work closely with experienced leaders, and help shape how we deliver for clients.

Employment Eligibility

• This is a U.S.based hybrid role, St. Paul, Minnesota

• To be considered for this position, candidates must reside in one of the following U.S. states: MN

• Candidates residing outside these states are not currently eligible for consideration.

• Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S.

• FormativGroup is unable to sponsor or assume sponsorship of an employment visa for this position

• Not open to 3rd party/C2C engagement

We are committed to pay equity and transparency. The compensation range for this position represents our good faith estimate of the range we reasonably expect to pay for this role at the time of posting. The actual compensation offered will be determined based on factors such as the candidate’s experience, skills, education, work location, and internal equity.

In addition to base pay, employees may be eligible for discretionary bonuses, commissions, or other incentive programs, as well as a comprehensive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off, etc.

Estimated Compensation Range:

$70—$80 USD

FormativGroup operates within the critical middle layer of business technology, where applications and systems connect infrastructure to business processes. We are specialists who help the middle market take full advantage of their technology investments with deep, industry-centric expertise, all in one place, to unify fragmented systems. With deep technical expertise across cloud architecture, system integration, AI, and data strategy, we bridge the gap between business goals and modern platforms.

Motive's Customer Engineering team is a post-sales technical solutions function for our largest, most strategic, and business-critical customers. As the Director, Customer Engineering, you'll lead and develop a team of Customer Engineers who turn difficult operational problems into working solutions using Motive's products, supported APIs, data, reporting, and automation.

You'll combine people leadership, technical judgment, and customer-facing problem solving to help the team deliver measurable customer value. You'll establish how the team prioritizes engagements, maintain a high bar for solution quality, and ensure successful customer work becomes reusable expertise for Motive's customers and broader Solutions Engineering organization.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role where you’ll help the team solve meaningful customer problems, validate what works, drive lasting customer value, and ensure clear ownership after handoff.

• Strong Solutions Engineering, technical consulting, post-sales engineering, or comparable customer-facing experience; you understand the difference between demonstrating a solution and delivering one.

• Credible technical depth in enterprise SaaS, API-based capabilities, data analysis, automation, integrations, advanced product configuration, and troubleshooting product behavior.

• Experience turning ambiguous customer problems into delivered solutions with clear adoption and measurable business results.

• Ability to coach practitioners through customer discovery, technical problem solving, stakeholder management, solution validation, and evidence-backed documentation.

• Ability to work directly with customer executives, IT leaders, frontline operators, and account stakeholders while influencing internal Product and Engineering teams.

jobs.title: HPC/GPU Performance / Kernel Engineer - Member of Technical Staff
jobs.description:
HPC/GPU PERFORMANCE / KERNEL ENGINEER 
- MEMBER OF TECHNICAL STAFF

Location: Hybrid | Bellevue, WA (downtown)
Multiple roles and levels available





OPTIMIZE THE PERFORMANCE LAYER POWERING NEXT-GENERATION AI INFRASTRUCTURE



ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

A well-funded, rapidly growing AI infrastructure company is building a next-generation cloud platform designed to power the full lifecycle of artificial intelligence. The organization is developing a comprehensive AI infrastructure, platform, and services portfolio that supports the full spectrum of AI workloads—including large-scale compute, model training, fine-tuning, inference, and emerging agentic AI applications.



Backed by significant long-term investment, the company combines the speed, ownership, and innovation of a startup with the stability and resources of an established parent organization. Engineering teams are intentionally lean, highly collaborative, and AI-native, leveraging modern tooling and automation to build infrastructure capable of supporting the industry's most demanding AI workloads.



We're seeking GPU Performance / Kernel Engineer to optimize the data plane powering large-scale AI workloads. This role focuses on improving GPU utilization, reducing latency, and maximizing throughput across training and inference environments by tuning kernels, identifying performance bottlenecks, and driving efficiency across the GPU fleet.

 
 


THE OPPORTUNITY

This is a high-impact engineering role focused on extracting maximum performance from large-scale GPU infrastructure. You'll work at the intersection of GPU architecture, AI workloads, systems performance, and low-level optimization.



As part of a highly technical infrastructure team, you'll analyze workload behavior, optimize performance-critical code paths, and develop the techniques and tooling required to operate AI systems efficiently at scale.



This opportunity is ideal for engineers who enjoy deep technical challenges involving GPU computing, kernel optimization, distributed AI workloads, and hardware/software performance.

 
 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Profile, analyze, and optimize GPU kernels to improve latency, throughput, and overall utilization.

 - Identify and eliminate data-plane bottlenecks impacting GPU performance across large-scale AI workloads.

 - Tune performance-critical workloads across training and inference environments.

 - Work closely with AI infrastructure, machine learning, and platform engineering teams to understand workload characteristics and optimize system behavior.

 - Develop benchmarking methodologies and performance measurement practices across GPU infrastructure.

 - Evaluate emerging GPU technologies, performance tools, and optimization techniques as hardware platforms evolve.

 - Contribute to engineering practices that improve GPU efficiency, scalability, and reliability across the fleet.

 


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Strong experience with GPU kernel development and performance optimization using technologies such as CUDA, ROCm, or comparable GPU programming frameworks.

 - Demonstrated experience improving GPU utilization, reducing latency, or increasing throughput for production AI workloads.

 - Strong understanding of GPU architecture, memory hierarchy, parallel computing, and the data path from application layer to hardware execution.

 - Experience profiling and debugging performance issues in complex AI or distributed computing environments.

jobs.title: Application Developer (Java, JavaScript) (Full-Stack)
jobs.description:
At Broadway Ventures, we transform challenges into opportunities with expert program management, cutting-edge technology, and innovative consulting solutions. As an 8(a), HUBZone, and Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB), we empower government and private sector clients by delivering tailored solutions that drive operational success, sustainability, and growth. Built on integrity, collaboration, and excellence, we’re more than a service provider—we’re your trusted partner in innovation.

Position Summary

The Application Developer builds the Java services that ingest public health IT data, observe deployed FHIR endpoints, validate what they find, and assemble reproducible evidence cases for Project Argos. You write the deterministic validators that make pass/fail determinations, plus the retry, rate-limiting, and instrumentation logic that keeps monitoring safe and repeatable. Agentic components may summarize and draft, but they do not make final compliance calls, and your code enforces that boundary.

Type:

• The position is open to both W2 and 1099

• Part-time, variable hours, 10 - 29 hours a week

• 1 year contract

Pay:

• W2: pay rate of $55 - $60/hr

• 1099: $65 - $70/hr

Works with: Technical Lead, AI/Engineering Lead, Senior Systems Engineer, and Project Manager.

About Broadway Ventures and Project Argos

Broadway Ventures, LLC is a Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) and HUBZone federal contractor headquartered in Vicksburg, Mississippi, with operations in the Madison/Huntsville, Alabama area.

Project Argos is an agentic AI proof of concept for the Office of the National Coordinator for Health IT (ONC). Broadway is the prime contractor, with Audacious Inquiry as subcontractor. The pipeline pulls published API endpoint data for roughly 290 certified health IT products from the Certified Health IT Product List (CHPL), tests those endpoints on a repeatable schedule, and builds reproducible evidence cases for compliance gaps under 45 CFR Part 170. It runs in a contractor-hosted AWS GovCloud environment, and a qualified human reviews every finding before it becomes a confirmed issue.

Key Responsibilities

- Build ingestion connectors for CHPL, Service Base URL Lists, developer-published FHIR Bundles, Lantern, and other approved public sources. Preserve raw artifacts, timestamps, request metadata, response headers, and hashes.
- Normalize developer, product, version, criterion, CHPL ID, endpoint, organization, and validation records into the project's common data model in DynamoDB, with lineage and source-of-truth precedence rules.
- Implement publication checks that fetch endpoint lists and classify availability failures: URL not found, timeouts, obscuring redirects, malformed responses, and non-machine-readable content.
- Build safe, non-authenticated endpoint observation for metadata and CapabilityStatement retrieval, and detect drift as endpoints are added, removed, moved, or changed.
- Run FHIR R4 validation against Endpoint, Organization, and Bundle resources, preserving both raw and normalized results.
- Build the evidence case package with source metadata, request and response logs, validation outputs, severity, and rule traceability. Support deduplication, clustering, and export to Government-designated systems.
- Design scheduling, retry and backoff, rate limiting, error handling, and audit logging for pipeline and agentic components.
- Make test runs replayable so a reviewer can re-run a test for any evidence case.
- Write unit and integration tests, including stub and mock endpoints for failure scenarios. Participate in code review and keep technical documentation current.
- Keep the code from requesting, collecting, or storing patient data, PHI, credentials, or tokens unless the Government authorizes it in writing.

Required Qualifications

- 5+ years of Java (17+) development, including concurrency and networked services
- 3+ years of Spring Boot or an equivalent framework
- 2+ years of JavaScript/Node for tooling and front-end development
- 4+ years building REST APIs and working with JSON
- 3+ years of working knowledge of HTTP and TLS fundamentals
- 3+ years with the AWS SDK, DynamoDB data modeling, and S3
- 2+ years building and running containerized services
- 4+ years of automated testing (JUnit, integration tests)
- 3+ years of code review and technical documentation
- 1+ year building with LLM APIs or using AI coding assistants in development, including testing and validating AI-generated output
- Authorized to work in the United States

PreferredQualifications

- HAPI FHIR or other FHIR R4 validation experience (US Core, CapabilityStatements)
- HTTP client internals, including timing and connection instrumentation
- Scheduling, retry and backoff, and rate-limiting design
- Testcontainers or stub and mock services for failure testing
- SMART on FHIR, Inferno, or ONC certification testing
- Health IT or federal program experience

What to Expect Next:

After submitting your application, our recruiting team will review your qualifications. This may include a brief telephone interview or email communication to verify resume details and discuss compensation expectations. Interviews will be conducted with the most qualified candidates. Broadway Ventures conducts background checks and drug testing prior to the start of employment. Some positions may also require fingerprinting.

Broadway Ventures is an equal opportunity employer and a VEVRAA federal contractor. We do not discriminate against applicants or employees on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, protected veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.

Reasonable accommodations are available for applicants with disabilities. Broadway Ventures utilizes the OFCCP-approved Voluntary Self-Identification of Disability Form (CC-305).

The pay range shown is a good-faith estimate of the compensation Broadway Ventures reasonably expects to pay for this position at the time of posting. It is not a guarantee of any particular wage, salary, or total compensation. Actual pay offered depends on job-related factors, which may include skills, experience, education, certifications and licensure, geographic work location, contract funding and budget. For positions covered by the Service Contract Act, pay is also governed by the applicable Department of Labor wage determination, which the government may revise.

Location Eligibility: Broadway Ventures cannot consider applicants who live in, or would work from, any of the following locations: California, Colorado, Connecticut, the District of Columbia, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, North Dakota, Ohio, Oregon, Rhode Island, Washington State, and Wyoming. Candidates must live in and work from an eligible U.S. state when they are hired and for as long as they are employed. Applications from residents of the locations listed above will not be considered.

Notice: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Our Hiring Process

Broadway Ventures uses an artificial intelligence (AI) tool to help review applications for this position.

• Who built it: Broadway Ventures developed the tool in-house.

• What it does: It compares your resume to the requirements in this job posting and gives a score from 0 to 100 showing how closely your qualifications match.

• What information it uses: The text of your resume, your name, your current or most recent job title, your location, and this job posting.

• What it cannot see: Your answers to voluntary demographic or equal employment opportunity questions, interview feedback, or offer information.

• How it is used: The score is one factor in our initial review of applications. The tool does not reject anyone. A member of our recruiting team reviews every application before any decision is made.

• Your options: If you would like your application reviewed without the AI tool, or you need a reasonable accommodation at any point in the hiring process, contact us at recruiting@broadwayventures.net. Making a request will not affect whether you are considered for this position.

jobs.title: HR Generalist

About Us

Powerlattice is a well-funded semiconductor start-up company backed by leading Silicon Valley venture capital firms. We are developing groundbreaking chiplet power delivery technology that will transform how high-performance processors are powered, enabling the next generation of AI and advanced computing.



About the Role

We are seeking a detail-oriented HR Generalist with 2-4 years of experience to support the day-to-day people operations of a growing start-up. In this role, you will work closely with HR leadership, finance, and hiring managers across engineering and operations to keep our policies, programs, and employee records accurate, compliant, and easy for employees to use.

This position offers hands-on experience across the full range of HR operations, including policy writing, employment law compliance, compensation and benefits administration, onboarding, and employee support, while helping build the foundation of a fast-growing technology company. Candidates who enjoy practical, process-driven work and want to broaden their generalist skill set are encouraged to apply.

As an HR Generalist, you will be a go-to resource for employees and managers on HR questions. Working under the guidance of HR leadership, you will draft and maintain policies, administer programs, and keep our practices aligned with federal and state requirements in Arizona and Washington.



Key Responsibilities

 - Policies & Handbook: Draft, update, and maintain HR policies, procedures, and the employee handbook. Research federal and state requirements, prepare clear policy language for review, and help communicate policy changes to employees and managers.

 - Employment Law Compliance: Help keep HR practices compliant with federal, California, Arizona, and Washington employment laws, including FLSA, FMLA, ADA, Title VII, EEO, I-9, state paid sick leave, and Washington Paid Family & Medical Leave. Track required postings, notices, and filings, and flag changes in regulations to HR leadership.

 - Compensation Administration: Support salary structures and pay ranges by gathering market data, maintaining job codes and levels, and preparing offer and pay-change documentation. Help ensure correct FLSA exempt/non-exempt classification and pay transparency compliance in job postings.

 - Benefits Administration: Administer health, dental, vision, life, disability, and 401(k) plans. Coordinate open enrollment, process qualifying life events, answer employee benefit questions, and work with brokers and carriers to resolve issues. Support COBRA, ACA reporting, and leave of absence processes.

 - Onboarding & Offboarding: Coordinate new-hire paperwork, I-9 verification, benefits enrollment, and orientation. Manage offboarding steps including final pay timing, benefits continuation notices, and exit interviews.

 - HR Operations & Records: Maintain accurate employee records and data in the HRIS. Process new hires, job changes, and terminations, and partner with finance to support accurate payroll. Prepare routine HR reports and metrics.

 - Employee Support: Serve as a first point of contact for employee and manager questions on policies, pay, benefits, and leave. Help document and escalate employee relations concerns according to established procedures.



Minimum Qualifications

 - This is a Hybrid role requiring 3 days a week onsite at our HQ’s in Vancouver, WA (Greater Portland Area) or Chandler, AZ (Greater Phoenix Area)

 - BS or BA in Human Resources, Business Administration, Psychology, or a related discipline.

 - 2-4 years of experience in a human resources generalist, coordinator, or specialist role.

 - Working knowledge of core U.S. employment laws, including FLSA, FMLA, ADA, Title VII, EEO, and I-9 requirements.

 - Experience writing or updating HR policies, procedures, or employee handbook content.

POSITION TITLE: Quality Assurance Supervisor

SALARY RANGE: $3,447.76- $ 5,093.93 Bi-weekly / $89,641.76 - $ 132,442.18 Annual

REPORTS TO: Director of Community Services

LOCATION: Concord

The Regional Center of the East Bay (RCEB) is one of 21 Regional Centers that are community-based, private non-profit corporations under contract with the California Department of Developmental Services. RCEB provides intake, assessment, diagnosis, and coordinates community-based services for over 25,000 children and adults with developmental disabilities in Alameda and Contra Costa counties.

RCEB envisions a future where persons with developmental disabilities are truly a part of the community. Persons with developmental disabilities receive supports and services they need to succeed. The supports and services change as the need changes.

In our dream, children with developmental disabilities live with families in typical communities. Many choose to attend their neighborhood schools and play with neighborhood friends. Adults with developmental disabilities live in the residence of their choice – with family members, with friends, or with their spouse / significant other. They engage in activities of their choice – work, volunteering, education, training, or leisure. They have meaningful relationships with friends and coworkers and are seen as valuable, contributing members of their communities.

POSITION SUMMARY

This Quality Assurance Supervisor position is a supervisory-level classification. Under general direction, this role is responsible for performing administrative and supervisory functions to ensure the delivery of high-quality, effective services for consumers of the Regional Center of the East Bay (RCEB). This role oversees QA staff and operations across residential and non-residential vendor programs, while leading training, technical assistance, and in-service orientations aligned with RCEB standards and Person-Centered practices. The position maintains responsibility for developing and implementing QA policies with a focus on Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) compliance and the Special Incident Report (SIR) processes, while ensuring adherence to Title 17 regulations. Serving as a liaison to external partner agencies, including the Department of Developmental Services (DDS) and Community Care Licensing, this role requires strong analytical skills, exceptional written and verbal communication, and the ability to foster cooperative working relationships with culturally diverse populations. This position reports to the Director of Community Services.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

• Perform administrative and supervisory functions, as assigned, to ensure that effective and high quality of services are provided for consumers of the Regional Center of the East Bay.

• Interview, select, train, assign, schedule, supervise, and evaluate Quality Assurance staff.

• Supervise Quality Assurance process for residential and non-residential vendors of the Regional Center of the East Bay.

• In coordination with Resource Development Staff and the Director of Community Services, supervise a program of training and technical assistance for Regional Center of the East Bay vendors, which includes RCEB’s philosophy and policies regarding standards of service and specific expectations of vendor services and programs.

• Provide consultation and assistance in the interpretation and enforcement of Title 17 regulations for RCEB staff, providers, and other agencies.

• Asses need, develop and provide in-service trainings and orientation to RCEB staff as assigned.

• Serve as consultant or liaison to assigned community programs, agencies, or organizations, including DDS and Community Care Licensing.

• Review and make recommendations regarding the proposed evaluation of programs and services as assigned.

• Develop, coordinate, and implement quality assurance policies for RCEB, concentrating on HCBS.

• Assist in the supervision and direction of SIR Coordinators and processes.

• Assisting with HCBS compliance activities, including participating in statewide committees, DDS funding activities, and promoting Person Centered Training.

• Perform other related duties as required.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

A degree in another discipline will be considered if the applicant has had 8 years managing a program providing residential supports, living supports or day program supports to people with IDD.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

WORK ENVIRONMENT

BENEFITS

jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

At Sprinter Health, our mission is to reimagine how people access care by bringing high quality care directly into the home.

Using the same technology that powers leading marketplace platforms, we deliver care where people are, especially those who need it most.

We’ve supported millions of patients across 22 states and consistently maintained a 90+ NPS, reflecting the quality and experience we strive to deliver every day.

Our clinical teams are at the center of making healthcare more accessible, connected, and personal.



Where patient experience isn’t a metric. It’s a standard.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Sprinter, you’ll bring healthcare directly to patients in the comfort of their homes. You’ll spend your day on the road providing a variety of preventative and diagnostic services, including blood draws, vitals, height and weight assessments, urine collection, support with Annual Wellness Visits, and more.

This role is perfect for someone who enjoys independence, connecting with patients, and a workday that looks different from a traditional clinic setting.

What We Offer

 - Guaranteed daily hours

 - National Mileage reimbursement, currently $0.76/mile reimbursement starting at mile 31

 - Company paid healthcare premiums

 - 100% 401(k) contribution of 3%

 - Company provided equipment including iPhone, iPad, scrubs, and supplies


WHAT YOU’LL DO

Life as a Sprinter starts before the first patient visit. Your car becomes both your office and your lab on the go, so preparation and organization are everything.

 - Prepare for your day by reviewing your schedule and ensuring you have the proper supplies and PPE.

 - Travel to patients’ homes throughout your assigned service area.

 - Provide scheduled services including blood draws, vitals, height and weight measurements, urine collection, support with Annual Wellness Visits, and other preventative and diagnostic services.

 - Use your expert phlebotomy skills to make blood draws as comfortable as possible for each patient.

 - Create a warm, welcoming, and professional experience in every patient’s home.

 - Accurately document each patient visit using Sprinter technology.

 - Properly label, handle, and transport specimens for lab drop off or shipment.

 - Manage your time, supplies, and schedule independently as you move from patient to patient throughout the day.


SOUND LIKE YOU?


MASTER OF YOUR CRAFT

 - Do you have exceptional blood draw skills?

 - Have you been the “go to” for hard sticks?

 - Are you confident in drawing blood from a wide range of patients?

 - Are you comfortable learning and performing additional clinical services?


ROAD WARRIOR

 - Do you enjoy a change of scenery during your workday?

 - Are you comfortable spending a significant portion of your day on the road?

 - Are you willing to travel an hour or more to visit patients?

 - Can you comfortably drive before 7:00 a.m. when your first patient is scheduled at 7:00 a.m.?


PATIENT FOCUSED

 - Are you passionate about helping others?

 - Are you kind, empathetic, and an effective communicator?

 - Do you enjoy meeting new people and creating a great patient experience?


SEEN IT ALL BEFORE

 - Are you comfortable providing care in a variety of home environments, recognizing that each patient’s living conditions and standards may be different from your own?

 - Can you remain calm, adaptable, and professional when faced with challenging or unexpected situations?


COMMITTED TO EXCELLENCE

 - Do you pride yourself on being reliable, dependable, and trustworthy?

 - Are you solution oriented and able to think critically when challenges arise?

 - Is your mode of transportation as reliable as you are?


TECH PROFICIENT

 - Are you proficient using Apple iPhones and iPads beyond calling and texting?

 - Are you comfortable navigating apps, electronic health records, telehealth platforms, and other digital tools?

 - Can you confidently learn and navigate new technology independently?

If you’re nodding yes, you’re off to a great start. Here are a few more things you’ll need to be successful as a Sprinter.


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - Strong phlebotomy skills, including experience with challenging sticks

 - Patient facing healthcare experience as a Phlebotomist, Medical Assistant (MA), Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN), or Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN) in home preferred

 - Current BLS certification

 - Valid driver’s license, current auto insurance, and personal, reliable vehicle

 - Availability Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–3:30 p.m.

 - Ability to drive before 7:00 a.m. to arrive at your first scheduled patient on time

 - Proficiency using Apple iPhones and iPads

 - Ability to meet applicable state specific certification or licensing requirements


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

 - Ability to lift and carry up to 25 lbs.

 - Ability to spend prolonged periods driving between patient appointments

 - Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, and carry medical supplies and equipment

 - Ability to safely navigate a variety of patient home environments, including locations with stairs

jobs.title: Associate SOC Analyst
jobs.description:
You’ve got the spark, the curiosity that makes you ask “why?” when others move on. You love solving puzzles, learning new tools, and understanding how things work (and how they break). Maybe you’ve done some hands-on IT work, tinkered with packet captures, or even caught yourself reading about the latest exploits for fun. If that sounds like you, you might be exactly who we’re looking for.

At Expel, we protect customers by thinking like attackers. Our analysts investigate alerts, dig through data, and communicate findings with empathy and precision. As an Associate SOC Analyst, you’ll be on the front lines of our Managed Detection & Response (MDR) service, helping detect, analyze, and respond to threats across diverse environments from endpoint to cloud.

This is more than an entry point, it’s a launch pad. We’ll train you, mentor you, and help you grow from your first alert triage to full-scale investigations. You’ll learn from expert analysts who’ve seen it all (and lived to meme about it). You’ll refine your craft in real-world scenarios, protecting real organizations, and making a visible impact.

What Expel Can Do For You

• Analyze and investigate alerts to identify, assess, and respond to potential threats.

• Collaborate with teammates and customer security teams to remediate incidents and strengthen defenses.

• Conduct threat hunts and root-cause analysis to uncover attacker activity.

• Take ownership of alert triage through the entire lifecycle—from detection to resolution.

• Constantly look for ways to improve how we detect, defend, and deliver for our customers.

• Participate in 24x7 rotational coverage, because attackers don’t sleep.

What You Can Do For Expel (With the help of training, of course)

• Get you out of theory and into real security operations.

• Surround you with seasoned mentors who want to see you succeed.

• Offer training, tools, and hands-on experience to accelerate your career.

• Immerse you in a collaborative, growth-minded culture that values curiosity, communication, and creativity.

• Provide transparent pay, unlimited PTO, flexible work, and up to 24 weeks parental leave.

What You Should Bring With You

• Integrity, curiosity, and a client-first mindset.

• Strong written communication, you can adapt tone and detail whether you’re messaging a teammate or writing a customer report.

• A fundamental understanding of TCP/IP, operating systems, and common network protocols.

• Experience with Windows, macOS, and Linux systems, including command-line familiarity.

• Awareness of cloud applications (O365, Okta) and cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, GCP).

• Familiarity with detection and response tools like SIEM, EDR, and IDS/IPS.

• A curiosity about attacker techniques, the MITRE ATT&CK framework, and how defenders can outsmart them.

• 1–2 years of IT or security experience is preferred, but if you’ve got passion, potential, and a compelling story, we want to hear it.

Additional notes

The base salary range for this role is between $85,000 USD and $90,000 USD + 20% bonus (paid out quarterly) & equity.

We believe in paying transparently and equitably. Your salary will ultimately be based on factors such as your experience, skills, team equity, and market data. You’ll also be eligible for unlimited PTO (which we model and encourage), work location flexibility, up to 24 weeks of parental leave, and really excellent health benefits.

We’re only hiring those authorized to work in the United States. We do not currently sponsor immigration visas.

We’re an Equal Opportunity Employer: You’ll receive consideration for employment without regard to race, sex, color, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, or on the basis of disability.

We’ll ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please let us know if you need accommodation of any kind.
