jobs.title: Staff AI Platform Engineer
jobs.description:
About Life360

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 107.7 million million monthly active users (MAU), as of September 30, 2026, across more than 180 countries.

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. By continuing to innovate and deliver for our customers, we have become a household name and the must-have mobile-based membership for families (and those friends who are basically family).

Life360 has more than 500 (and growing!) remote-first employees. For more information, please visit life360.com.

Life360 is a Remote-First company, which means a remote work environment will be the primary experience for all employees. All positions, unless otherwise specified, can be performed remotely (within the US) regardless of any specified location above.

We are AI Native

We are building an AI native company where AI is an integral part of how we build and operate. AI tool usage during interviews varies by role. You may be asked to demonstrate proficiency with AI tools, discuss how you leverage AI, or complete interview exercises without AI assistance. Your Recruiter will provide clear guidance as you move through the interview process.

Undisclosed use of AI not previously discussed with or approved by your Recruiter may impact your candidacy.

About The Team

The AI Platforms team builds the shared foundation that lets Life360 use AI quickly and safely: model access and routing, MCP gateway and connectors, the agent runtime and orchestration platform, memory and knowledge infrastructure, evals and observability, and cost controls. We work alongside AI Dev Tooling and Agentic PDLC, the teams reshaping how Life360 builds with agents, and we're extending the same foundations to power AI features for our members.

About the Job

The AI Platforms team at Life360 builds the shared foundation that enables the rapid and safe use of AI across the organization. This includes model access and routing, the MCP gateway and connectors, the agent runtime and orchestration platform, memory and knowledge infrastructure, evaluations and observability, as well as cost controls. As an AI Platform Engineer, you will play a crucial role in developing the infrastructure that supports every engineer and agent at Life360, extending it from internal productivity to member-facing product features.

In this role, you will own production components end to end, setting the technical direction for your area and transforming early momentum into established pathways that other teams will adopt. You are a builder at heart, responsible for shipping code, reviewing designs, and making pragmatic build-vs-buy decisions as the model and tooling landscape evolves. You will collaborate closely with the AI Dev Tooling and Agentic PDLC teams, which are reshaping how Life360 builds with agents, while also extending the same foundational capabilities to power AI features for our members. You will report to the Director of AI Platforms.

The US-based salary range for this position is $149,000 to $271,500 USD. We take into consideration an individual's background, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience in determining final salary. Base pay may also vary based on geographic location, with US work locations falling into one of three geographic tiers.

Total compensation is inclusive of equity compensation in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), as well as a comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, vision, financial, and other benefits.

What You’ll Do

• Establish the overarching vision and paved paths that enable teams across Life360 to adopt AI-native engineering best practices

• Build the agent runtime and orchestration platform, including identity, authorization, and audit for scheduled and unattended agents

• Operate the MCP gateway and connector infrastructure: secure brokering so agents reach internal data, APIs, repos, and SaaS tools through managed, auditable connections rather than unmanaged direct access

• Support the LLM gateway: model access and routing, authentication, rate limits, token budgets, and per-team cost attribution

• Build eval and regression infrastructure: golden datasets, offline evals, CI hooks, and result storage, with quality regression treated as a first-class alert

• Setup observability: prompt and response tracing, cost per request, quality signals, and drift detection

• Work with Security, Privacy, and Legal to build data handling, tenant isolation, and auditability into the platform from day one

• Define how product teams access, run, and monitor AI inference in production at member scale: serving, latency, reliability, and provider management

• Own what you build in production: SLOs, dashboards, deployment pipelines, and incident response

• Enable memory, retrieval, and knowledge infrastructure that agents can share

• Make the right way the easy way: SDKs, templates, reusable skills, docs, and internal champions that engineers and their agents choose to use

• Partner with AI DevX and Agentic PDLC to turn their needs into shared primitives instead of one-off builds

• Mentor engineers on agent architecture and evaluation rigor, and write design docs and standards other teams can build against

• Explore foundational memory, retrieval, and shared knowledge capabilities for agents as longer-term platform needs evolve

What We’re Looking For

• 8+ years of engineering experience, including 3+ years building platforms or infrastructure used by other engineers

• Experience building and operating production AI systems, such as agentic workflows, LLM integrations, retrieval, and evaluation

• Working knowledge of MCP and agent orchestration, including how agents connect to internal systems with appropriate controls

• Strong backend and cloud fundamentals: distributed systems, APIs, infrastructure as code, and reliability and observability practices

• Experience running AI inference in production, including latency, reliability, provider management, and cost tradeoffs

• Sound judgment on what deserves a shared platform investment and what doesn't

• Clear written communication: design docs and standards precise enough for other engineers (and their agents) to build against

Bonus Experience

• Experience with non-human identity, service-account, or agent authZ models

• Experience building or operating an agent orchestration or deployment platform, or an MCP-style connector gateway

• Familiarity with SOC 2, GDPR, or similar compliance frameworks

• Background in ML infrastructure or model observability

• Experience with consumer-scale products or privacy-sensitive data

AI-Native Expectations

We use AI coding tools as a professional standard on this team. Here's what that means in practice:

• Daily use: You use AI coding assistants (we support Claude Code, Cursor, and GitHub Copilot) for real, substantive tasks: analysis, coding, refactoring, testing, navigating codebases, and documentation. Not just research or autocomplete.

• Judgment and ownership: AI-generated code gets the same review you'd give any PR. You are accountable for everything you ship.

• Velocity: We expect senior engineers who use AI well to operate with meaningful leverage — doing more with the same time, taking on problems that would otherwise require a larger team.

• Team leadership: You share what works. You automate prompting strategies that others can build on and help teammates earlier in their AI workflow adoption get up to speed.

• Continuous learning: The tooling is changing fast. You stay current and bring recommendations to the team when something would meaningfully improve how we work.

Our Benefits

• Medical, dental, vision, life and disability insurance plans (100% paid for employees)

• Paid parental leave

• 401(k) plan with company matching program

• Mental Wellness Program & Employee Assistance Program (EAP) for mental well-being

• Generous time off: flexible PTO, companywide holidays throughout the year plus summer and winter shutdowns

• Learning & Development programs

• Equipment, tools, and reimbursement support for a productive remote environment

• Free Life360 Platinum Membership and Tile trackers

AI Usage: We use AI to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Life360 hiring teams

Life360 Values

Our company’s mission-driven culture is guided by our shared values to create a trusted work environment where you can bring your authentic self to work and make a positive difference

• Be a Good Person - We have a team of high integrity people you can trust.

• Be Direct With Respect - We communicate directly, even when it’s hard.

• Members Before Metrics - We focus on building an exceptional experience for families.

• High Intensity, High Impact - We do whatever it takes to get the job done.

Our Commitment to Belonging

Life360 is an equal opportunity employer. We don’t discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status, or any other legally protected status. We believe diverse perspectives make us better, and we’re building a workplace that reflects the communities we serve. Don’t meet every qualification? Apply anyway.

jobs.description:
Who We Are

Verkada is transforming how organizations protect their people and places with an integrated, privacy-sensitive AI-powered platform that includes solutions for video security, access control, air quality sensors, alarms, intercoms, and visitor management.

We’ve got serious momentum in the market: more than 30,000 customers (including 100+ of the Fortune 500), a $5.8B valuation, more than $1 billion in annualized bookings, and backing from CapitalG, Sequoia Capital, General Catalyst, Felicis Ventures, Next47 and more. Physical AI is one of the most consequential technology shifts of our time, and Verkada is at the center of it.

You can look at all kinds of communities to see our platform’s impact in the world. It's the retailer that uses our agentic AI to deter theft before it happens. The warehouse that uses AI-powered alerts to make sure its team is protected on the floor with proper PPE. The school that’s alerted to a threat in real-time and triggers a lockdown in seconds, not minutes. We’re rapidly scaling this impact: today, more than 2 million Verkada devices are deployed across 170+ countries.

As a Channel Sales Manager, you'll be pivotal in scaling Verkada's reach and impact by developing and managing a network of high-performing reseller partners. You'll be responsible for driving net new business through the channel—building pipeline and executing strategic plans that result in measurable growth.

This individual contributor role requires strategic thinking and hands-on execution as you collaborate across sales, marketing, and partner teams to grow Verkada’s presence in Eastern Ohio and Pittsburgh.

What You’ll Do

You’ll be at the heart of Verkada’s mission, working hand-in-hand with our sales teams to drive growth and success with channel partners. You’ll be responsible for building pipeline and generating net new business through reseller partners while executing a best-in-class channel strategy. Here’s what you’ll own:

• Drive Net New Pipeline: Proactively identify and generate pipeline with net new end-user customers through strategic reseller partners. Collaborate closely with field sales teams to co-sell and close high-value opportunities.

• Execute Regional Channel Strategy: Develop and manage a focused partner business plan for your territory that aligns with Verkada’s overall GTM objectives and quarterly sales targets.

• Empower Our Partners: Train and enable partner executives, sales teams, and technical stakeholders on Verkada’s full product portfolio, programs, and campaigns to ensure deep engagement and capability across all levels.

• Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Work closely with Verkada’s internal sales, marketing, and pre-sales teams to drive joint activities, including partner events, demand generation campaigns, and customer-facing initiatives.

• Lead with Insight: Conduct regular QBRs and ad-hoc business reviews with partners to align on priorities, track performance, celebrate wins, and identify opportunities for improvement.

• Strengthen the Channel Ecosystem: Influence partner sales teams to prioritize Verkada in key deals and business planning efforts. Leverage insights from the field to recommend improvements to Verkada’s channel tools, incentives, and partner program offerings.

• Drive Awareness and Demand: Lead and participate in regional in-person and virtual events to grow Verkada’s brand awareness, build community, and strengthen relationships with key partner contacts and stakeholders.

• Operate Strategically and Tactically: Own the full lifecycle of partner engagement in your region—from onboarding and enablement to pipeline development and revenue realization.

• This role requires regular travel, estimated to be at least 50% of the time, including both domestic and international destinations as needed. The successful candidate must be comfortable with frequent travel to support business operations, customer and partner engagements and team collaboration.

What You Bring

• Experience & Success: 4+ years of channel sales or partner management experience with a strong track record of building new business via Security Integrators or IT VAR partners. Recognition, such as President’s Club, is a plus.

• Strategic & Creative Thinking: A process-driven approach, complemented by innovative thinking to create scalable, partner-focused initiatives.

• Relationship-Builder: Ability to influence and engage across all levels—from partner sales reps to executive leadership.

• Technical Fluency: Comfortable navigating product discussions and sales operations. Proficiency in Salesforce, Excel, and business intelligence tools.

• Clear Communicator: Strong verbal and written communication skills with sharp attention to detail and a professional presence.

• Locally Based in Eastern Ohio or Pittsburgh: Open to 50% travel across Eastern Ohio or Pittsburgh to meet with partners weekly, and attend trade shows and conferences when needed.

US Employee Benefits

Verkada is committed to fostering a workplace environment that prioritizes the holistic health and wellbeing of our employees and their families by offering comprehensive wellness perks, benefits, and resources. Our benefits and perks programs include, but are not limited to:

Annual Pay Range

IronMountain Solutions is seeking an experienced Availability Project Manager (APM) with a strong mechanical maintenance background to support the United States Coast Guard Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC), Icebreaker, Buoy and Construction Tender Product Line (IBCTPL).

The ideal candidate will bring extensive hands-on mechanical experience, preferably involving marine engines, propulsion systems, gas turbines, hydraulics, or auxiliary machinery, combined with the ability to plan, coordinate, and oversee vessel maintenance and repair projects.

We are particularly interested in candidates with prior military or commercial maritime mechanical experience, including former U.S. Navy Machinist's Mates, Gas Turbine Systems Technicians, Coast Guard Machinery Technicians, Marine Engine Technicians, and other experienced mechanical maintenance professionals.

While direct engine maintenance experience is highly preferred, candidates with substantial experience in other complex mechanical systems, including hydraulics, refrigeration, HVAC, and auxiliary machinery, are also encouraged to apply.

The APM will support the planning, coordination, and execution of depot-level maintenance and repair activities for Coast Guard cutters and support vessels, working closely with government engineers, logistics personnel, contracting specialists, and commercial shipyards.

Key Responsibilities

• Plan, coordinate, and manage Coast Guard cutter maintenance availabilities from initial development through execution and closeout.

• Evaluate mechanical maintenance requirements involving propulsion engines, gas turbines, hydraulic systems, auxiliary machinery, HVAC, refrigeration, piping, and other shipboard equipment.

• Review equipment maintenance histories, casualty reports, technical manuals, and Condition Found Reports to identify repair requirements and recommend corrective actions.

• Apply practical mechanical maintenance knowledge to evaluate equipment failures, troubleshooting findings, repair recommendations, and maintenance procedures.

• Develop and review technical specifications, maintenance work packages, Statements of Work, government estimates, and repair documentation.

• Coordinate with Coast Guard engineers, maintenance personnel, shipyards, and contractors to support the successful execution of maintenance projects.

• Review engineering drawings, mechanical schematics, equipment specifications, and technical publications.

• Support procurement activities for replacement parts, mechanical equipment, and repair services.

• Monitor project schedules, milestones, budgets, and contractor performance.

• Participate in shipboard inspections, maintenance planning meetings, shipyard progress meetings, and project closeout activities.

• Utilize Coast Guard logistics and maintenance management systems, including Fleet Logistics System (FLS), Contract Workbook Database (CWD), and related databases.

• Provide technical recommendations and project status updates to government stakeholders.

• Travel to Coast Guard facilities and commercial shipyards as required.

Required Qualifications and Experience

• Minimum of five (5) years of experience supporting U.S. Coast Guard Naval Engineering maintenance practices and procedures.

• Minimum of five (5) years of ship or boat maintenance experience, including dry-docking or major maintenance availabilities.

• Minimum of five (5) years of project management experience supporting vessel maintenance, repair, modernization, or sustainment programs.

• Minimum of five (5) years conducting vessel maintenance assessments and identifying repair requirements.

• Minimum of two (2) years developing technical specifications, maintenance procedures, repair packages, or engineering documentation.

• Strong technical understanding of mechanical equipment, maintenance procedures, troubleshooting, and repair practices.

• Working knowledge of marine propulsion, electrical distribution, auxiliary machinery, piping, HVAC, hydraulics, and related shipboard systems.

• Ability to interpret technical manuals, engineering drawings, mechanical schematics, and repair specifications.

• Experience supporting procurement activities, repair specifications, or government contracting documentation.

• Experience with Coast Guard logistics systems or comparable maintenance management software.

• Strong organizational, communication, and project coordination skills.

• Ability to travel approximately three days per month.

Highly Preferred Mechanical Background

Candidates with hands-on mechanical maintenance experience in one or more of the following areas are strongly preferred:

• Marine Engines and Propulsion: Diesel engines, marine propulsion equipment, engine maintenance, troubleshooting, overhaul, and repair.

• Gas Turbine Systems: Operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of gas turbine engines and associated equipment.

• Hydraulic Systems: Hydraulic pumps, motors, valves, actuators, fluid power systems, and mechanical troubleshooting.

• Auxiliary Machinery: Pumps, compressors, mechanical drives, piping systems, and shipboard support equipment.

• Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (AC&R): Maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of shipboard HVAC and refrigeration systems.

• Heavy Mechanical Equipment: Industrial machinery, mechanical power transmission, equipment repair, and preventive maintenance.

Preferred Military and Technical Experience

We strongly encourage applications from candidates with prior military mechanical maintenance experience, particularly those who have served in positions such as:

• U.S. Navy Machinist's Mate (MM)

• U.S. Navy Gas Turbine Systems Technician (GSM/GSE)

• U.S. Coast Guard Machinery Technician (MK)

• U.S. Navy Engineman (EN)

• Marine Diesel Engine Technician

• Marine Propulsion or Power Plant Technician

• Marine Mechanical Maintenance Supervisor

• Shipboard Auxiliary Systems Technician

• Hydraulic Systems Technician

• Marine HVAC / AC&R Technician

Additional preferred experience includes:

• Previous support of the U.S. Coast Guard Surface Forces Logistics Center (SFLC).

• Depot-level maintenance planning and execution.

• Commercial shipyard maintenance and repair operations.

• Experience supporting Coast Guard cutters, icebreakers, buoy tenders, construction tenders, or comparable vessels.

• Experience transitioning from hands-on mechanical maintenance into maintenance planning, supervision, or project management.

Education

A bachelor's degree in Engineering, Marine Engineering, Naval Architecture, Engineering Technology, Project Management, or a related technical discipline is preferred.

Relevant military training, technical certifications, and extensive hands-on mechanical maintenance experience may be considered in place of formal education, where permitted by contract requirements.

Certification:

Preferred certifications include:

• Project Management Professional (PMP)

Equivalent military training and professional experience will be considered.

jobs.title: Account Executive - Enterprise, National
jobs.description:
About Thatch

For most people, health insurance is something that happens to them: a plan chosen by someone else, with little room to fit their life. Thatch is changing that. We help companies give every employee a real healthcare budget instead of a one-size-fits-all plan, so people can choose the coverage and care that works for them, and employers get predictable costs they can control.

It’s a simple idea, but making it real means solving hard problems across healthcare, payments, and technology, and we’re just getting started. We look for people who like solving complex problems, use good judgment, and are comfortable working through ambiguity. People here care deeply about our customers, take real responsibility for what gets built, and are driven by doing work that matters.

About the role

We're looking for an exceptional Enterprise Account Executive, National Accounts to help establish and scale Thatch's enterprise business nationally.

This is a strategic, hands-on sales role for someone who understands employer-sponsored healthcare, knows how to navigate complex enterprise purchasing decisions, and has experience working with leading national benefits consulting firms, including Mercer, Aon, WTW, Lockton, and Gallagher.

Success requires more than traditional enterprise sales experience. You must understand how large employers evaluate healthcare strategies, how consultants influence those decisions, and how to effectively engage both audiences. You know when to sell directly, when to engage consulting partners, and how to maintain ownership of the sales process.

You'll report to our VP of Revenue and regularly engage with Thatch's founders and executive leadership team on strategic opportunities, partnerships, and enterprise growth.

This is the first of several planned enterprise sales hires. We're looking for a proven individual contributor who is equally excited about helping build the strategy, playbook, and team we'll develop over the next two years. For the right person, this role offers meaningful opportunities for future leadership.

What you'll do

Drive National Enterprise Growth

• Build and own a national pipeline of large employer opportunities.

• Lead complex sales cycles from prospecting through contracting.

• Develop relationships with CHROs, CFOs, benefits leaders, and executive decision-makers.

• Build compelling financial and strategic business cases for Thatch.

• Navigate enterprise procurement, RFPs, legal reviews, and multistakeholder decisions.

• Deliver consistent sales performance, pipeline discipline, and accurate forecasts.

Develop Strategic Consulting Relationships

• Build relationships with Mercer, Aon, WTW, Lockton, Gallagher, and other leading consulting firms.

• Understand consultant influence, RFP processes, and employer decision-making.

• Generate opportunities through both direct employer engagement and consulting partnerships.

• Maintain direct employer relationships while working collaboratively with consultants.

• Position Thatch as a credible alternative to traditional employer-sponsored healthcare.

Bring Deep Healthcare Expertise

• Translate complex healthcare financing and benefits strategies into executive-level conversations.

• Understand fully insured, self-funded, and alternative employer healthcare models.

• Engage employers on healthcare costs, financial risk, plan design, and employee experience.

• Partner with internal finance, product, carrier, and operations teams to develop solutions.

• Guide employers and consultants through the evaluation of ICHRA and emerging healthcare models.

Help Build Our Enterprise Business

• Partner with the VP of Revenue to shape enterprise sales strategy and execution.

• Help establish target account strategies, sales processes, and consulting engagement models.

• Provide market feedback to inform product development and enterprise positioning.

• Contribute to hiring, mentoring, and developing future enterprise sellers.

• Remain accountable for individual sales performance while helping scale the organization.

Background we're looking for

Required Experience

• 5–7+ years of enterprise sales experience in employer-sponsored healthcare, insurance, or benefits solutions.

• Proven success originating and closing complex, high-value enterprise opportunities.

• Experience in one or more of the following:

• Health insurance carriers, particularly national accounts or large group.

• Third-party administrators (TPAs) or self-funded benefits administration.

• Employer benefits consulting or healthcare advisory services.

• Healthcare benefits technology and solutions, including navigation, cost management, and care delivery.

• Experience working with national consulting firms and understanding their role in employer purchasing decisions.

• Demonstrated ability to sell directly to employers and alongside consulting partners.

• Strong understanding of enterprise procurement, RFPs, contracting, and executive decision processes.

• Established credibility with senior HR, finance, and executive stakeholders.

• Strong financial acumen, executive communication, and negotiation skills.

• Willingness to travel nationally.

Experience We'd Be Especially Excited About

• Deep self-funded healthcare expertise, including ASO, stop-loss, claims experience, network strategies, and renewal economics.

• Established relationships with national benefits consultants and large employer decision-makers.

• Experience selling innovative healthcare solutions that challenge traditional insurance models.

• Familiarity with ICHRA, defined contribution benefits, or alternative healthcare financing.

• Success creating direct employer demand rather than relying exclusively on consultant referrals.

• Experience building a new market, enterprise sales motion, or go-to-market strategy.

• Interest in mentoring sellers and potentially leading an enterprise team as Thatch grows.

Who Thrives in This Role

You're a builder. You want to create an enterprise business, not simply inherit a territory and established playbook.

You understand healthcare. You know how employers, consultants, carriers, and administrators interact, and you're comfortable discussing the economics of self-funded healthcare.

You can sell directly and through partners. You value consulting relationships but know how to create demand and develop executive relationships independently.

You can sell change. You're comfortable challenging conventional thinking and guiding sophisticated employers through consequential healthcare decisions.

You operate at the executive level. You can engage a CFO on healthcare economics, a CHRO on workforce strategy, and a consultant on benefits design.

You have an ownership mentality. You're resourceful, accountable, and energized by building something new.

You want to grow. You're motivated by individual success today and the opportunity to help build and potentially lead a national enterprise sales team tomorrow.

Why Thatch

Enterprise healthcare is at an inflection point. Employers are looking for alternatives to traditional approaches that have delivered rising costs, limited flexibility, and increasingly complex benefits experiences.

Thatch is positioned to help lead that transformation.

You'll have the opportunity to work directly with our founders and executive team, shape our national enterprise strategy, influence product development, and help build a business with significant growth potential.

We're looking for someone who wants to win meaningful enterprise business today and help build the organization that will define our growth tomorrow.

What to expect

We interview rigorously based on integrity, talent, and drive; the trust we display in our teammates from day 1 is a reflection of the confidence we have in this process. We aim to evaluate the things you’ll be doing every day as best we can, and we move quickly. Here's what to expect:

• 30 minute video meeting to talk through your background and interest in Thatch

• 30-45 minute video meeting with the hiring manager to get a high level understanding of your experience and deep into your sales experience

• 30 minute video meeting to meet 3 members of the team

• 30 minute video meeting to go over a case study assignment

• 30 minute video meeting with our founders to discuss your approach to culture and our operating principles

Please note: The posted compensation range reflects On-Target Earnings (OTE), not base salary.

Estimated Compensation Range

$250,000—$300,000 USD

jobs.title: Head of People Partnership
jobs.description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

Varda has grown to about 300 people and with significant growth ahead we are hiring our first dedicated people partner. You will be a trusted advisor to our Executive Leadership team, coaching and challenging them through rapid growth and change. You will work closely with your peers in Recruiting, Finance, and Systems/Analytics, to approach our people needs from a holistic, full-cycle, employee experience mindset.

This role is not set up for you. There is no existing function or playbook, and most leaders do not yet know the value of a People Partner. You will earn credibility by solving real problems and delivering results people can see.

What You'll Do

• Advise and coach leaders. Partner with our four executives and their leadership teams on how they lead, organize, and grow. Many of our managers are leading for the first time, so you will coach on feedback, delegation, and hard conversations.

• Talent evaluation. Operationalize performance so employees grow through outcomes, not effort. Partner in talent reviews and calibration, advise on development and succession, and guide pay and promotion decisions rooted in strong performance.

• Compensation modeling. Build our compensation philosophy into day-to-day practices, guiding through changes as the market shifts. Develop leadership understanding of pay, leveling, offers, promotions, and equity.

• Resolve conflict early. Teach leaders to give direct feedback and de-escalate situations before they become employee relations issues. This is yours end to end.

• Product mindset. Start from first principles, question everything, ship small, and measure what works, iterate and deliver again.

• Collaborate across teams. Align with peer functions so everyone drives changes as one team, in the same direction, toward the same horizon line.

• Use data and AI. Sharpen your point of view with real numbers, measure impact, understand the insights and what is missing. Use AI to deliver smarter, easier and faster.

Why Varda?

• Build the Future: Varda is building a new technology and a new market, help create the people foundation so our vision becomes reality.

• Solve Hard Problems: Create capability within the organization that directly enables the company manifest.

• Ownership & Impact: Join a fast-growing, passionate team where your work directly shapes the future of space and humanity.

What You Bring

• 10+ years in HR, including business partnering to engineering or hardware organizations. Experience as a first or founding HR hire is strongly preferred.

• Deep compensation expertise and experience teaching leaders to apply it.

• Strong coaching skills, including with first-time managers and senior executives.

• Experience with talent reviews, calibration, and promotion decisions, with a bias toward outcomes.

• Credibility with technical leaders. You are practical, direct, and useful.

• First-principles thinking, comfort with ambiguity, and the self-direction to build without a roadmap.

• Skill at building relationships and aligning peers without formal authority.

• Experience in hardware, manufacturing, or deep tech is a plus.

Compensation & Location

• Salary Range: $175,000 - $225,000/per year

• This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA

• Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance

• You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

ITAR Requirements

Varda, like all employers, must ensure that its employees working in the United States are lawfully authorized to work in the U.S. Additionally, our employees are exposed to and have access to certain export-controlled items. Because our employees are provided access to export-controlled items, our policy is to only hire “U.S. persons” who are permitted to have access to our technology without an export license.

“US person” means: U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident, or protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) (i.e., individual admitted to the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum).

jobs.description:
About the Company

Transmit Security protects large enterprises from fraud and identity attacks. Our platform spans Mosaic (SaaS identity and fraud orchestration), FlexID (on-prem IAM), standalone fraud prevention and detection, and Agentic Trust, which secures AI agents that act on behalf of customers. Our technology is recognized by analysts, and our buyers are CISOs, fraud and financial crime leaders, and identity and digital channel owners. The product is ahead of the brand.

About the Role

At Transmit Security, you will help enterprises secure digital interactions through agentic trust, identity security, and fraud prevention for people and AI agents. As an IT Support & Systems Specialist, you will own end-to-end IT support for US-based and global employees, helping them stay productive in a Mac-first, cloud-based environment. You will manage onboarding, offboarding, device provisioning, troubleshooting, and the systems under your responsibility. Working closely with the global IT team, you will handle requests through our IT service management platform and improve the employee support experience.

What you’ll do

• Provide day-to-day remote IT support to employees, primarily across US time zones, ensuring fast, high-quality, and friendly service.

• Own the full employee lifecycle from an IT perspective: onboarding (device provisioning, orientation, training, etc.) and offboarding.

• Manage, prioritize, and resolve tickets and requests through the company’s ITSM system, meeting defined SLAs.

• Set up, configure, and support end-user devices, including Mac computers, iPhones, iPads, and peripherals.

• Manage Apple devices via MDM (Iru, formerly Kandji, preferred), including enrollment, configuration profiles, app deployment, and patching.

• Administer Apple Business Manager (ABM), including Automated Device Enrollment, Managed Apple Accounts, and app/license management.

• Work directly with Apple (AppleCare for Enterprise, Apple Business/account teams) on purchasing, warranty, repairs, and escalations.

• Administer Google Workspace, including users, groups, and organizational units.

• Administer and support Zoom (Meetings, Rooms, Phone), including setup, configuration, and troubleshooting.

• Track and maintain IT asset inventory, including device assignment, shipping, and recovery for remote employees.

• Create and maintain documentation, knowledge base articles, and self-service guides for end users.

• Contribute to IT initiatives and continuous improvement of processes, automation, and the employee experience.

• This role requires working hours aligned with the U.S. Eastern Time zone (EST/EDT)

What you’ll need

• 3+ years of experience in an IT support / help desk role.

• Apple Certified Support Professional (ACSP) certification or proven hands-on macOS experience.

• Hands-on experience with an Apple MDM solution and Apple Business Manager.

• Experience administering SaaS systems such as Google Workspace, Zoom, and Slack.

• Experience working with an ITSM / ticketing system.

• Proven experience providing remote support to distributed employees.

• Strong organizational skills, including IT asset management.

• Customer service oriented, with excellent communication skills.

• Experience working in a fast-paced team environment.

Compensation and Benefits:

The on-target earnings (OTE) range for this position is US$85,000 to US$110,000. Individual compensation for this role is determined based on various factors, including but not limited to qualifications, experience, location, and overall business and organizational needs.

As a full-time employee, you will be eligible to participate in the company’s health, dental, and vision plans, in accordance with the plan documents, which may be subject to change. Additional benefits include potential equity, unlimited PTO, paid sick leave, and parental leave.

jobs.title: Research Grants Coordinator
jobs.description:
ABOUT MERCOR



Mercor's mission is to organize human intelligence to power the AI economy. We're a leading AI data company, building the layer between human expertise and frontier models. Millions of domain experts on the platform are paid over $4 million per day to train frontier AI models. Mercor's APEX benchmark family measures AI's real-world impact on professional work. Mercor Enterprise brings this same infrastructure to Fortune 500 companies: helping companies capture how their best people actually work, translating that expertise directly back into agents.

 

Mercor is creating a new category of work where expertise powers AI advancement. Achieving this requires an ambitious, fast-paced and deeply committed team. You’ll work alongside researchers, operators, and AI companies at the forefront of shaping the systems that are redefining society. Mercor is a profitable Series C company valued at $10 billion. We work in-person five days a week in our San Francisco, NYC, or London offices.


About the Role
We’re looking for a Research Grants Coordinator to help run Mercor’s research funding programs. Initially, you’ll be responsible for $10m of funding.

You’ll work closely with our research team and external researchers to move promising projects from initial application through funding, delivery, and publication. You’ll coordinate the day-to-day grantmaking process, build relationships across the research community, and make sure applicants and grantees receive clear, timely support. This role suits someone who is highly organized, enjoys working with researchers, and takes ownership of getting things done.

What You’ll Do

 - Coordinate the grant process: Manage applications, organize reviews with Mercor researchers, track decisions, and keep applicants informed.

 - Outbound to grantees: Reach out to applicants and potential applicants to make them aware and keep them informed of the grants process.

 - Support grantees: Serve as the main operational contact for funded researchers, coordinating onboarding, answering questions, and connecting them with relevant people and resources.

 - Keep projects moving: Track milestones, budgets, and deliverables; follow up on progress; and flag issues early.

 - Coordinate agreements and payments: Work with legal, finance, and operations to get grants set up and funding delivered on time.

 - Build research relationships: Identify prospective applicants, support outreach to universities and research organizations, and help grow the community around Mercor’s funding programs.

 - Communicate results: Coordinate project updates, publications, and announcements, and help the team understand what funded projects have achieved.

 - Improve how we work: Build straightforward systems for tracking grants, managing communications, and reporting on program progress.

 - Organize events: Organize kickoff, checkin, and wrapup events for grantees and the wider research community.
   

What We’re Looking For

 - Experience: Ideally 2–3 years in program coordination, research operations, grant administration, consulting, or a related role.

 - Organization: Strong attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple projects, deadlines, and relationships.

 - Communication: Clear, concise writing and confidence working with researchers, applicants, and internal teams.

 - Ownership: You follow through, resolve problems independently, and know when to ask for input.

 - Research interest: Curiosity about AI research and the ability to understand and summarize a project’s goals and progress.

 - Practical judgment: Comfortable handling confidential proposals and funding information, adapting to changing priorities, and improving processes as you go.



Compensation

 - $10K proximity bonus (if you live within 0.5 miles of our office)

 - $1.5K monthly stipend for meals

 - Free Equinox membership

 - $200 monthly laundry reimbursement

 - $200 monthly personal wellness reimbursement

 - Health, Dental, Vision insurance

 - 401(k) with company match

 - Up to $15k Relocation bonus

jobs.description:
At Yondr, we believe in the power of presence. Our mission is to create phone-free spaces that deepen human connection and elevate shared experiences. We partner with artists, educators, and visionaries to design environments that put people, not devices, at the center.



Yondr’s business segments span numerous industries, primarily across education and live events. Yondr supports schools through cell phone-free programs. Our education programs facilitate the successful implementation of phone-free school environments by providing administrators and teachers with education, training, and development resources, along with all necessary equipment. In addition, Yondr supports top artists in music and comedy by creating phone-free shows, allowing performers and audience members to enjoy live performances without the distraction of phones.



POSITION SUMMARY

The Account Executive, Education is responsible for driving new business growth by developing partnerships with K–12 schools and school districts throughout an assigned territory. This role is responsible for generating new sales opportunities, managing the full sales cycle, and building trusted relationships with education leaders to advance Yondr's mission of creating phone-free learning environments.

Reporting to the Education Sales leadership team, the Account Executive serves as a consultative partner to prospective customers, identifying their needs and delivering tailored solutions that improve student engagement and learning outcomes. The ideal candidate is a proactive, relationship-driven sales professional who thrives in a fast-paced environment, enjoys building meaningful connections, and is passionate about helping schools create distraction-free spaces where students can thrive.

Business Development & Sales

Sales Operations & Collaboration

 - Participate in ongoing sales training, professional development, and product education to strengthen sales effectiveness and industry knowledge.

 - Experience in outbound prospecting, cold calling, lead generation, and pipeline development.

 - Ability to travel up to 60% to support customer meetings, conferences, and business development activities.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

 - Excellent interpersonal, communication, presentation, and negotiation skills.

 - Ability to build trust and credibility with school administrators and executive-level decision-makers.

 - Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple opportunities simultaneously.

jobs.title: Lead Toddler Teacher
jobs.description:
Help toddlers discover who they are and what they can do.

At Guidepost Montessori, our Lead Toddler Guides create calm, purposeful environments where curiosity, independence, and confidence grow every day.

If you’re passionate about early childhood development and ready to lead a classroom designed for exploration and independence, this is your opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

Your Role

As a Lead Toddler Guide, you’ll lead a mixed-age toddler classroom in a Montessori environment thoughtfully designed to support children during one of the most formative stages of development.

Montessori guides prepare beautiful, orderly environments that invite exploration and support independence. Through careful observation, individualized lessons, and respectful guidance, you’ll help each child develop language, coordination, self-regulation, and confidence.

Your leadership will empower toddlers to explore freely, make choices, and take pride in what they can accomplish laying the foundation for lifelong learning.

What You’ll Do

• Observe each child closely to understand and support their physical, emotional, and cognitive development

• Prepare and maintain a beautiful, orderly classroom that fosters focus, independence, and exploration

• Support independence by encouraging toddlers to “do it themselves”

• Provide lessons in practical life skills, language development, and grace and courtesy

• Build warm, trusting relationships with children and families

• Communicate and collaborate with parents to support each child’s growth

• Lead classroom routines and collaborate with team members to create a respectful, joyful community

The Montessori Prepared Environment

Every Guidepost toddler classroom is fully equipped with high-quality Montessori materials and designed according to the principles of beauty, order, and independence.

Our toddler environments feature:

• Open spaces that encourage movement and exploration

• Child-sized furniture and tools to support independence

• Curriculum that builds skills in dressing, feeding, and toilet learning

• Scientifically designed materials for fine and gross motor development

• Natural elements including cozy rugs, real plants, and abundant light

• Beautiful, breakable materials made from wood, metal, and glass

• Opportunities to climb, crawl, and explore without restrictive devices

What We’re Looking For

• Interest in pursuing fully sponsored Montessori certification through our Prepared Montessorian Institute, or a previously earned Montessori diploma

• Experience working with children ages 0–3 in a group care or early learning setting

• Alignment with child-led educational approaches (Montessori, Reggio Emilia, or similar)

• Required ECE or Child Development credits

• Bachelor’s degree (any field)

What We Offer

• Sponsored Montessori diploma training and ongoing professional development

• Competitive salary Salary Range: $37,000-44,000

• Health, dental, and vision insurance

• Paid time off and paid holidays

• 75% tuition discount for up to two children at any Guidepost school

• A collaborative, supportive network of peers and mentors

• Clear opportunities for career growth and leadership advancement

About Guidepost Montessori

Guidepost Montessori is a growing network of over 80 schools across the U.S. and Asia, serving children from 3 months to 6 years old in our Nido, Toddler, and Children’s House programs.

We believe children are capable and we intentionally design environments that empower them to explore, grow, and flourish. Our mission is to transform education by nurturing independence, joy, and lifelong learning.

If you’re inspired by toddler development, excited to partner with families, and ready to lead with purpose, we’d love to welcome you to Guidepost Montessori.

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer
jobs.description:
Staff Software Engineer

ROLE / DEPARTMENT OVERVIEW

Pathstream is seeking a Staff Software Engineer to lead large, cross-team technical work on our platform. This is a senior individual contributor role on one of our engineering pods. Our pods are small, fast-moving teams that own their area end to end and ship to production often. You will report to your pod's engineering lead and have no direct reports.

You will be an expert in the systems your team owns, and you will understand how data moves through the rest of Pathstream's platform. You will lead multi-person projects from design to production, set the technical bar for your pod, and help the engineers around you grow.

A core expectation of this role is the ability to advance Pathstream's AI-native engineering practices. AI adoption is already deeply embedded in how we build software at Pathstream. We are looking for a technical leader who not only embraces this approach but actively pushes the organization forward in building, evaluating, and deploying AI-enabled development tools and agentic engineering workflows. Both as a hands-on practitioner and as a force-multiplier for engineers across the org.

WHAT WE DO

Pathstream was founded on the premise that substantial unrealized economic and human potential exists within each organization's frontline workforce. We are reshaping the way employees and managers on the frontlines excel in their careers. In this age of rapid tech evolution, our enterprise partnerships transform frontline teams from transactional to relational, and from task-oriented to strategic.

We impact companies' bottom lines with improved productivity, increased retention, and differentiated quality of customer experience, while employees experience greater success in their current roles and unlock future professional growth.

We're a tight-knit, hardworking, mission-driven team of ~60 employees eager to scale our solution and transform the careers of our customers.

THE ROLE

AI-NATIVE ENGINEERING

• Own how your team delivers with AI, in addition to your own output. Reshape how projects are scoped, sequenced, and staffed now that implementation is cheaper, so the team's throughput goes up.

• Own the team's shared AI patterns as a set: context files, skills, conventions, and workflows, including ones others wrote. Keep them maintained, and retire the ones that no longer help.

• Lead adoption of new AI tools and methods in your area. Our current toolset includes Claude Code, Claude skills, MCP servers, and AI code review.

• Notice when the team's verification practices fall behind how fast code is now produced, and drive the fix end to end. Test strategy, staged rollout, and observability are part of that work.

• Make room for the team to experiment, and keep it safe to report that something did not work. Tell an experiment worth running from a distraction, and say no to distractions without killing the team's appetite to try new things.

TECHNICAL OWNERSHIP & DELIVERY

• Lead large feature releases end to end. These are usually multi-person projects that cross team boundaries.

• Take on significant, unique engineering problems where the data is incomplete and the trade-offs include intangibles. Diagnose root causes quickly and guide others through the trade-offs.

• Break complex initiatives into clear, maintainable pieces that less experienced teammates can own.

• Know when to focus on stability and quality, and when to ship quickly and iterate.

• Write architecture documents that show how systems work together and where they are weak. Review other teams' technical documents with clear, timely feedback.

QUALITY, SECURITY & OPERATIONS

• Recognize when systems or workflows need reinforcement to protect quality, and drive the solution end to end.

• Apply strong security practice in your domain. Partner with engineering leadership on SOC2, vulnerability management, and the controls that protect our enterprise customers and learners.

• Give code review that others seek out because it is thorough, helpful, and kind.

• Jump into incidents outside your normal scope in an emergency. Improve how the team detects, prevents, and responds to incidents.

COLLABORATION & MENTORSHIP

• Grow other engineers over an extended period. Tailor feedback to each person's skills, background, and working style.

• Build strong relationships with product, design, and cross-functional partners. Represent your team's technical view in conversations about scope, sequencing, and trade-offs.

• Write clear narratives that create understanding and help decisions get made. Adapt how you communicate to your audience.

• Influence hiring and help develop strong engineering talent.

ABOUT YOU

AI PRACTICE

• AI is a core part of how you work today. You can describe, with examples, how it changed the way you scope, build, and review software.

• You have built AI tooling for yourself and for others: skills, MCP servers, context files, evaluation harnesses, or multi-step agentic workflows. Other engineers adopted and kept using at least one of them.

• You have shipped AI features in production systems where an LLM is a first-class component. You have dealt with evaluation, observability, and cost.

• You verify AI output with rigor. You can name the failure modes you watch for and the checks you added to catch them.

• You keep up with the tools because you want to, not because someone asked you to. You run your own experiments, you have opinions about what works, and you share what failed as readily as what worked.

EXPERIENCE

• You bring 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, with a strong track record as a senior engineer.

• You are an expert in one or more technical areas and proficient across a broad range of others.

• You have led projects that crossed team boundaries, and you have shipped systems that other engineers depend on.

• You bring deep familiarity with modern web application stacks similar to ours: Ruby on Rails, React, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Docker, PostgreSQL, and AWS.

• You have practical experience operating production systems that hold customer data, including security and compliance work in a SaaS environment.

HOW YOU WORK

• You lead through influence. Other engineers seek you out for technical feedback because your advice is thorough, helpful, and kind.

• You are comfortable with ambiguity and shifting priorities. You make data-informed decisions when perfect information is not available.

• You stay calm under pressure and help your team through change.

• You ask for feedback and act on it. You celebrate the work of others, and you treat disagreement as a way to reach a better answer.

WHAT WE OFFER

• Transparent and social culture, challenging work, fast learning cycles, practical training, and meaningful feedback

• Strong sense of ownership and strategic work that impacts our product, users, colleagues, business, and world

• Salary and total compensation offerings are contingent upon the candidate's level of expertise and geographic location, ensuring equitable remuneration.

• Tier 1: San Francisco Bay Area and New York City: $190,000 to $220,000

• Tier 2 metropolitan markets: $171,000 to $198,000

• Tier 3 regional markets: $152,000 to $176,000

Comprehensive benefits package:

• 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision for you; 50% for partner/spouse and dependents

• Health, commuter, and parking flexible spending accounts

• Employee Assistance Program (mental health, financial health, legal support)

• Free access to wellbeing apps (Ginger, Headspace)

• Flexible paid time off and paid holidays

• Generous paid parental leave

• Short and long-term disability insurance

• Annual professional development budget

• Company-provided laptop

• Remote-first culture

• Life insurance (100% company paid)

• 401(k)

COMMITMENT TO DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION

Our company values diversity and believes diverse teams make innovation possible. We work on complex, difficult problems with no linear or clear solutions. We need a diverse team that can bring different perspectives and approaches, and whose experiences reflect the full set of stakeholders we seek to serve. Pathstream is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage all qualified applicants from any race, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or other characteristics to apply.

WORK AUTHORIZATION

Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time.

You will take full ownership of your enterprise territory end to end, driving pipeline through targeted account-based prospecting, orchestrating complex multi-threaded evaluations across the C-suite, and leading high-value engagements through security, legal, and procurement to close. This role reports to the VP of Enterprise Sales.

WHO YOU ARE

You are an accomplished enterprise sales professional with an extensive track record of winning large, complex deals in highly competitive market landscapes. You take complete ownership of your territory, proactively pairing targeted outbound prospecting and executive account mapping with inbound and partner channels to build a predictable, multi-quarter pipeline. You thrive in fast-paced environments, navigate ambiguous situations with ease, and possess the consultative authority and executive presence to engage, challenge, and align senior leadership around strategic business outcomes. Above all, you are a curious, highly motivated team player driven by continuous improvement, operational discipline, and the satisfaction of closing transformative enterprise partnerships.

• Synthesize findings into clear, concise value propositions and business cases for C-level executives to easily understand the ROI and time-to-value of implementing our solutions.

WHAT YOU’LL BRING

At Carvana, we sell cars but we aren’t car salesmen. Our promise is simple: we won’t sell a car to a customer that we wouldn’t sell to our own Mom. Period.

To make sure our cars are in first-rate condition, we’ve built multiple vehicle Reconditioning Centers around the country, where our cars are inspected, perfected, and photographed before reaching the Carvana website.

Job Title: Patient Financial Advocate

About Us

At West Cancer Center, we are dedicated to providing compassionate, patient-centered care while advancing groundbreaking research. Our team fosters collaboration, innovation, and professional growth, ensuring that every role contributes to making a difference in patients’ lives. Join us in our mission to provide comprehensive support to those navigating the challenges of cancer treatment.

Position Overview

The Patient Financial Advocate serves as the primary liaison for patients regarding financial matters throughout their care experience at West Cancer Center. This role provides support with insurance billing, coverage verification, financial assistance screening, and patient education regarding financial responsibility. Advocates work closely with patients and internal teams to ensure affordability and accessibility to care while maintaining dignity and confidentiality.

Key Responsibilities

• Serve as the primary financial point of contact for patients throughout their care

• Conduct initial and ongoing evaluations of insurance coverage and benefit verification

• Review and create estimates; explain out-of-pocket costs to patients

• Assist with financial assistance and charity application processing

• Coordinate patient needs with departments such as care support, nurse navigation, and revenue cycle

• Obtain patient signatures for ABNs or assistance applications when applicable

• Track and follow up on past due accounts and payment plans

• Refer patients to external financial resources as needed

• Utilize community resources to support non-medical patient needs

• Maintain professional and compassionate communication with patients regarding sensitive topics

• Meet or exceed productivity and collection benchmarks

• Perform all other duties as assigned

Qualifications

Education & Experience

• Minimum of 3 years of experience in medical billing, insurance verification, or financial counseling

• Familiarity with insurance rules (Medicare, commercial payers, referrals, and pre-certifications)

• Experience with a healthcare information system required

Skills & Abilities

• High-level interpersonal skills with ability to navigate difficult financial discussions

• Excellent verbal and written communication

• Critical thinking and analytical skills to assess insurance benefits and financial options

• Ability to explain insurance coverage and billing responsibilities clearly to patients

• Strong understanding of patient assistance programs and pharmaceutical assistance criteria

• Empathetic, courteous, and detail-oriented approach to patient financial counseling

Why West Cancer Center is a Great Place to Work

• Meaningful Impact: Play a direct role in supporting patients through one of the most challenging times of their lives.

• Collaborative Culture: Work alongside a multidisciplinary team of dedicated professionals committed to improving cancer care.

• Professional Development: Benefit from ongoing training, educational resources, and growth opportunities.

• Mission-Driven Environment: Be part of an organization guided by compassion, integrity, and innovation.

No nights, weekends, or holidays. Comprehensive benefits package.

Join Us

If you're passionate about helping others, especially during one of the most vulnerable times in their lives, we invite you to join the West Cancer Center team. Apply today to begin your journey as a Patient Financial Advocate and help make a lasting impact.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT SAVVY WEALTH:

Wealth management is a $545 billion industry that still runs on manual work. 75% of advisors offer no digital communication beyond email, and most still build financial plans by hand in Excel. Savvy is reinventing what it looks like to be a financial advisor. Founder Ritik Malhotra saw the fragmentation firsthand after seeking out his own advisor, and started Savvy to give independent advisors a modern, AI-native home.



Savvy is a registered investment advisor (RIA), and we partner with experienced financial advisors who want to grow without running the back office themselves. Advisors bring their book and join Savvy, running under their own brand (or ours), and Savvy earns a percentage of the assets they manage. In return, they get a true business-in-a-box: a proprietary tech platform and client portal, an in-house marketing team that helps them grow, a world-class investment management team, and a dedicated client services team that runs day-to-day operations and support. Advisors at Savvy service up to 50% more households and save 19 hours a week.



AI runs through everything we do. On the product side, Savvy Intelligence (released April 2026) is the only AI built for wealth managers that can see a client's complete financial picture. Internally, everyone at Savvy uses Claude and is encouraged to experiment with it, backed by a dedicated AI enablement team and a RevOps org building agents in-house.



The trajectory is steep and it's still early. We're a Series C company with 170+ people, $200M raised, and $100M ARR in sight this year. Inc. ranked us the No. 1 fastest-growing financial services company in America in 2026. Come build the next stage with us!



Recognition:

We're a Certified Great Place to Work and have been honored for our culture and our growth:

 - Newsweek's America's Greatest Startup Workplaces (2026)

 - Fortune Best Workplaces in New York™ (2026)

 - Great Place to Work Certified™ 
   
   


THE ROLE

Savvy is hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to lead three engineering teams building the platform where AI meets fiduciary advice. You'll inherit three established, high-performing teams, each anchored by a senior tech lead who owns day-to-day technical direction. Your job is to keep those teams shipping high-impact product and platform work, keep the engineers on them growing, and hold the technical and quality bar as we scale.



This is a hands-on management role. You're based in our NYC HQ, working in person alongside the Product Managers, Product Designers, and stakeholders who shape what we build, and you manage a fully remote engineering team across LATAM that works the same hours we do. You're the bridge between the two: translating product direction into clear technical execution, and bringing engineering reality back into how we plan. AI tooling has let our managers stay genuinely technical while they lead, and we expect the same here. You'll review the hard changes and make architectural calls, not from the sidelines.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own delivery health across three teams: predictable shipping, sane scope, and unblocking engineers fast, in close partnership with Product and Design.

 - Grow and retain a strong team: coaching, career development, substantive feedback, and keeping your engineers engaged and leveling up.

 - Drive our hiring process for these teams: raising the bar on who we bring in and running a tight, fair loop.

 - Stay hands-on with the code: review complex changes, set and hold engineering patterns and standards across product and platform work, and make architectural calls with your tech leads.

 - Champion AI tooling across the team (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and whatever's next), modeling it in your own work and raising the team's velocity with it.

 - Partner with Product and Design at HQ to shape scope and de-risk execution on high-ambiguity problems, and carry that context clearly to a remote team.




MUST HAVE

 - Experience managing remote or distributed engineering teams.

 - 3+ years managing engineers, including owning delivery, performance, hiring, and growth for a team.

 - You use AI tools aggressively in your daily workflow: Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and whatever else is useful. You're ahead of the curve on what's emerging, you stay technically proficient because of it, and you translate that into how your team builds.

 - A track record of shipping complex product and platform work end-to-end with measurable business impact, and holding the quality bar throughout.

 - Strong full-stack or platform engineering depth, enough to lead and review with credibility. We use Rails, React, Next.js, PostgreSQL, and GraphQL; you're comfortable across the stack or close gaps fast.

 - Strong system-design judgment: data models, service boundaries, failure modes, and how systems hold up at scale, applied to guiding architecture and raising the team's instincts.

 - Strong communication: you write clearly, give effective feedback, and collaborate well across functions in a startup environment, including with a remote team.

 - Based in or willing to relocate to NYC and work in person at our HQ.




NICE TO HAVE

 - You've built AI-powered features customers rely on in production: LLM integrations, agentic workflows, intelligent automations, or similar, and you understand the real tradeoffs around reliability, latency, cost, and failure modes.

 - Fintech domain knowledge: financial services, wealth management, regulatory compliance, or financial data integrations.

 - Experience leading in an early-stage, high-ambiguity startup environment.


BENEFITS:

 - Competitive salary and equity package

 - We offer a generous relocation package to help top talent make the move to our NYC office

 - Unlimited PTO + paid company holidays

 - Access to holistic medical, dental, and vision plans

 - Company 401(k) (including Mega backdoor Roth options), Commuter, and HSA/FSA plans 

 - NYC office in Union Square

 - Lunch and snacks provided in the office, & dinner if you stay late

 - Access to virtual mental health care (Spring Health) and health concierge (Rightway) to help you find the right care

 - Access to counseling for stress management, dependent care, nutrition, fitness, legal, and financial issues (Guardian WorkLifeMatters EAP)

 - Benefits are available to full-time employees

jobs.title: Tax Manager
jobs.description:
THE POSITION
Our roster has an opening with your name on it

We’re looking for an experienced indirect tax professional to join FanDuel’s Indirect Tax team.  This role will report to the Tax Director (Indirect) in a hybrid role that will be based out of our New York City office.  In this role, the Tax Manager (Indirect) will own sales and use tax compliance across FanDuel’s multi-state footprint while also serving as a technical resource on the legal principles that drive indirect tax outcomes — nexus, taxability of digital and gaming products, sourcing, and exemption certificate management.  Our ideal candidate is someone who can help the business run a clean, on-time compliance cycle and also creatively interpret and practically apply complex state and local sales tax laws, regulations, and rulings.

THE GAME PLAN
Everyone on our team has a part to play

• Own the end-to-end sales and use tax compliance cycle across FanDuel’s multi-state footprint and assist our outside advisors with return preparation and review, filings, registrations, notices, and account reconciliations — ensuring accuracy and on-time delivery.

• Research and document the legal basis for the company’s indirect tax positions using primary authority and translate that analysis into practical guidance the business can act on.

• Monitor nexus, taxability, and sourcing developments across state and local jurisdictions, including rules specific to digital goods, information services, software, subscriptions, and gaming products, and assess the impact on filings, systems, and pricing.

• Assist the Tax Legal team with indirect tax audits, notices, and Department of Revenue inquiries.

• Drive process improvements and scalable solutions across the compliance calendar, leveraging tax engines, automation, AI, and data analytics.

• Partner with cross-functional teams (Finance, Legal, Product, Tech) to ensure indirect tax is considered early in new product launches, market entries, and system changes.

• Own business controls related to indirect tax within the SOX control environment, ensuring documentation, testing, and audit readiness.

• Manage exemption certificate compliance, voluntary disclosure agreements, and refund claims, and review the work of external advisors where engaged.

THE STATS
What we’re looking for in our next teammate

• Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, economics, or a related field required

• 5+ years of indirect tax experience, with substantial time spent on multi-state sales and use tax compliance (industry, Big 4/national firm, or state revenue department)

• Demonstrated command of the legal principles underpinning sales and use tax — nexus, taxability and characterization, sourcing, bundling, and exemptions — and the ability to research and defend a position from primary authority rather than software output

• Proven ability to review and challenge complex analyses prepared by others, testing both the numbers and the technical support for the position taken

• Working knowledge of how indirect tax rules apply to digital goods, subscriptions, and other non-traditional offerings, or the ability to get there quickly

• Skilled in building stakeholder relationships across internal functions and with state tax authorities, auditors, and external advisors

jobs.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

PROPULSION ENGINEER, RAPTOR INTEGRATION

The Raptor Fleet Operations team is responsible for the fleet of Raptor Engines from the time they leave the factory in Hawthorne until the time they fly. Today, the team is focused on enabling rapid design iteration by taking lessons from flight and engine testing and applying those lessons across the fleet. In the future, the team will begin to focus on developing the processes necessary to maintain a large fleet of engines capable of continuous reuse. As a Propulsion Engineer on this team, you will serve an important role in developing the processes that will be used to maintain the fleet of engines and will be the technical interface between the hardware and RE teams. Engineers in this role demonstrate a very high level of engineering intuition, critical thinking, system level expertise, and are comfortable working under tight deadlines with loosely defined requirements and minimal oversight. Combining these skills, these engineers face challenges across a wide variety of work centers at the company and are at the forefront of developing integration and test processes for current and next generation engines.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

• Lead troubleshooting and diagnostic efforts of engine issues in the field

• Support integration and testing of R&D hardware to inform future designs and improve on engine performance and reliability

• Manage changes and upgrades to a large fleet of engines

• Develop standards and processes to increase reliability and decrease process time

• Author work instructions to address both nominal and off nominal engine work

• Interface with design, build, and systems engineering as well as production leadership and technicians in the field

• Contribute to the development the Raptor production line, and provides feedback to design engineering to maximize efficiency and minimize cost/ton to orbit

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

• Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline or physics

• 1+ years of hands-on engineering experience (design teams and previous internships qualify)

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

• Systems engineering experience, ability to understand multi-disciplinary integrated systems

• Experience creating, reading, and interpreting electrical and fluid schematics

• Experience with integration and testing of propulsion and/or electrical systems

• Experience in planning and execution of complex test operations

• Experience developing test software/automation

• Experience writing test plans, procedures and providing go/no-go judgment and rationale

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Ability to work on ladders, lifts, and at elevated heights (up to 300 feet) with proper PPE

• Ability to respond to emergencies to support priority projects, missions, and launches

• Available to work extended hours and weekends as needed based on site operational needs; flexibility is required

• Must be able to work in extreme outdoor environments when needed – heat, cold, wind, rain, etc.

• Must be able to work in an environment requiring exposure to fumes, odors, and noise

• Must be willing to travel to other SpaceX sites when needed (up to 20%)
