jobs.title: Warehouse Associate/Truck Driver
jobs.description:
We are looking for a Warehouse Associate/Driver to join our RES team located in Indianapolis, IN!

Summary:

Employee’s level and pay will be dependent on their level of experience, knowledge, and capabilities. The Warehouse Associate/Truck Driver I is responsible for efficiently and accurately filling customer orders, receiving, stocking, staging, and shipping material in a manner that meets company standards for safety, security, accuracy, and productivity. Responsible for all warehouse transactions, as well as the upkeep and maintenance of the branch warehouse environment and equipment. This role also has an essential driving component and may be assigned to operate a delivery vehicle for up to 50% of its time delivering products to/from customers, company branch/warehouse locations, and company suppliers in a delivery van or box truck (No CDL required). Responsible for ensuring that deliveries are prepared to meet customer requirements in the most efficient manner and materials are correct and free of damage.

What You'll Do:

• 7am-4pm
• Contribute to a culture and environment focused daily on employee safety and a safe work environment
• Follow established Standard Operating Procedures, Environmental Health and Safety Rules, and immediately address safety concerns
• Receive material coming into the building by vendors, customers, or other warehouses and verify the quantity and description of materials received by checking merchandise against the packing list
• Keep incoming orders stocked on shelves orderly and in designated area and report freight damage claims
• Prepare branch orders from the warehouse and ensure that the correct number and type of product is being shipped
• Process paperwork regarding shipments including but not limited to verifying that the merchandise to be shipped is correct, applying the correct postage tape and label, following customer shipping instructions, and insuring the shipment when necessary
• Operate machinery including forklift, reach truck, and wire cutting machine when required
• Load common carrier and company vehicles
• Inspect and perform minor maintenance on equipment
• Perform inventory counts and reconcile any discrepancies
• Operate delivery vehicles to make deliveries to and from customers, company branch/warehouse locations, and company suppliers
• Inspect company vehicle for visual and operating defects; responsible for completing a daily inspection report
• Keep company vehicle clean, serviced, and maintained; alert supervisor of repair and/or service needed
• Must follow Department of Transportation (DOT), local and state driving laws and regulations
• Load or unload vehicle and ensure all material for each order is correct (quantity and type of material) and that material is free of damage before departure
• May assist in preparing orders for delivery
• Ensure all appropriate documentation is thoroughly completed at the time of delivery, including delivery receipt is signed by the customer, packing list and branch/warehouse manifest
• Pick up material returns from customers; responsible for inspecting the condition of the material and verify quantities and catalog numbers
• Pick up material from company suppliers
• Participate in the training of entry level Truck Drivers and provide mentorship and coaching
• May be required to perform other job functions within a branch when required including but not limited to counter sales and customer support
• Perform other duties as assigned

Job Duties Disclaimer:

The information contained in this job description is intended to describe the essential job functions required of those assigned to this job. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, knowledge, skills, and abilities needed to perform the job. Please note that management retains the right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. The ability to competently perform all the essential duties of the position, with or without reasonable accommodation, demonstrate commitment to effective customer service delivery, integrity, and the ability to work productively as a member of a team or work group are basic requirements of all positions at Rexel USA.

What You'll Need

• No experience required
• Prior warehouse experience a plus
• Certification to operate forklift, hand truck, pallet jack, and other warehouse equipment preferred
• Must have a valid driver's license
• Must be at least 21 years of age
• Must pass a pre-employment and annual review of the Motor Vehicle Record
• Must obtain verification of non-expired medical certificate as required by law within 30 days of hire
• Must not have had a suspended driver's license for a traffic accident/violation within the past 3 years
• Must not have any at fault accidents in the past 3 years
• High School or GED - Preferred

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

• General knowledge of electrical products a plus
• Basic computer knowledge
• Ability to effectively communicate with co-workers and customers
• Ability to handle basic issues and problems
• Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations to accurately complete job tasks
• Ability to organize and prioritize job tasks and requirements
• Excellent organizational and time management skills
• Ability to meet deadlines
• Ability to handle loads with a combine weight not to exceed 26,000 GVW
• Strong knowledge of safety regulations and be familiar with traffic and driver laws
• Willingness to adhere to assigned routes, schedules, safety procedures, and transportation laws
• Ability to work overtime as needed

Physical Demands:

• Sit: Must be able to remain in a stationary position - Occasionally – up to 20%
• Walk: Must be able to move about inside/outside office or work location - Constantly – at least 51%
• Use hands to finger, handle, or feel: Operates a computer and other office machinery - Constantly – at least 51%
• Stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl: Must be able to crouch down to stock shelves, pick up boxes, or position oneself to maintain computers in the lab/under desks/in server closet - Constantly – at least 51%
• Climb or balance: Must be able to ascend/descend on a ladder, forklift, pallet jack, or other warehouse equipment - Constantly – at least 51%
• Talk, hear, taste, smell: Must be able to use senses to effectively communicate with co-workers and clients and detect hazardous conditions - Constantly – at least 51%

• Up to 25 pounds - Constantly – at least 51%
• Up to 50 pounds - Constantly – at least 51%

jobs.title: Head of Ecosystem

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We aim to empower developers by providing a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

We're looking for a Head of Ecosystem to lead the teams that make Supabase the backend for the platforms and tools developers already use. That covers AI app builders and coding agents, integrations with the developer tools teams rely on, and the Supabase Marketplace. You'll build this org from the ground up and shape how Supabase extends beyond its own platform.

You'll also drive hiring, onboarding, and career development while maintaining high engineering standards.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN:

 - Set and maintain clear roadmaps that balance partner needs with platform priorities

 - Partner with Product, Partnerships, and Sales to define and execute our ecosystem strategy

WHAT YOU BRING:

 - Experience building and running platform, API, or integration surfaces that third parties depend on in production

 - Technical credibility with partner engineering teams, and the judgment to say no

 - Experience building teams or an org from a small base, including hiring and developing engineering managers

 - Strong organizational and execution skills: setting roadmaps, driving accountability, and keeping teams moving under uncertainty

 - Experience managing remote, globally distributed teams

 - Collaborative, low-ego, and adaptable

Bonus points if you:

 - Have experience with OAuth, platform APIs, or app marketplaces

 - Have worked on a developer platform's partner or app ecosystem

 - Have worked with AI app builders or coding agents


WHAT WE OFFER

ABOUT THE TEAM

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

jobs.title: Principal Engineer, Privacy
jobs.location: Remote-Friendly (Travel-Required) | San Francisco, CA | Seattle, WA | New York City, NY
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is working on frontier AI systems that handle sensitive information at enormous scale. How we protect that data, and how we build privacy into our systems rather than bolting it on afterward, is central to our mission of building AI that is safe and beneficial.

As one of our principal privacy engineers, you will be among Anthropic's most senior individual contributors on privacy. You will set technical strategy for how personal data is handled across products, research, and infrastructure, and execute the hardest parts of delivering it. You'll work at the intersection of privacy engineering, distributed systems, and AI safety, on problems without established answers. You will lead through influence, quality of thinking, and trust rather than formal authority.

Key responsibilities

• Define and drive technical strategy and architecture for major areas of privacy, spanning product surfaces, research and training data, internal tooling, and multiple clouds

• Identify and lead the highest-complexity, company-critical privacy initiatives, guiding engineers across many teams. Be comfortable building the most difficult pieces yourself

• Architect the primitives that make privacy the default and the safe path the fastest one: data discovery, classification, lineage, purpose-based access control, audit, retention, deletion, and export

• Turn regulatory, contractual, and consent obligations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, the EU AI Act) into enforced, continuously verified technical controls in partnership with Legal, Policy, and Compliance team

• Anticipate where AI capabilities, regulation, and customer expectations are heading, and position our systems ahead of them

• Mentor and develop staff and senior staff engineers, raise the bar for privacy design across engineering, and help hire senior privacy talent

• Represent Anthropic's privacy engineering to customers, regulators, standards bodies, and the research community

Minimum qualifications

• A track record of operating as a Principal engineer or equivalent: setting technical direction that multiple teams adopted, and delivering company-critical, multi-year initiatives

• Deep experience applying privacy engineering principles in production systems with a large user base, including privacy by design, data minimization, and purpose limitation

• Experience architecting data governance infrastructure (classification, lineage, access control, retention, or deletion) across distributed systems and cloud infrastructure at scale

• Proficiency in Python, Go, or similar languages; you are effective writing design docs, making architectural calls, and coding in critical paths

• Understanding of privacy regulations such as GDPR and CCPA, and the ability to work as a peer with legal and policy experts to turn requirements into technical designs

• Written and verbal communication that builds alignment across engineering, research, legal, and product teams, up to senior leadership

Preferred qualifications

• Experience building privacy infrastructure or controls for machine learning or AI systems, including training data governance or AI agents

• Hands-on experience with privacy-enhancing technologies (e.g., differential privacy, homomorphic encryption, secure enclaves, secure multi-party computation)

• Experience establishing or re-architecting a privacy engineering practice under enterprise-customer or regulatory scrutiny

• Experience briefing executives, auditors, regulators, or enterprise customers on privacy risk, and defending your recommendations under challenge

• A history of growing engineers into Staff-level and more senior roles

• Contributions to open-source privacy tooling, privacy research, or industry standards

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

$485,000—$625,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

About the Opportunity

jobs.description:
Primary Function of Position

The Future Forward group within Intuitive Surgical is seeking a Senior Mechanical Engineering Technician to support early-stage R&D of next-generation flexible energy delivery instruments and accessories. This is a hybrid role: you’ll build and iterate functional prototypes from early engineering concepts, and you’ll also support dosimetry-focused testing (benchtop, ex vivo, and in vivo) to help the team understand the energy dose delivered to tissue and resulting tissue effects. The candidate should be comfortable working with minimal supervision, and with minimal work instructions and be able to take ideas from R&D engineers and figure out how to build fully functional instrument prototypes. The ideal candidate is hands-on, detail-oriented, comfortable with minimal supervision, and able to translate rough direction into reliable builds, experiments, and data.

Essential Job Duties

• Builds and refines medical device components and catheter assemblies and provide input for the catheter assembly.
• Assisting with all aspects of early prototype builds, including procurement of material, inspection of materials and subassemblies, rework of components, assembly, troubleshooting, and repair of prototype instruments.
• Prepare instruments/electrodes/fixtures/tissue samples and run experiments from approved protocols.
• Support preclinical lab evaluations (including in vivo), equipment setup, and procedural assistance as needed.
• Perform tissue handling and histology prep activities (orientation/inking/trimming, fixation, cassette prep, labeling, sample tracking); coordinate outsourced histology and perform cryosectioning when applicable.
• Assisting engineers in benchtop and excised tissue lab evaluations of prototypes
• Collecting, recording, and reporting test results.
• Preparation of prototype instruments and accessories for benchtop testing and pre-clinical lab evaluations, organizing, overseeing, and collaborating with other groups to assemble and test prototypes.
• Setup, organization, and maintenance of engineering lab and equipment.
• Documenting assembly procedures and training other technicians on assembly.
• Assisting in knowledge transfer to other groups / teams.

Required Skills and Experience

• 5+ years R&D technician experience in medical device development
• Minimum Associate of Science degree, or equivalent work experience
• Strong hands-on prototyping/assembly skills and comfort working from limited work instructions.
• Hands-on skills and knowledgeable in prototyping and manufacturing methods, including soldering, microscopic wire and cable stripping, use of rotary tools, drills, small hand tools and adhesive bonding.
• Knowledge of catheter materials and manufacturing processes including laminating, braiding, bonding, flaring, tipping.
• Manual dexterity to assemble small components, with microscope or similar magnification.
• Experience running benchtop and/or tissue-based testing; comfortable in an animal lab environment.
• Experience with tissue prep for histology and meticulous sample/data record keeping.
• Proficiency with Excel/Word/PowerPoint; familiarity with ImageJ or similar image analysis tools.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Cryosectioning and outsourced histology submission experience.
• Basic electrical measurement experience (multimeter/oscilloscope) and metrology tools (calipers/micrometers/vision)
• Knowledge of medical grade adhesives.
• Ability to inspect components using metrology equipment (including calipers, micrometers, vision systems, CMM).
• Computer skills in Microsoft Office required, SolidWorks experience desirable.
• Excellent organizational skills.
• Able to work independently.
• Strong design to learn and apply new technology.

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

The Senior Space Build Reliability Engineer partners closely with the design and manufacturing teams to right-size processes and controls to enable scaling the production of spacecraft hardware. Build Reliability Engineers ensure production processes yield verified, reliable hardware at rate. You will flex beyond Build Reliability to support Quality, Flight Reliability, and Mission Assurance. The ideal candidate is a responsible, collaborative, process-oriented engineer with hands-on hardware design/test/manufacturing/troubleshooting experience.

Responsibilities

• Contain suspect or known non-conforming product, providing guidance to quality inspectors, technicians, shop supervisors, and engineers.

• Lead failure investigations in production, test, and operation; identifying and mitigating immediate and underlying root causes to reduce risk and improve the reliability of designs and processes.

• Provide critical peer review of hardware during design reviews and acceptance and qualification test campaigns.

• Perform failure modes and effects analyses, build requirements compliance matrix tools, and ensure adequate test coverage, change management, and manufacturability of flight hardware.

• Own vehicle level deliverables for regulatory bodies including requirements compliance, functional or flight hazard analyses, and verification evidence.

• Support Mission Assurance's vehicle level risk management and identification/tracking/execution of mitigations.

Basic Qualifications

• Bachelor's degree in aerospace, computer science, electrical, manufacturing, mechanical, or material sciences engineering.

• 5+ years professional experience in aerospace, design, quality, or related engineering role.

• Hands-on hardware test, qualification, troubleshooting, or failure analysis experience.

• Commitment to lean quality principles without compromising safety or reliability.

• Demonstrated application of process controls in high volume manufacturing, test, and quality environments.

• Experience generating, processing, and/or analyzing data for production insight.

• Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, with a drive to innovate and improve reliability in cutting-edge technology.

Preferred Skills and Experience

• Full project lifecycle ownership experience (cradle-to-grave).

• Proficiency with quality tools such as measurement systems analysis, design of experiments, statistical process control, root cause analysis and corrective action, advanced product quality planning (APQP), metrology, process failure mode and effects analysis (PFMEA), control plans, and various problem-solving approaches.

• Hands-on knowledge of CNC machining, additive manufacturing, casting, welding, fastening, or other special manufacturing processes.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Production Finance team is responsible for overseeing the financial execution of our manufacturing organization. We are the intersection between engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and finance as it relates to production; we leverage data and business relationships to drive towards the best financial outcome for Anduril. You get to partner with Anduril’s functional and business leaders by providing key insights on demand signals, production attainment, resource allocation, and Product profitability.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Senior Financial Analyst with 2-4 years of experience to join our Production Finance team. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in financial modeling, experience in manufacturing or operations environments, and can build firm business relations with internal customers. This individual will directly own financials as well as budget control for a given product portfolio, guiding strategic decision-making, and optimizing financial performance. The successful candidate will play an active role in shaping strategy rather than functioning solely as a service provider – the deeper you go the better your results.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

• End-to-end financial management of production execution: including, but not limited to, headcount, cash/working capital, demand planning, standard costing, production attainment, inventory analysis, and managing product margins.

• Establish transparency into unit economics and material cost for existing and future Anduril products.

• Work cross-functionally with Production, Supply Chain, Demand Planning, Quality, and Division Finance teams to own costing models, business case analyses, and decision-making frameworks.

• Perform in-depth quantitative analyses including variance analysis (actuals vs. plan), trend analysis, scenario modeling, and root-cause investigations to identify performance drivers and risks.

• Develop complex financial models to assess various financial scenarios and support strategic initiatives.

• Identify and implement process improvements to streamline FP&A activities and enhance reporting accuracy.

• Support the development of leadership reporting and present financial insights to senior management.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field; MBA/ technical background (Manufacturing/ Supply Chain/ Operations/ Service) is a plus.

• You have 2-4 years of experience in manufacturing finance, operations finance, business unit finance, cost accounting, investment banking, or similar.

• You have a strong understanding of financial and accounting concepts.

• Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to convey complex financial information in an understandable manner.

• You have strong analytical aptitude and take ownership. You intuitively think about problems in terms of numbers. You are able to quickly execute analyses in Excel & translate findings to business partners You are comfortable using corporate systems (e.g. Oracle, Salesforce) and analytic / dashboarding tools (e.g. Palantir Foundry)

• You are comfortable communicating broadly and having a lot of eyes on your work. This role can at-times require comms to large groups and senior leadership.

• You enjoy working at a place where no one minds if you leave early one day to go to an appointment or run an errand, but you also don’t mind responding to Slacks in the evening while you’re watching Netflix.

• Must be authorized to work in the United States.

US Salary Range

$76,000—$101,000 USD

The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:

Benefits

At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

• No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

• Please always verify communications: Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address. Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

• Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

• What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Data Privacy

To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.

By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

jobs.title: Manager, Audience Insights and Impact
jobs.description:
FIXED-TERM FULL-TIME JOB VACANCY
MANAGER, AUDIENCE INSIGHTS AND IMPACT
AUDIENCE ENGAGEMENT DIVISION
Location: London, Berlin, Brussels, Stockholm or Amsterdam
Application Deadline: 22 November 2026

Human Rights Watch (HRW) is seeking a Manager, Audience Insights and Impact to help us better understand our global audiences and strengthen the reach and impact of our communications.

Combining audience research, data analysis, and impact measurement, the successful candidate will turn data into actionable insights that shape editorial decisions, distribution strategies and advocacy communications around our human rights work.

You will establish consistent measurement and reporting practices across HRW’s outreach efforts, helping communications teams understand not just how our content performs, but who it reaches, who it doesn’t, how audiences respond, and what we need to adapt to drive increased ambition and impact.

This fixed-term one-year role is new and sits within the Audience Engagement division of HRW's Communications Department, reporting to the Associate Director of Audience Engagement, and will work closely with colleagues across the Communications Department.

Candidates must be based within commuting distance of HRW's offices in Amsterdam, Berlin, Brussels, London or Stockholm and able to work from their local office as needed.

Responsibilities:

Audience Insights

• Lead audience research and analysis, using quantitative and qualitative methods to understand priority audiences, their needs, behaviors, and information habits.

• Analyze performance across HRW's communications outreach, including earned media, website, social channels, video, newsletters, and other digital products.

• Translate findings into recommendations for distribution strategies across functions, including content choices, formats, and channels.

• Identify changes in audience behavior and the media landscape that affect HRW’s communications, including search, AI-driven discovery, and emerging platforms.

Measurement and impact

• Develop shared KPIs, benchmarks and measurement frameworks aligned with HRW’s communications objectives across channels and languages.

• Evaluate priority investigations, reports and campaigns using performance data and qualitative evidence; work with colleagues – including in Advocacy and Research – to assess communications’ contribution to wider outcomes.

• Support practical testing and experimentation, ensuring lessons inform future editorial and campaign planning.

Reporting, systems and collaboration

• Build and maintain dashboards and concise reporting that bring together earned-media, web, social, video, and email insights, with clear recommendations for teams and leadership.

• Improve tracking, tagging, data quality and reporting standards; provide analysis for priority campaigns and donor or fundraising requirements.

• Work with managers, editors and outreach colleagues to embed insights into decision-making; strengthen data literacy through guidance and training.

• Work with vendors and colleagues to improve analytics tools and promote responsible, privacy-conscious use of audience data.

Qualifications:

Education:  A bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent professional experience.

Experience: At least five years’ relevant experience in audience insights, digital analytics, communications research, impact evaluation, or a related field.

Essential Skills

• Strong quantitative and qualitative analytical skills, including audience research, segmentation and interpretation of performance metrics.

• Experience with Google Analytics 4, social media analytics and data visualization or dashboard tools (e.g. Data Studio, Power BI or Tableau).

• Ability to develop KPIs, explain the limits of impact evidence and communicate findings clearly to non-specialists.

• Excellent writing, presentation, collaboration and project management skills; fluency in English and commitment to HRW’s mission.

Desired Skills

• Experience in advocacy impact evaluation or monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL), and in multilingual or multi-market analysis.

• Familiarity with media-monitoring or listening tools, Sprout Social, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, SQL or other advanced analysis tools.

• Proficiency with traditional media and PR tracking tools such as Meltwater, PRNewswire, Cision, TalkWalker, and Newswhip.

• Experience in project management software such as Asana, Monday.com or similar products.

• Knowledge of digital discoverability, experience managing research or analytics vendors, or proficiency in an additional HRW language.

Other: Applicants for this position must possess valid work authorization for the location where they wish to be based.

Salary and Benefits: HRW seeks exceptional applications and offers competitive compensation and employer paid benefits.

How to Apply: Please apply by 22 November 2026, by visiting our online job portal at careers.hrw.org and attaching a resume and cover letter, preferably as a PDF file.

No calls or email inquiries, please. Only complete applications will be reviewed, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

If you are experiencing technical difficulties with your application submission, or if you require a disability-related accommodation, please email recruitment@hrw.org. Due to the large response, application submissions via email will not be accepted and inquiries regarding the status of applications will go unanswered.

Human Rights Watch is strong because it is diverse. We actively seek a diverse applicant pool and encourage candidates of all backgrounds to apply. Human Rights Watch does not discriminate on the basis of disability, age, gender identity and expression, national origin, race and ethnicity, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, or criminal record. We welcome all kinds of diversity. Our employees include people who are parents and nonparents, the self-taught and university educated, and from a wide span of socio-economic backgrounds and perspectives on the world. jobs.title: Office Coordinator

Office Coordinator

Dome Construction | Full-Time | Hourly / Non-Exempt

Help make great things happen behind the scenes.

At Dome Construction, we know that building great projects starts with having great people behind them. We're looking for an organized, resourceful, and people-oriented Office Coordinator who takes pride in creating a welcoming, well-run workplace where employees and visitors feel supported.

This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys variety in their day, takes initiative, and genuinely likes being the person others can count on. From coordinating meetings and company events to managing office operations, supporting employees, and keeping everything running smoothly, you'll play an important role in the day-to-day experience of our team.

If you're someone who enjoys staying organized, solving problems, juggling multiple priorities, and making things happen, we'd love to meet you!

What You'll Do

No two days will look exactly the same. You'll be at the center of our office operations, helping keep things organized, welcoming, and running efficiently. Your responsibilities will include:

Office Operations & Administration

• Coordinate incoming and outgoing mail, packages, deliveries, and shipments.

• Manage document filing, administrative records, and office communications.

• Monitor office emails, Teams messages, and phone calls, helping route questions and requests to the right people.

• Provide general administrative support to employees and departments across the company.

Workplace & Facilities Coordination

• Help maintain an organized, functional, and welcoming office environment.

• Keep kitchen, coffee, and common areas stocked and presentable.

• Monitor office supplies, place orders, and coordinate maintenance requests.

• Work with property management and service providers to address office needs across multiple Dome locations.

Meetings, Events & Employee Support

• Coordinate food and beverage orders for meetings, trainings, field lunches, and company events.

• Help organize meeting spaces, invitations, reservations, and event logistics.

• Welcome visitors and serve as a friendly, helpful first point of contact.

• Assist employees with everyday office needs, including supplies, printing, shipping, and workplace access.

• Support new hire orientation, onboarding and offboarding logistics, and employee workplace setup.

Vendor & Purchasing Coordination

• Serve as a point of contact for office vendors and service providers.

• Coordinate deliveries, service appointments, maintenance, and pickups.

• Purchase office, kitchen, meeting, and event supplies.

• Troubleshoot vendor or delivery issues and follow through to resolution.

Business Support & Special Projects

• Assist with administrative documentation, records management, and internal processes.

• Support Accounting, Payroll, and other departments with administrative needs.

• Help maintain office procedures and standard operating documentation.

• Participate in special projects, reporting, and process improvement initiatives as organizational needs evolve.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who is proactive, dependable, and enjoys being part of a team. You don't have to know everything on day one, but you should be comfortable taking ownership, figuring things out, and jumping in wherever help is needed.

Ideally, you bring:

• A high school diploma or equivalent; some college coursework is preferred.

• At least 2 years of administrative, office coordination, workplace services, or related experience preferred.

• Experience coordinating vendors, meetings, events, or office services.

• Proficiency in Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Microsoft Teams.

• Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities.

• Excellent communication and customer service skills, with a welcoming and solutions-oriented approach.

• Attention to detail and a commitment to following through.

• The ability to work independently, adapt to changing priorities, and respond to unexpected needs.

• The ability to learn new systems and processes quickly.

• A notary commission is preferred, or a willingness to obtain one.

This position also requires occasional local travel between Dome offices and nearby vendors, so a valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and appropriate vehicle insurance are required.

Why Dome Construction?

At Dome, our people are what make us who we are. We're proud of the relationships we build, the work we do, and the collaborative culture we've created along the way.

Joining Dome means becoming part of a team where people support one another, take pride in their work, and understand that every role contributes to our success. jobs.title: Biologist II
jobs.description:
AECOM is actively seeking a highly motivated Biologist for remote employment. This position would predominantly support a large gas and electric utility in the southern California region with a focus on Natural Resources.  This position is a remote  adjunct position, with hours ranging between 30 and 36 hours per week. This position would provide coordination and natural resources expertise for construction projects, supporting the projects from the design phase, through construction, to the post-construction phase. Activities may include, but are not limited to, desktop analysis, coordination with internal and external stakeholders, issuing work to consultants, review of reports, compliance documentation, direct coordination with construction personnel, and implementation of their programmatic Environmental permits.

Responsibilities will include:

• Performing desktop assignments that require background in wildlife ecology, botany, and aquatic resources.
• Supporting writing assignments, including completing or reviewing survey and monitoring reports.

• Possessing some knowledge of major state and federal agencies (e.g., USACE, USFWS, BLM, BOR, CDFW, RWQCB, and CCC) and major regulatory frameworks (e.g., NEPA, CEQA, ESA, CESA, CFGC, CWA and CCA as well as knowledge of regional conservation planning (i.e., MSCP, MHCP, MSHCP) and apply to assigned tasks.
• Working under the supervision of an AECOM project manager and senior-level client team member.
• Coordinating with design and construction personnel regarding constraints and scheduling.
• Coordinating with biologists to schedule job walks, biological surveys, biological monitoring, and post-construction reports.
• Ensuring assigned tasks stay on schedule and budget.

Note that this position is a contract-specific hire with expected duration through February 2029 (but is dependent on client authorization of contracted work and contingent on contract terms and conditions).

While this position would predominantly support the adjunct role described above, there is potential to support other clients and projects with a multitude of tasks, including biological resources assessments, writing or coordination assignments, and/or data management. This position may also support proposal preparation under the direction of a senior biologist.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s Degree in related field (biology, ecology, etc.) + 2 years of experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education
• A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records check.

Preferred Qualification

• Experience working with gas and electric utility companies.
• Experience with flora and fauna in California.
• Prior consulting experience.
• Ability to work in a fast-paced work environment where changing client priorities result in the need to determine creative ways to get the job done.
• Candidate must be flexible and willing to support multiple projects as needed.
• The ability to work independently and as part of a team; be innovative and a problem solver.
• Writing and reviewing biological technical reports.
• Desktop biological and aquatic resources constraints analysis.
• Data management experience, including electronic data collection in field, managing large data sets, programming, and/or web development, including experience with field data collection tools such as ArcGIS Field Maps and Fulcrum.
• Experience with protocol and general wildlife surveys, special-status plant surveys, habitat assessments, and/or wildlife tracking.
• Proficiency in Microsoft Office: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; Ability to create and maintain tracking spreadsheets and documents.

• Sponsorship is not available for this position.

jobs.description:
Urschel, a 100% employee-owned company, is seeking an energetic and service-focused Runner to join the Food & Beverage team at the Grand Gardner Hotel. The Grand Gardner Hotel is an Urschel Development property located in downtown Valparaiso, Indiana. Urschel Development is a wholly owned subsidiary of Urschel Laboratories in Chesterton, Indiana.

The Grand Gardner Hotel is an independent boutique hotel featuring 58 guest rooms and suites, a speakeasy, banquet space, and welcoming shared spaces. As part of our employee-owned culture, every team member contributes to the hotel's success. We believe that excellent guest experiences are the result of employees who understand how their work impacts guests, coworkers, and the overall operation of the business.

At Grand Gardner Hotel, we value teamwork, accountability, and pride in a job well done. Whether serving guests directly or supporting operations behind the scenes, each employee-owner plays an important role in maintaining the high standards that define our property.

Why You’ll Love Working at the Grand Gardner Hotel:

• Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP), Stock Issued Annually

• Accrued Paid Time Off & Holiday Pay

• Health, Dental, & Vision Insurance

• Free Health Clinic (Available to Employees and Their Dependents)

• 401(k) with Employer Matching

• Free Life Insurance

• Hotel stay and on-property dining discounts

• Flexible scheduling whenever possible

• Free 24/7 Access to An Onsite Workout Center with Personal Trainers @ Urschel’s Chesterton Facility

• Professional Development Support

• Support for Community Involvement/Philanthropy

The Runner serves as a vital connection between the kitchen, bars, and guests, ensuring food and beverages are delivered accurately, efficiently, and with exceptional presentation. This position plays an important role in creating memorable dining experiences by supporting servers, bartenders, chefs, and banquet staff while maintaining seamless communication between the front and back of house. Runners help uphold the Grand Gardner Hotel's commitment to hospitality by anticipating guest needs, maintaining service standards, and contributing to a smooth and enjoyable dining experience across Little Gem, The Honor Roll, Bar 101, banquets, and room service operations.

The ideal candidate is dependable, attentive, and passionate about hospitality. Successful candidates thrive in fast-paced environments, enjoy working as part of a team, and take pride in delivering exceptional guest experiences. Candidates should possess strong communication skills, excellent attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm and organized during busy service periods. Previous restaurant, food runner, banquet, hotel, or guest service experience is preferred. Candidates with experience working with point-of-sale systems, food safety standards, and elevated dining service will be especially successful in this role.

What You'll Do

• Deliver food and beverages promptly and accurately while maintaining presentation standards.

• Verify guest orders, dietary restrictions, garnishes, and plating quality before food leaves the kitchen.

• Describe menu items, ingredients, accompaniments, and preparation methods when delivering dishes.

• Support service teams by clearing tables, resetting place settings, and maintaining dining room appearance.

• Anticipate guest needs and assist with requests such as refills, extra napkins, condiments, and service items.

• Communicate effectively between the kitchen and front-of-house teams to ensure smooth and efficient service.

• Assist servers, bartenders, barbacks, chefs, banquet staff, and room service operations as needed.

• Support dining room and expo line setup before service and complete cleaning and closing duties after service.

• Polish silverware and glassware, stock service stations, and maintain organized work areas.

• Follow food safety, cleanliness, and hospitality standards throughout each shift.

• Support banquet events, private functions, and special hotel events as business needs require.

• Work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays.

Physical Requirements

• Remain standing and walking for extended periods, including frequent movement throughout the property.

• Frequently lift, carry, push, and move items weighing up to 50 pounds.

• Carry multiple plates and service items while maintaining balance and presentation standards.

• Bend, reach, twist, crouch, and navigate stairs throughout the shift.

• Work efficiently in fast-paced restaurant, banquet, and bar environments with moderate noise levels.

• Maintain a professional and guest-focused demeanor during busy service periods

jobs.title: Commercial Counsel
jobs.description:
ABOUT CROSBY

Crosby is built on a simple conviction: a great legal system is the watermark of a great society — and the best legal work comes from combining human expertise with the right technology, not replacing one with the other.

Crosby is the first AI-native law firm, helping ambitious companies like Cursor, Ramp, and Cognition sign commercial contracts faster.

Legal work is both art and science, and we're mapping the frontier between the two — codifying what can be systematized, amplifying human judgment where it matters most. That's why the right way to bring AI into law isn't to sell software and walk away. It's to own the outcome together: higher-quality work, delivered faster. We build proprietary tools and human-in-the-loop workflows that change what's possible for corporate legal teams.

Crosby was founded by Ryan (Stanford Law, Cooley, startup GC) and John (Penn, first 15 engineers at Ramp).  Help us transform one of society's most important industries.


The Role:

 - Sit at the center of modern deal-making. You’ll review and negotiate the commercial contracts that get deals to signature for companies like Cursor, Ramp, and Cognition.

 - Direct AI, don’t babysit it. You’ll orchestrate Crosby’s tooling over a contract and spend your judgment where it counts.

 - Own outcomes end-to-end and chase the small touches that turn a closed deal into one a client can’t help but tell others about at dinner.

 - This is a high-impact role for a lawyer excited to apply AI to their own practice, obsessive about quality execution, and drawn to leverage over billable hours.

What You'll Do:

 - Review and negotiate commercial contracts with speed and precision, catching the obligations, risks, and off-market terms that matter.

 - Collaborate with other Crosby legal team members to interpret contract terms and surface the anomalies and edge cases that need an expert’s read.

 - Spot inefficiencies and recurring patterns in how contracts get reviewed, and turn them into improvements that sharpen how the whole team works.

 - Help standardize and codify recurring contract types and playbooks so the team’s judgment compounds instead of resetting on every deal.

 - Partner with engineering and operations to evolve our legal service delivery model.

Who You Are:

 - 4+ years reviewing commercial contracts in private practice or in-house

 - You have impeccable attention to detail, and sound, commercial judgment. You catch buried clauses, the wrong cross-reference, and can distinguish signal from noise.

 - You hold a high bar for your own work and get restless when something could be better.

 - You embrace change and move confidently in a fast-paced, sometimes ambiguous environment.

 - You write and speak clearly, and can explain a hard call simply.

 - You’re already tinkering with AI, or excited to, and drawn to the frontier of legal work.

Benefits & Perks

 - Equity and bonus compensation

 - Flexible, generous PTO

 - Medical insurance (multiple plan options through Anthem & Cigna)

 - HSA or FSA, depending on your plan choice

 - Dental insurance

 - Vision insurance

 - One Medical membership

 - 401(k) match


EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer – The Jewish Federation of Greater Ann Arbor
jobs.location: Jewish Federation of Greater Ann Arbor
jobs.description:
Chief Executive Officer – The Jewish Federation of Greater Ann Arbor

About the Jewish Federation of Greater Ann Arbor

The Jewish Federation of Greater Ann Arbor serves as a vital force and hub for a thriving Jewish community, raising $1.8 million in its last campaign and holding an endowment of more than $3 million. Ann Arbor anchors Jewish life in Washtenaw County, with an estimated 20,000 Jews in the surrounding area and seven congregations offering diverse religious and cultural experiences. The Ann Arbor JCC houses the Early Childhood Center, the Jewish Federation of Greater Ann Arbor, and the Hebrew Day School, and runs community-wide programs; Jewish Family Services, housed separately, supports various populations, primarily new immigrants. The Hebrew Day School offers a strong K-5 education serving a broad cross-section of the Jewish community, including Israelis in Ann Arbor for graduate study.

Ann Arbor, one of the top ten cities to live in the U.S., according to U.S. News & World Report’s Quality of Life Index, and the hub of Washtenaw County, is a university town of about 150,000, including 50,000 University of Michigan students, roughly 6,000 of whom are Jewish and engaged through one of the country’s biggest Hillels. A highly active and philanthropic UM Jewish alumni network spans the U.S., and the Jewish community remains a vibrant, cohesive part of both campus and town life.

The community’s vibrant cultural life includes performances by renowned groups such as the Royal Shakespeare Company and New York Philharmonic, local theater and symphony organizations, university arts departments, and museums dedicated to art, archaeology, science, and children’s education and discovery. Beyond the University of Michigan, Detroit is located 40 minutes away, and the DTW international airport is only 25 minutes from Ann Arbor. Washtenaw County is also home to Eastern Michigan University, Washtenaw Community College, the University of Michigan Health System, Trinity Health System, strong K–12 schools, and more than 140 parks, rivers, lakes, and recreational facilities.

The CEO Opportunity

The CEO leads the Jewish Federation of Greater Ann Arbor and the Community Foundation, providing overall leadership and guidance in fostering a thriving, inclusive Jewish community in Washtenaw County, the Diaspora, and Israel.

Working with the Board, the CEO is the face of the Federation, responsible for governance, policy development, and implementation, as well as oversight of planning, development, implementation, coordination, and evaluation of all Federation initiatives and operations.

The CEO leads the Federation's financial resource development efforts, overseeing fundraising strategy while cultivating strong relationships with current and prospective donors and community foundations. The CEO manages a high-performing professional staff, ensures effective and efficient operations, and serves as a compelling, confident communicator both internally and externally.

As a collaborative and visible community leader, the CEO strengthens partnerships across Ann Arbor’s Jewish ecosystem, including organizations, schools, synagogues, volunteers, and other key stakeholders. Through strategic leadership, the CEO advances fundraising, expands programs, and creates meaningful opportunities that deepen engagement and ensure the long-term vibrancy and sustainability of Ann Arbor’s Jewish community.

Key Responsibilities

Organizational Leadership and Strategic Vision

• Provide strategic leadership to the Board, staff, and broader community by developing and advancing a clear, forward-looking vision that strengthens the Federation’s role as a central convener and leader.

• Recruit, lead, and evaluate a high-performing professional and lay team through strong supervision, coaching, and mentorship, fostering a collaborative, accountable, and high-performing culture capable of advancing the Federation’s mission and core programs.

• Create a positive work environment that values employees through professional development and teamwork.

• Ensure the Federation’s data platforms and technology systems are aligned and optimized to support organizational goals and evolving needs.

Resource Development

• Lead the organization’s fundraising strategy, strengthening donor engagement, and growing the annual campaign, corporate gifts and overall donor base.

• Actively cultivate relationships with major donors and personally solicit leadership gifts for the annual campaign, designated initiatives, and endowment.

• Implement a strategic total financial resource development model that integrates Annual Campaign, Jewish Community Foundation, capital and other special campaigns and fundraising initiatives.

• Oversees the administration and operation of the Jewish Community Foundation, including multiple direct reports on that team.

Community Relations

• Advance the Federation’s role as convener and facilitator of strategic partnerships, programs, and community-wide initiatives, both within and beyond the Jewish community.

• Partner with volunteer and professional leaders to build strategic relationships with community organizations, agencies, and external stakeholders, fostering an inclusive, connected community and respectful engagement around critical issues.

• Serve as the Federation’s chief ambassador and spokesperson, representing the organization throughout the community’s religious, cultural, and civic life and engaging with partners, funders, and stakeholders across a broad range of constituencies.

• Ensure the Federation’s story, messaging, and positions are clearly articulated to both the Jewish and broader community, supported by an integrated marketing, PR, and communications plan that builds understanding of and support for its work.

• Cultivate relationships with local, county, state, and federal government authorities, alongside a full-time Community Relations professional, to secure funding and support for Jewish communal initiatives.

• Provide decisive leadership during crises, ensuring sound decision-making, continuity of operations, and transparent communication with key stakeholders.

Board and Lay Partnerships

• Develop and execute short- and long-term strategies to engage, cultivate, train and sustain a strong pipeline of lay leadership.

• Serve as a trusted advisor to the Board across areas including finance, policy, programs, and governance.

• Partner with the Board and its committees to shape and advance the Federation's strategic vision and leadership priorities.

Financial and Operational Management

• Provide sound fiscal leadership and strong fiduciary oversight to ensure the organization’s financial health and sustainability.

• Partner with finance and administration staff and volunteer leadership to ensure effective financial management and oversight of the Federation and Foundation, including development of the annual budget with alignment, transparency, and buy-in from lay leadership.

• Provide oversight to ensure that organizations and initiatives receiving Federation allocations use funds appropriately and in alignment with their intended purposes.

Community Planning

• Foster an inclusive approach to community growth and development by strengthening the Federation’s role as a convener and steward, engaging Jewish organizations and their representatives as well as other community and governmental organizations and agencies.

• Provide direction and support for a long-term community strategic planning process, including current work with the Older Adults and Capital Needs planning committees.

• Maintain a commitment to building an inclusive community through sensitivity to the diversity of the constituency.

Qualifications

• Passion for advancing an ambitious vision for the Federation, with the energy, drive, and collaborative leadership approach necessary to bring it to life.

• Commitment to core Jewish values, a strong connection to Israel and Zionism, and sensitivity to and respect for the diversity of Jewish identities, perspectives, and practices.

• Strong knowledge of the organized Jewish community at the local, national, and international levels, including JFNA and global Jewish issues, with the ability to translate broader communal priorities into meaningful local engagement, programming, and fundraising.

• Demonstrated ability to:

• Inspire and lead an organization toward a shared vision, measurable impact, and sustainable growth.

• Provide strategic and operational leadership, including organizational development, planning, financial stewardship, and effective administration.

• Lead and manage a complex, mission-driven organization, ideally within the Jewish communal or nonprofit sector.

• Cultivate major donors, secure significant philanthropic investments, lead successful annual campaigns, grow endowments, and advance diversified fundraising strategies.

• Build and sustain trust, credibility, and productive relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, including lay leaders, donors, community partners, volunteers, and professional staff.

• Significant progressively responsible leadership experience, including executive-level management responsibilities.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to inspire, influence, and engage diverse audiences.

• Engaging, approachable, and relationship-oriented leadership style.

• High personal integrity, sound judgment, and strong commitment to ethical leadership.

Compensation Package

Salary Range: $180,000-$200,000 (commensurate with experience)

Benefits & Perks: The Jewish Federation of Greater Ann Arbor offers reimbursement up to $5,000/year for individual health insurance purchased by employees, retirement plans, short and long-term disability, life insurance and 401(k) employer match.

The Jewish Federation of Greater Ann Arbor is an equal opportunity employer.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Head of Insights and Analytics - North America
jobs.description:
The Senior Director / Head of North America Insights & Analytics leads the function responsible for converting market, customer, competitive and performance information into decisions for North America in-line and launch products. As a member of the department leadership team, this leader advises senior North America Commercial and cross-functional stakeholders on portfolio strategy, resource allocation, forecasting and execution.

The role directly owns North America primary market research, secondary analytics and commercial reporting, forecasting, competitive intelligence, field excellence (including segmentation and targeting strategy), and market access analytics. This leader will help identify and address the most important business needs and will partner with commercial leadership and functional leaders to enable data-driven decisions and proactively deliver actionable insights.

**Please note this is a hybrid remote position with occasional travel.  While other candidates will be considered, the preferred candidate will live in the Boston area, coming into the Waltham office 1-2 days per week and working remotely otherwise.

Key Responsibilities

• Portfolio Strategy and Decision Support
• Lead North America portfolio insights and provide evidence-based recommendations for commercial planning, launch readiness and investment prioritization across therapeutic areas and lifecycle stages
• Translate North America performance, market, access and competitive evidence into clear options, trade-offs, risks and recommendations for senior leaders.
• Integrate North America epidemiology, pricing and reimbursement, customer behavior and competitive developments into cohesive strategic perspectives.

Performance Analytics and Forecasting

• Own North America performance reporting and dashboarding, including portfolio and brand performance frameworks, KPI definitions, recurring and ad hoc reports, and executive business reviews.
• Own customer segmentation and targeting strategy, and national and sub-national analytics.
• Connect campaign, channel and promotional-response measurement with brand and portfolio performance, forecasting and decision support.
• Own short- and long-range North America commercial forecasting for in-line and launch products, with transparent assumptions and alignment to North America financial planning, supply planning and launch decisions.

Market, Customer and Access Insights

• Own the North America primary market research and customer insight agenda across HCPs and patients, including qualitative and quantitative research design, execution, synthesis and application.
• Lead the competitive intelligence program, with competitive intelligence focused on commercial competitors and clinical pipeline developments, while integrating relevant regulatory and market access developments and insights from Sales, Marketing and Market Access teams into actionable implications.

Own and lead the market access analytics capability, which serves as the analytics thought partner for payer, channel and patient access across Sobi’s portfolio, and is responsible for translating complex access, channel and patient journey data into actionable insights.

Department and Cross-Functional Analytics Partnership

• Collaborate with Advanced Analytics team and other Strategic Capabilities and Operations (SCO) teams to support initiatives to guide brand strategy and execution
• Integrate predictive analytics, machine learning and AI-enabled approaches to identify relevant use cases and engage the advanced analytics and AI team when appropriate.
• Partner with the advanced analytics and AI team to shape use cases and evaluate outputs for business relevance, assumptions, limitations and actionability.
• Partner with Data Team to define business requirements for commercial data, reporting and analytics capabilities.

Leadership and Operating Model

• Establish intake, prioritization and stakeholder engagement processes across all directly owned capabilities.
• Own resource allocation, budgets and vendor management across all directly owned capabilities; determine when work should be built internally, purchased or outsourced.
• Pursue novel research methodologies that offer new capabilities and ways to optimize project efficiency

• Bachelor's degree in a relevant business, quantitative, life sciences or other related field
• 15+ years of relevant biotechnology, pharmaceutical, life sciences or healthcare experience, including 10+ years in progressively responsible Insights & Analytics leadership roles at Director level or above.
• Recent experience building capabilities in a startup, emerging or high-growth life sciences organization.
• Deep expertise across several areas, including commercial analytics, segmentation and targeting, HCP and patient market research, North America commercial and launch product forecasting, competitive intelligence, field intelligence and market access analytics.
• Working knowledge of advanced analytics and AI-enabled approaches, with demonstrated ability to define business use cases, evaluate outputs and partner effectively with peer technical teams.
• Experience supporting North America in-line brands, launches and portfolio decisions in a complex, matrixed environment.
• Proven ability to influence senior executives, lead teams, manage budgets and external partners, and communicate complex issues clearly.
• Experience with Veeva CRM, Tableau or comparable commercial data, CRM and visualization platforms.

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience in oncology, hematology, immunology, rare disease and/or orphan-drug markets.
• Experience using real-world evidence, patient-level claims and specialty pharmacy data, and integrating promotional-response and ROI outputs produced by partner teams into commercial decisions.
• Experience establishing functional standards, governance processes and operating models for Insights & Analytics.

Leadership Attributes

• Enterprise mindset; strategic courage; executive communication; analytical judgment; inclusive people leadership; collaboration and influence; agility; operational discipline; and a hands-on builder mentality.

Travel and Compensation

• Ability to travel to North America offices in Waltham, Massachusetts and Durham, North Carolina, and to other meetings as business needs require.

Compensation and Total Rewards at Sobi

At Sobi, we are dedicated to providing our employees with a comprehensive and industry-competitive total rewards package. Our compensation philosophy is designed to recognize and reward talent, ensuring that your contributions are valued and reflected in your overall rewards.

Your total compensation at Sobi goes beyond just your base salary and annual bonus. It also includes a robust suite of benefits, such as:

• A competitive 401(k) match to support your financial future.
• Tuition and wellness reimbursements to invest in your personal and professional growth.
• A comprehensive medical, dental, and vision package to prioritize your health and well-being.
• Additional recognition awards to celebrate your achievements.

The base salary range for this role is $220,000-$280,000. Each individual offer will be determined based on several factors, including your experience, qualifications, and location. Additionally, this role is eligible for both short-term and long-term bonuses, as outlined in the plan details.

All Sobi employees need to demonstrate behaviors in line with Sobi's core values: Care, Ambition, Urgency, Ownership and Partnership. Are you ready to be on the Sobi team? Come join a culture that empowers every person to be the person that makes a difference for rare disease.

Why Join Us?

We are a global company with over 1,900 employees in more than 30 countries and are committed to the societies where we operate. With a deeply skilled management team directing our day-to-day wins, and a Board with a stellar track record, we’re ready to take on the world’s diseases, ailments and adversity. Our people believe they have the power to make a positive impact in others’ lives because that’s exactly what we do here. If you’re seeking a career that taps into your talents in a way that makes the world a better, healthier place, we just may have a job for you.

We know our employees are our most valuable asset, and our culture conveys that. We offer a competitive benefits package, to support the health and happiness of our staff.

Sobi Culture

At Sobi, we refuse to accept the status quo. This is because we have witnessed first-hand the challenges facing those affected by rare diseases, and have used this knowledge to shape our business to find new ways of helping them.

As a specialized biopharmaceutical company, we are dedicated to rare diseases. And we see this focus as a strength. By effectively turning our research into ground-breaking treatments, we help make medicine more accessible and open up more possibilities for patients and more opportunities for those caring for them. This has been our approach since day one, but we know we can’t change the world of rare diseases on our own. Accomplishing this requires strong partnerships with patients, partners and stakeholders across the entire value chain. Together, we define how our business can create solutions that serve the needs of those affected by rare diseases while facilitating sustainable growth.

An Equal Opportunity Employer

Sobi is an Equal Opportunity Employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any kind. All employment decisions at Sobi are based on business needs, job requirements and individual qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion or belief, national, social or ethnic origin, sex (including pregnancy), age, physical, mental or sensory disability, HIV Status, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veterans and/or expression, marital, civil union or domestic partnership status, past or present military service, family medical history or genetic information, family or parental status, or any other status or protected groups by the laws or regulations in the locations where we operate.
