jobs.title: Histology Technician-Mohs Surgery Part Time Days
jobs.description:
**This is a Part Time position at 25 hours per week located at the Glenview clinic for Mohs Surgery. Schedule is as follows: Monday 7:30am-4:00pm, Tuesday 7:30-5:00pm, and Wednesday 7:30-4:00pm.**

The Technician, Histology reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

The Technician, Histology provides technical and clinical support for various physicians and sub-specialists by performing histology related laboratory tests to aid in the diagnosis, prognosis, treatment, and follow up of patients with various health conditions. This position acts as a liaison between the physicians and staff by answering questions and providing educational assistance.

Responsibilities:

• Under the directorship of the Mohs surgeon performs frozen tissue preparations for microscopic examination.
• Properly identifies and orients tissue.
• Uses Mohs frozen section technique to orient, map, freeze, cut, and stain frozen tissue sections.
• Recognizes adequacy of cryo-sectioning.
• Labels specimens as appropriate.
• Operates automated instrumentation to stain microscopic slides.
• Evaluates stains microscopically for acceptable results.
• Identifies and corrects staining deficiencies.
• Performs manual methods during instrument downtimes.
• Recognizes, resolves, and documents unacceptable staining and cover slipping results and/or instrument failure.
• Maintains logbook of Mohs specimens as well as other manual and electronic records for easy retrieval of data as necessary.
• Records all documentation consistently and legibly in accordance with established policies, procedures, and regulations.
• Responsible for maintaining Quality Control and Quality Assurance documentation to assure compliance with CLIA regulations.
• Prioritizes technical workload based on assignment or established priorities, responds effectively to changes in workflow adjusting work to incorporate STAT requests or fluctuations in work volume.
• Cleans, disinfects, performs, and documents routine equipment and instrument per SOP.
• Monitors laboratory inventory to ensure supply levels are appropriate and adequate.
• Notifies coordinator promptly of any supply issues.
• Fosters department and laboratory teamwork through effective communication.
• Participates in Safety and Infection Control activities.
• Follows all required safety procedures, assumes a proactive role in laboratory safety.
• Assists in cleaning, wrapping and sterilization of instruments.
• Assist in maintaining inventory of clinical supplies.
• Assist in clerical duties such as scanning of patients’ records into EMR.
• Takes initiative for personal development by attending teleconferences, educational sessions, and required meetings, etc.
• Possesses motivation, self-reliance, initiative, a team player.
• Performs other duties as assigned.

Minimum Requirements:

Education:

• High School Diploma or GED equivalent.

Experience:

• Zero (0) to two (2) years’ experience in a relevant role.
• Previous experience in molecular laboratories (in situ hybridization, polymerase chain reaction).

Preferred:

• One of the following:BS degree or higher in biological science
• OR
• Associate Degree in a laboratory science, or medical laboratory technology from an accredited institution
• OR
• Have education and training that includes 60 semester hours from an accredited institution that includes 24 hours of medical laboratory technology courses
• OR
• 24 semester hours that include 6 hours of chemistry, 6 hours of biology and 12 hours of chemistry, biology, or medical laboratory technology in any combination
• HT(ASCP) American Society for Clinical Pathology Histotechnician certification or complete once eligible.
• Experience in immunohistochemistry and tissue processing

jobs.title: Manager, Wealth Planning Advisor
jobs.description:
Manager, Wealth Planning Advisor

Dalio Family Office

Dalio Family Office Overview:

The Dalio Family Office (DFO) supports Barbara and Ray Dalio and their family in their ventures, investments, and philanthropic efforts under Dalio Philanthropies, which includes OceanX, Dalio Education, Endless Network, and the Beijing Dalio Foundation. The core of the DFO’s culture is built around meaningful work and meaningful relationships and the family’s commitment to giving back. The office is headquartered in Westport, CT with regional offices in New York City, Singapore, and Abu Dhabi.

Position Summary:

The Manager, Wealth Planning Advisor sits within Global & Strategic Planning (GSP) and supports the design and execution of estate, trust, and wealth-transfer planning for the Dalio Family Office globally. The role provides technical analysis, drafting support, and coordination that turns planning strategy into well-documented, executable structures. The purpose of the role is to serve as a strong wealth planning advisor who advances planning workstreams day to day - preparing analyses, supporting trust and entity structuring, and coordinating with internal Pillars and external advisors — under the direction of Head of Global Strategy & Planning. Success in the role means planning matters move forward with technical rigor and minimal re-work, documentation cleanly reflects the intended plan, and cross-border and trust structures are analyzed and sequenced with sound, detail-oriented judgment.

Day-to-day responsibilities would include a combination of the following:

Wealth Planning Support

• Support the design and refinement of multi-generational estate, gift, and wealth-transfer strategies under the direction of senior GSP leadership.

• Prepare technical analyses, planning memos, and structural options that frame choices and tradeoffs for review.

• Track planning decisions and ensure follow-through from design to executed structure.

Trust Planning & Structuring

• Support the structuring of new trusts and the modification or migration of existing trusts, including cross-border considerations.

• Draft and review planning documents in coordination with external counsel, ensuring accuracy and consistency with the intended plan.

• Help ensure trust planning is integrated with investment, income-tax, and philanthropic considerations.

Global & Cross-Border Planning

• Support estate and structural planning for cross-border matters.

• Assist with residency, citizenship, mobility, and situs analyses as they affect estate, trust, and transfer-tax planning.

• Coordinate U.S. and non-U.S. legal and tax inputs into clear, decision-ready materials.

Cross-Pillar Coordination & Execution

• Coordinate day to day with Tax, Legal, Finance, and external advisors to advance planning initiatives.

• Maintain initiative documentation: objectives, scope, dependencies, decision points, and status.

• Help ensure initiatives produce the intended outcome without turning GSP into a routine execution team.

Technical Rigor & Risk Awareness

• Apply a careful legal, tax, and regulatory lens to estate and trust structures across jurisdictions.

• Flag novel or higher-risk issues for senior review and support “case of first impression” analysis.

• Monitor legislative and regulatory developments relevant to estate, gift, and transfer-tax planning.

Stakeholder & Advisor Interface

• Participate in working sessions with external advisors and internal leaders, ensuring alignment and clean follow-through.

• Provide continuity and institutional context across multi-year matters.

• Additional duties as assigned.

The ideal candidate will possess the following knowledge, skills, attributes, and values:

• Strong drafting, analytical, and organizational skills with high attention to detail and discretion.

• Ability to manage multiple workstreams and coordinate effectively across internal teams and external advisors.

Illustrative Benefits:

• 100% company paid medical premiums

• 17 company paid holidays

• Friday summer hours

• Monthly community happy hours

• Hybrid work environment

• Free catered food services for in-office days

• Generous PTO offering

• Casual dress code

• 150% 401(k) match up to $7,500 and 100% match above $7,500 ($15k match limit)

• Gym reimbursement, back up childcare services, insurance, financial, and legal services, and much more!

Qualifications:

• D. required; LL.M. in Taxation or Estate Planning or equivalent experience preferred.

• At least 7 years of estate, trust, and wealth-transfer planning experience, ideally within a private client / trusts & estates practice, single family office, financial institution, or other UHNW advisory setting.

• Strong technical grounding in U.S. estate, gift, and generation-skipping transfer tax, trust law, and entity structuring.

• Global / cross-border planning experience is a key requirement, including exposure to residency, situs, and multi-jurisdictional trust and entity matters.

• Experience working within a family office or exposure to ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) family structures.

Compensation:

Compensation for the role includes a competitive salary in the range from $360,000 -$600,000 (inclusive of a merit-based bonus, dependent on years of experience, level of education obtained, as well as applicable skillset) and an excellent benefits package, including  paid time off ranging from 15 to 25 days based on years of service, paid sick and safe leave, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, paid parental time off, birth mother recovery pay, sick family member pay, parental ramp back up program, gym reimbursement and generous employer match for 401k.

jobs.title: Stringer Operator (Pitman Day Shift)
jobs.description:
Summary of Position

The Stringer Operator is responsible for the safe, efficient, and precise operation of the Stringer machine. This role requires a combination of production expertise, technical understanding, and mechanical aptitude to ensure consistent product quality, maximum equipment uptime & FTT (first time through). The Stringer Operator will monitor Stringer performance, operate using HMIs, perform hands-on preventive and autonomous maintenance, and assist with troubleshooting and minor repairs under the guidance of maintenance and engineering teams. The schedule for this position is 12 hour rotating shifts from 6AM - 6PM.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

· Safely operate and monitor stringer machinery, ensuring proper function and throughput.

· Load materials, visually inspecting solar cells and verifying product quality against established standards.

· Operate and navigate HMI and NC equipment interfaces for machine control, diagnostics, and basic troubleshooting.

· Perform hands-on preventive maintenance (PM) and autonomous maintenance tasks such as cleaning, lubrication, and inspection of key components.

· Troubleshoot, communicate and help resolve basic machine faults issues to minimize downtime, escalate as needed

· Record hourly production and performance data accurately and report deviations or abnormalities.

· Collaborate with maintenance, engineering, and quality teams to implement process improvements and corrective actions.

· Follow all established safety, quality, and operational procedures, maintaining a clean and organized work area.

· Support training and onboarding of new operators on stringer operation and maintenance best practices.

· Other duties as assigned by Lead Hand and Supervisor

Skills

· Experience working with HMIs and operating numerical control (NC) or automated production equipment.

· Strong understanding of preventive maintenance and basic mechanical/electrical troubleshooting.

· Fine motor control and steady hand-eye coordination for handling delicate solar components.

· Clear and effective communication skills for documenting and reporting equipment or process issues.

Traits

· Critical thinker with the ability to identify root causes and propose practical solutions.

· High attention to detail and commitment to producing quality work.

· Team-oriented with a proactive approach to safety and continuous improvement.

· Dependable, adaptable, and eager to develop advanced technical skills.

Education and/or Experience

· High School Diploma or equivalent required; technical diploma or certificate preferred.

· Minimum 2 years of production experience in an autonomous manufacturing environment.

· Hands-on experience operating HMI-controlled equipment, NC machinery, and performing preventive/autonomous maintenance.

· Familiarity with basic mechanical, pneumatic, or electrical systems preferred.

Compensation and Benefits

• Wage: $21/hr - $24/hr
• Paid Time Off (vacation, sick, and holiday)

• Medical/Dental/Vision Insurance Plans

• Tuition Reimbursement Program

jobs.title: Connectivity Partner Specialist
jobs.description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join:

The Airbnb Hotels team is a fun, fast-growing group leading Airbnb’s expansion into the hotel sector. Operating with an entrepreneurial spirit, this team combines the simplicity, product excellence, and guest-centered ethos that define Airbnb. This team’s mission is to deliver the smoothest, most intuitive hotel booking experience for guests, while helping hotels easily drive incremental bookings so they can focus on delivering the best hospitality. The ultimate aim is to help more people discover high-quality hotels, creating value for guests and our hotel partners.

The Difference You Will Make:

In this role, you will provide API specialist support and act as a subject matter expert for our connectivity operations. Your responsibilities include conducting analysis and technical troubleshooting to solve complex problems, monitoring key metrics, and error logs to optimize performance and ensuring timely error resolution. You'll serve as a technical point of contact for both internal and external partners, offering expert insight into Airbnb’s API’s and our partner systems. You’ll support the Connectivity Team and Enterprise Account Team with projects designed to achieve Airbnb’s commercial goals. You'll also help to create and improve internal knowledge bases and training materials so teams can independently handle API-related questions.

A Typical Day:

• Provide day-to-day technical support for internal and external systems, including connectivity issues, to proactively mitigate partner impact.

• Develop a deep understanding of technical integrations across Property Management Systems (PMS), Channel Managers, and Central Reservation Systems (CRS) to provide targeted partner support.

• Use data to identify strategic opportunities and drive sales growth.

• Educate partners on product updates and share partner feedback with internal stakeholders Implement and oversee effective troubleshooting processes, escalating as needed

• Identify patterns in data and feedback to improve services and products.

• Research technical information to deepen your understanding and support decision-making.

• Contribute to the development of technical communication materials such as policies, procedures, and presentations.

• Collaborate with your team to design and manage projects which support the commercial goals of Airbnb and our hotel and connectivity partners.

Your Expertise:

• 3+ years of experience in a Connectivity Operations, Solutions or Technical Partner Manager role.

• Strong understanding of hospitality/travel software; CRS,PMS, Channel Managers

• Proficiency in SQL, Looker and Excel.

• Tableau, Asana, Jira and Salesforce experience preferred.

• Solid technical troubleshooting skills and project management experience.

• Excellent communication and presentation abilities, with confidence in engaging clients across multiple channels with stakeholders at various levels.

• Effective time management and ability to prioritize in a fast-paced environment.

• Strong quantitative skills with a proven ability to leverage data in decision-making Adaptability to shifting priorities, projects, and deadlines.

• Passion for Airbnb, travel, and the sharing economy—being an Airbnb host is a plus

jobs.title: Manager, Wealth Planning Advisor
jobs.description:
Manager, Wealth Planning Advisor

Dalio Family Office

Dalio Family Office Overview:

The Dalio Family Office (DFO) supports Barbara and Ray Dalio and their family in their ventures, investments, and philanthropic efforts under Dalio Philanthropies, which includes OceanX, Dalio Education, Endless Network, and the Beijing Dalio Foundation. The core of the DFO’s culture is built around meaningful work and meaningful relationships and the family’s commitment to giving back. The office is headquartered in Westport, CT with regional offices in New York City, Singapore, and Abu Dhabi.

Position Summary:

The Manager, Wealth Planning Advisor sits within Global & Strategic Planning (GSP) and supports the design and execution of estate, trust, and wealth-transfer planning for the Dalio Family Office globally. The role provides technical analysis, drafting support, and coordination that turns planning strategy into well-documented, executable structures. The purpose of the role is to serve as a strong wealth planning advisor who advances planning workstreams day to day - preparing analyses, supporting trust and entity structuring, and coordinating with internal Pillars and external advisors — under the direction of Head of Global Strategy & Planning. Success in the role means planning matters move forward with technical rigor and minimal re-work, documentation cleanly reflects the intended plan, and cross-border and trust structures are analyzed and sequenced with sound, detail-oriented judgment.

Day-to-day responsibilities would include a combination of the following:

Wealth Planning Support

• Support the design and refinement of multi-generational estate, gift, and wealth-transfer strategies under the direction of senior GSP leadership.

• Prepare technical analyses, planning memos, and structural options that frame choices and tradeoffs for review.

• Track planning decisions and ensure follow-through from design to executed structure.

Trust Planning & Structuring

• Support the structuring of new trusts and the modification or migration of existing trusts, including cross-border considerations.

• Draft and review planning documents in coordination with external counsel, ensuring accuracy and consistency with the intended plan.

• Help ensure trust planning is integrated with investment, income-tax, and philanthropic considerations.

Global & Cross-Border Planning

• Support estate and structural planning for cross-border matters.

• Assist with residency, citizenship, mobility, and situs analyses as they affect estate, trust, and transfer-tax planning.

• Coordinate U.S. and non-U.S. legal and tax inputs into clear, decision-ready materials.

Cross-Pillar Coordination & Execution

• Coordinate day to day with Tax, Legal, Finance, and external advisors to advance planning initiatives.

• Maintain initiative documentation: objectives, scope, dependencies, decision points, and status.

• Help ensure initiatives produce the intended outcome without turning GSP into a routine execution team.

Technical Rigor & Risk Awareness

• Apply a careful legal, tax, and regulatory lens to estate and trust structures across jurisdictions.

• Flag novel or higher-risk issues for senior review and support “case of first impression” analysis.

• Monitor legislative and regulatory developments relevant to estate, gift, and transfer-tax planning.

Stakeholder & Advisor Interface

• Participate in working sessions with external advisors and internal leaders, ensuring alignment and clean follow-through.

• Provide continuity and institutional context across multi-year matters.

• Additional duties as assigned.

The ideal candidate will possess the following knowledge, skills, attributes, and values:

• Strong drafting, analytical, and organizational skills with high attention to detail and discretion.

• Ability to manage multiple workstreams and coordinate effectively across internal teams and external advisors.

Illustrative Benefits:

• 100% company paid medical premiums

• 17 company paid holidays

• Friday summer hours

• Monthly community happy hours

• Hybrid work environment

• Free catered food services for in-office days

• Generous PTO offering

• Casual dress code

• 150% 401(k) match up to $7,500 and 100% match above $7,500 ($15k match limit)

• Gym reimbursement, back up childcare services, insurance, financial, and legal services, and much more!

Qualifications:

• J.D. required; LL.M. in Taxation or Estate Planning or equivalent experience preferred.

• At least 7 years of estate, trust, and wealth-transfer planning experience, ideally within a private client / trusts & estates practice, single family office, financial institution, or other UHNW advisory setting.

• Strong technical grounding in U.S. estate, gift, and generation-skipping transfer tax, trust law, and entity structuring.

• Global / cross-border planning experience is a key requirement, including exposure to residency, situs, and multi-jurisdictional trust and entity matters.

• Experience working within a family office or exposure to ultra-high-net-worth (UHNW) family structures.

Compensation:

Compensation for the role includes a competitive salary in the range from $360,000 -$600,000 (inclusive of a merit-based bonus, dependent on years of experience, level of education obtained, as well as applicable skillset) and an excellent benefits package, including  paid time off ranging from 15 to 25 days based on years of service, paid sick and safe leave, dental, vision, life and disability insurance, paid parental time off, birth mother recovery pay, sick family member pay, parental ramp back up program, gym reimbursement and generous employer match for 401k.

jobs.title: Manager, Sales Operations
jobs.description:
Company Overview:
At Panopto, we are the most customer-centric learning technology company in the world. As the leader in visual and audio-based learning, we empower organizations to share knowledge effortlessly in a capture and post-capture world. We don’t just build software; we obsess over our users’ goals to deliver solutions that truly matter. Our mission is simple: to attract the brightest talent, people like you, to Elevate the Craft and do the most impactful work of your career.


To enhance our team, we are seeking an experienced Manager, Sales Operations who combines strong people leadership with a passion for operational excellence and continuous improvement. In this role, you will lead the team responsible for supporting our global sales organization throughout the quote-to-close lifecycle, including frontline sales support, deal desk, contracting, and order processing. You’ll play a key role in ensuring efficient day-to-day execution while proactively identifying opportunities to simplify processes, improve the seller experience, and drive scalable operational improvements in partnership with Sales Leadership and cross-functional teams. 
Position Summary
In this role, you will have the opportunity to do meaningful work in your career, elevating your craft while contributing to a team that values lifelong learning.
As a Manager, Sales Operations, you will lead, coach, and develop a team responsible for the day-to-day operational support of our sales organization. You'll oversee critical processes spanning sales inquiries, quoting, commercial approvals, contracting, and order processing, ensuring accurate and timely execution while maintaining appropriate commercial controls.
Beyond managing daily operations, you'll serve as a proactive partner to Sales Leadership, Business Systems, Finance, Legal, and Product, identifying operational bottlenecks, evaluating existing workflows, and driving improvements that enable our sales teams to work more effectively. You'll combine a hands-on understanding of sales operations with an analytical, solutions-oriented mindset to help build efficient, scalable processes that support revenue growth.
You will also have opportunities to contribute to other initiatives that directly advance our core values and support you in elevating your craft.
How You’ll Contribute 
In this role, you will have the opportunity to…
Lead, coach, and develop a team of Sales Operations Managers and Specialists responsible for frontline sales support, deal desk, contracting, and order processing. Establish clear expectations, manage workload distribution, and foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. 
Oversee daily sales support operations, ensuring timely and effective resolution of sales representative inquiries related to quoting, Salesforce processes, commercial policies, and other operational needs. Establish clear escalation paths and SLAs to ensure consistent, high-quality support.
Manage deal desk operations and commercial approval workflows, ensuring adherence to established pricing policies, discounting guidelines, and approval matrices. 
Partner with Sales Leadership and senior stakeholders to maintain and refine approval processes that balance deal velocity with appropriate governance. 
Serve as the primary operational escalation point for non-standard commercial terms, discounting approvals, and order processing exceptions, collaborating with Finance, Legal, and Sales leadership.
Ensure accurate and timely sales order processing, including validation of executed agreements, opportunity, and order data, and required documentation. Partner with Finance and Accounting to support data flow for accurate invoicing, reporting, and downstream financial processes.
Proactively evaluate sales operations workflows, identify recurring bottlenecks, manual processes and sources of friction, and develop actionable recommendations to improve efficiency, accuracy, and the overall seller experience.
Establish, track, and maintain operational performance metrics, including request volumes, turnaround times, processing accuracy, and recurring issue trends. Regularly report operational insights, emerging risks, and improvement opportunities to Revenue Operations leadership.
Identify opportunities to leverage automation, AI, and existing technology capabilities to reduce administrative burden, streamline repetitive tasks, and improve the scalability of sales operations.
Develop, maintain, and continuously improve standard operating procedures, process documentation, and internal knowledge resources to promote consistency, enable team development, and support efficient onboarding and execution.
Collaborate with Sales Enablement and Sales Leadership to identify recurring knowledge gaps and opportunities for improved training, communication, or self-service resources that reduce unnecessary operational requests and improve sales team effectiveness.
What Success Looks Like 
Within 3 Months: Build strong relationships with your team, Sales Leadership, and cross-functional partners; develop a thorough understanding of existing quote-to-close processes and operational challenges; establish visibility into team performance and workload; and identify initial opportunities to improve efficiency and the seller experience. 
Within 6 Months:Establish consistent operational performance standards and reporting, implement initial process improvements that address recurring bottlenecks, and strengthen collaboration with Sales Leadership and Business Systems to prioritize and execute workflow enhancements. Demonstrate progress in reducing unnecessary manual effort and improving the consistency and quality of sales support.
Within 1 Year: Deliver measurable improvements in operational efficiency, processing accuracy, and the seller experience. Establish a proactive, data-informed approach to continuous improvement, with scalable processes, stronger cross-functional workflows, and a team empowered to independently resolve challenges and contribute ideas for improvement. 
Your Legacy: You built a high-performing Sales Operations team that is recognized not only for delivering reliable, responsive support, but for proactively solving problems and making it easier for the business to operate. You’ve developed a team of confident, capable professionals and established a culture where operational challenges become opportunities for meaningful, lasting improvement. 
Values in Action
Customer First, Always: You proactively surface friction points in the customer experience before they are escalated — and propose solutions, not just reports.
Thrive Together: You share work-in-progress for early feedback, knowing that challenge improves the outcome. You separate critiques of ideas from critiques of people.
Elevate the Craft: You hold the bar high on your own work and invest in developing those around you. You treat every project as an opportunity to learn something new.
Act with Ownership: You define success by outcomes, not activity. You flag problems early and bring a proposed path forward, not just the problem.
Clarity Over Complexity: You default to the simpler solution. Your written communication — internal or external — is direct, specific, and free of filler.
How We Thrive
You’ll join a team that thrives on clarity, ownership, and continuous improvement.
We operate with a bias toward action, balancing strategic thinking with execution, and hold ourselves accountable to outcomes that drive the business forward. Collaboration is at the core of how we work, and we value diverse perspectives that strengthen our collective thinking.
The Foundation for Success
Education: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Operations, Information Systems, or a related field; or equivalent practical operational experience.
Experience: 5+ years of progressive experience within Sales Operations, Revenue Operations, Deal Desk, or Commercial Operations in a B2B SaaS or technology organization, with at least 1–2 years of direct people management or formal team leadership experience.
Demonstrated success leading operational teams, managing competing priorities, coaching and developing employees, and ensuring accurate, timely execution of critical business processes.
Proven ability to identify operational inefficiencies, analyze root causes, and implement process improvements that enhance productivity, accuracy, and scalability.
Strong proficiency in Salesforce CRM, including opportunity management, quoting workflows, approval processes, reporting, and data management. Experience working with CPQ solutions and related sales technologies.
Strong understanding of the quote-to-close lifecycle, including sales support, commercial approvals, contracting, order processing, and cross-functional handoffs to Finance and Accounting.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate operational challenges into actionable recommendations and collaborate effectively across teams.
What Sets You Apart
Experience partnering with Business Systems or IT teams to design and implement Salesforce enhancements, workflow automation, or other operational technology improvements.
Demonstrated success leading cross-functional process improvement initiatives across Marketing, Sales, Finance, Product, Customer Success, and Legal, from identifying opportunities through implementation and measuring outcomes.
Experience developing operational KPIs, capacity planning models, or dashboards to improve team performance and inform operational decisions.
Familiarity with AI-enabled productivity tools, ticketing platforms, or business intelligence solutions used to streamline operational workflows.
Prior success improving or scaling sales operations processes and teams in a growing B2B SaaS organization.
Join Us
Join Panopto and play a key role in building the operational backbone that powers our global sales organization. If you take pride in mentoring early-career talent, streamlining complex sales workflows, removing roadblocks for sales reps, and driving measurable operational efficiency, you will feel right at home here. 
Total Rewards
The salary range for this position is $115,000 - $125,000 USD per year. This position is also eligible for a bonus as part of the compensation package. 
Base pay offered may vary depending on various factors, including, but not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and other eligibility factors such as geographic location. The Total Rewards package includes competitive base pay and an opportunity to enroll in a variety of benefit programs such as health insurance, flexible spending accounts, retirement savings plans, life and disability insurance programs, and programs that provide for both paid and unpaid time away from work. At Panopto, we know that great people make an organization great. We value our people and offer employees benefits that are market competitive for our industry. Learn more about what working at Panopto can mean for you.
At Panopto, our commitment to pay equity and transparency is unwavering. We do not engage in salary negotiations beyond the established range to maintain fairness and prevent potential pay disparities among team members based on negotiation strategies.

jobs.description:

WHAT WE OFFER

 - Opportunity to take on high-impact technical work

 - Competitive cash compensation

 - Top-tier benefits and 401(k) match

 - Flexible, remote-friendly work environment

 

This role requires you to be based in the United States and authorized to work in the U.S.

jobs.title: Board Certified Behavior Analyst
jobs.description:
Acorn Health is an Applied Behavioral Analysis (ABA) treatment provider dedicated to providing the best quality care for our clients.  We aim to continually establish best-in-class standards in integrity and quality for not only ourselves, but also in the field of ABA.  We work courageously and with accountability to focus on the individuality of each child, collaborate with client families, and generate permanence in client outcomes. We strive to hire and to invest in our greatest asset - our employees, who are the heart of Acorn Health.

Acorn Health is a standard-setting family of ABA treatment providers.  We believe the best employees want to work with companies who share their beliefs, and that is true for families who entrust us with children they love. Every day and every interaction, we strive to demonstrate our Five Core Values.

Acorn Health is looking for a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) to join our team as a Program Supervisor in our Silver Spring location!

At Acorn Health, we're committed to increasing access to care through ethical practice, manageable caseloads, and meaningful collaboration. We believe great clinical outcomes start with supported clinicians who have the resources, guidance, and flexibility to do their best work.

We also have additional clinics throughout {{Neighboring Geographic Area}} and beyond!

Our Values

Every day and every interaction, we strive to demonstrate our Five Core Values.

• Authenticity: We present our true, consistent selves. Everyone hungers for genuine connections.

• Accountability: We keep our promises and can be trusted with the life and future of a child.

• Teamwork: The best outcomes are produced by people who collaborate with enthusiasm.

• Growth: We know the needs of children and their families are unique and ever-changing.

• Hustle: In autism care and treatment, time is always of the essence. We do things now.

What You'll Do

As a BCBA Program Supervisor, you'll lead individualized assessment and treatment planning while partnering with ~10 families, a team of Registered Behavior Technicians, and fellow clinicians to support meaningful progress.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Overseeing client care from initial assessment through ongoing treatment, including functional, behavioral, and developmental assessments.

• Developing, implementing, and monitoring individualized Behavior Intervention Plans (BIPs) and treatment plans using data-driven decision-making.

• Serving as the clinical lead for assigned cases, providing supervision, feedback, and training to Behavior Technicians.

• Monitoring treatment fidelity and client progress, analyzing clinical data, and adjusting interventions as needed.

• Partnering with parents and caregivers through family training, regular communication, and ongoing support.

• Collaborating with colleagues, schools, and other relevant partners to promote consistent, effective interventions across settings.

• Participating in team meetings, professional development, and opportunities to share clinical knowledge and evidence-based practices.

Services may be delivered in our centers, clients' homes, and/or community settings, depending on the needs of the client and the position, but the vast majority of our services are provided in center.

Why Work for Acorn Health?

We want our clinicians to have the support and resources they need to deliver high-quality care and continue growing professionally.

Compensation and Benefits

Our compensation package is designed to recognize clinical impact and achievement of established clinical impact hour expectations. We'll share additional details about the incentive structure during the interview process.

• Incentive bonus

• Paid time off, paid holidays, and paid parental leave

• Medical, dental, and vision insurance

• Retirement plan

• Life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage

• Compensation Potential: $90,000–$110,000 (includes base salary plus monthly incentive bonus)

Clinical and Professional Development

• Continuing education unit (CEU) opportunities

• Professional development funds

• Career advancement opportunities, including Acorn's Leadership Development Institute

• Opportunities to collaborate with and learn from our Clinical Advisory Board

Work Environment and Support

• Balanced caseloads and a flexible work environment

• A collaborative, interdisciplinary clinical team

• Administrative and operational support that helps you focus on clinical care

What You'll Bring

• A master's degree in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) or a related field that meets applicable certification requirements.

• Active Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) certification through the Behavior Analyst Certification Board (BACB).

• Knowledge of evidence-based practices in autism assessment and treatment.

• Experience working with children, adolescents, young adults, and their families.

• Strong verbal and written communication skills in English.

• Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to maintain accurate records and complete documentation in a timely manner.

• The ability to work independently while contributing effectively to an interdisciplinary team.

• Reliable transportation, a valid driver's license, and a satisfactory driving record, as required for the position.

• The ability to meet the essential physical and environmental requirements of the role, with reasonable accommodation where applicable.

• The ability to successfully complete required background screening.

If you're passionate about delivering high-quality ABA services and partnering with families to help children reach their potential, we'd love to connect with you.

Join Acorn Health and help us increase access to care.

About the Positions

We’re seeking Reporting Specialists of various skill levels to support large, complex heavy civil infrastructure programs, including highways, roads, bridges, transit (bus and rail), aviation (international airports), and water/wastewater projects delivered through both traditional and alternative delivery methods. These roles produce the recurring reporting a program publishes, the monthly, quarterly, and annual packages that reach program leadership, funding agencies, and oversight bodies, along with the input collection, verification, and version control standing behind every figure in them. You’ll run the reporting cycle and get a defensible package out on the date it was promised. If your work is weighted toward building data models, queries, and dashboards, our data analyst bank is the better fit, and if it is weighted toward authoring plans, procedures, and controlled documents, look at our technical writer bank.

This post is for future roles and not for a specific opportunity that is available right now. We accept applications and conduct interviews in advance of upcoming hiring needs. When a candidate is selected, their profile is activated in our talent pool for this specialty area. We notify our talent pool candidates first whenever we have a project need.

Responsibilities may include, but are not limited to, the following:

Note: We are seeking candidates of various skill levels, and the following responsibilities represent the core of these roles. Scope and complexity increase with experience level.

• Prepare the recurring monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting packages the program publishes, assembling progress, cost, schedule, change, and milestone content into the program’s approved format.

• May lead the reporting cycle from data cutoff through review and distribution, tracking who owes what and chasing late or missing inputs so the publication date holds.

• Collect reporting inputs from project teams, consultants, and contractors, and verify each figure and status statement against the source records held in the program’s PMIS, cost, and schedule systems.

• Review contractor and consultant reporting submissions for completeness and conformance with the reporting requirements in their contracts, and return submissions that do not meet the standard.

• Reconcile differences between what a contractor reports, what the PMIS holds, and what program records show, and escalate what cannot be settled before publication.

• Develop the exhibits behind the reporting, including milestone and progress charts, dashboard extracts, maps, and photo logs, and confirm each one matches the data it was drawn from.

• Apply the program’s reporting templates, data definitions, and format standards across projects and contracts so figures carry the same meaning at the program level.

• Maintain reporting trackers, logs, distribution lists, and the repositories where published reporting and its backup live, under version control, so any published figure can be traced back to its source.

• Coordinate with cost, schedule, change management, risk, quality, and document control teams to settle conflicting figures before they reach leadership.

• Assemble the documentation supporting funding, grant, and oversight agency reporting, researching project records, correspondence, and submittal and change logs to close the gaps.

• Prepare ad hoc status summaries and briefing materials for program leadership and project staff across all contract packages.

Attributes

• Excellent written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills.

• Excellent multi-tasking and organizational skills.

• Collaborative mindset that fosters teamwork, trust, and positive relationships.

• Natural curiosity, problem-solving abilities, and a commitment to continuous improvement.

Minimum Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in construction management, engineering, business administration, or public administration, or related field, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

• 5+ years of program or project reporting experience for large (>$500M), complex, heavy-civil infrastructure projects.

• Experience producing recurring reporting deliverables on a fixed cycle, including assembling content from multiple contributors and meeting a published distribution date.

• Experience verifying reported figures and status against source records, and resolving discrepancies with the team or organization that submitted them.

• Working knowledge of program controls and construction management reporting content, including progress, cost, schedule, and change status, and where each of those figures originates.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Power BI, Oracle Cloud Analytics, or other dashboard KPI reporting software.

• Experience with industry standard program reporting and document management software (e.g., Kahua, Unifier, e-Builder, SharePoint, ProjectWise, etc.).

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite/Office 365 (e.g., Outlook, Teams, Word, PowerPoint, etc.).

Preferred Qualifications

• Master’s degree in construction management, engineering, business administration, or public administration.

• Active professional certifications such as CCM (CMAA), and/or PMP or CAPM (PMI).

• Experience serving as the lead producer of a program’s recurring reporting package on a program exceeding $1B in construction value.

• Experience producing board, committee, or oversight body reporting deliverables on a publicly funded capital program.

• Experience assembling federal or state grant reporting, funding drawdown packages, or external audit responses, including the documentation trail behind them.

• Experience consolidating reporting across a portfolio of concurrent projects and contracts into a single program-level package.

• Experience developing reporting templates, data definitions, or format standards that other teams then produced reporting to.

Compensation Details

jobs.title: Account Executive (Independent Hotel Sales)
jobs.description:
Our Mission: Why Lighthouse?

At Lighthouse, we’re on a mission to revolutionize commercial strategy as hospitality’s most powerful AI platform. We take the world's largest hotel data network and transform it into real-time intelligence that drives action. We don't just deliver insights; we empower businesses to make decisions that move revenue.

With $370M in Series C funding and over $100M in ARR, we are scaling at lightspeed. Our 850+ teammates across 35 countries aren't just building software—they are leveraging cutting-edge AI to help hoteliers be the first to act. Tens of thousands of hotels across 185 countries trust Lighthouse to execute their commercial strategy, including every one of the top 15 global chains and thousands of independent hotels that consistently outperform their markets. With Lighthouse AI, the intelligence gets deeper. Decisions get smarter. Actions get faster. We help hoteliers be first to act.

Lighthouse Values: Our guiding light

We are Lumineers. Our shared values keep us on a collaborative path fostering a cultural and customer centric environment

• Pursuit of greatness: We’re innovators who care deeply about our customers’ success. Our team brings their best work, stays curious, and delivers excellence through attention to detail

• Meaningful work matters: We make every moment count by knowing what to deliver, why it matters, and how it drives Lighthouse forward

• Elevate each other: We don’t just work together - we grow together. What unites us is understanding each other as people and working toward shared goals

We’re more than just a workplace – we’re a community. Collaborative, fun, and deeply committed, we work hard together to revolutionize the hospitality sector. Are you ready to join us and shine brighter in the industry’s most exciting rocket-ship? 🚀

Job Details

• 💼 Revenue

• 📍 United States - Dallas, TX; Denver, CO

• 🕜 Full-Time/Hybrid

• 💰 $65,000.00 - $79,000.00 (Commission: $113,000.00 - $127,500.00 OTE)

What you will do

You’ll be the face of Lighthouse for independent hotels, owning the full sales cycle from prospecting to close. This is a hunter role: you carry a quota, you build your own pipeline, and you’re accountable to outcomes and success. No excuses, just results.

For independent properties with limited staff and time, every pricing decision, missed opportunity, or manual task adds up quickly. When AI takes repetitive work off their plate and helps hoteliers act faster, the impact is felt almost immediately.

You will be selling a comprehensive suite of AI-driven tools designed specifically to streamline and elevate independent hotel operations. You'll empower hoteliers to replace manual guesswork with automated pricing and reservation management, ultimately helping them drive up to 21% more revenue. This means less time behind the screen and more time delivering the exceptional guest experiences that keep independent properties competitive.

What makes this different: you won’t do it alone. Lighthouse is deploying an agent AI infrastructure — Enablement, Pre-Sales, and Coaching agents — alongside a modern revenue stack. AI handles the prep, the sequencing, and the pattern recognition so you can focus on what matters — building relationships, running sharp discovery, and closing deals.

Where you will have impact

Own your territory and your number. Build and execute a strategic territory plan to generate a net-new pipeline. Maintain 3x pipeline coverage, forecast honestly, and take full accountability for your results. Your quota is your commitment.

Hunt and build a pipeline. Source a meaningful share of your own pipeline through outbound sequences, ICP targeting, Lighthouse Connect events, and industry conferences. This is not an SDR-reliant role.

Run a disciplined sales process. Using MEDDPICC to qualify and advance opportunities. Use the AI Pre-Sales Agent to identify gaps before every major call. Advance deals through stage gates with evidence, not optimism. Leverage AI to make your days easier and focus on more selling time.

Use AI as a force multiplier. Leverage the Enablement Agent for call prep, discovery frameworks, and positioning. Use the Coaching Agent to surface patterns in your pipeline and win rate. Push back on the tools when they’re wrong — help make the system smarter.

Become an expert in the independent hotel market. Understand the unique challenges independent hoteliers face and position the Lighthouse Indy product suite — including Pricing Manager, Channel Manager, Reservation Manager, and Booking Engine — as the integrated solution that replaces fragmented point tools. Build trusted relationships with independent hotel owners and GMs by speaking their language and solving their problems.

Drive results beyond net-new. Consistently meet and exceed sales targets through new business and by identifying expansion and upgrade opportunities within your accounts. Partner with Product to share market feedback and influence the roadmap. Represent Lighthouse at industry events to build the brand and your network.

About our team

You’ll join a global Revenue team of 150+ sales professionals across 24 countries, dedicated to expanding Lighthouse’s presence in the independent hotel market. This team is focused on helping independent hoteliers unlock their revenue potential with tailored solutions. You’ll work closely with SDRs, product specialists, and regional leaders in a collaborative environment that rewards initiative and offers real career growth as we scale our Indies business.

What's in it for you?

• Impactful work: Shape products relied on by 85,000+ users worldwide.

• Competitive compensation: Proactively maintained to value your work.

• Flexible working environment: Work from home or at one of our global offices.

• Flexible time off: Autonomy to manage your work-life balance.

• 401k matching: Up to 4%.

• Health insurance: Two Blue Cross Blue Shield plans with 99% company contribution to the base plan and 75% for dependents and spouses, plus $25/month to HSA.

• Vision and Dental Insurance: Dental Buy-up plan option, 50% company contributions to premiums for both employees, dependents and spouses for both.

• Employee Assistance Program: 100% confidential and free.

• Employer paid Short Term Disability + $50,000 Life Insurance

• Parental leave: 12 weeks of company paid primary caregiver leave, 3 weeks of company paid secondary caregiver leave, $1,500 new parent bonus, and 4 week flexible return to work plan.

• Wellbeing support: Subsidized up to 80% ClassPass subscription.

• Referral bonus: Earn rewards for bringing in new talent.

Who you are

• 2+ years in a closing sales role, SaaS experience is a must but hunger and skill matters more than industry tenure.

• Self-directed, coachable, and driven to continuously improve. You seek feedback on your calls, your pipeline, and your positioning — and act on it within the next deal, not the next quarter.

jobs.title: Legal Engineer
jobs.description:
ABOUT LAWHIVE

Lawhive is a global, AI-native law firm. Operating in the US and UK, we’ve built our own agentic operating system for legal services.

We partner with leading Main Street law firms to give lawyers and back-office teams the AI platform, marketing, and operational support to grow faster than they could alone. Our specialized AI agent for legal work, Lawrence, works alongside lawyers, putting human legal judgment right where it belongs: at the center of every matter.

We most recently raised a $60M Series B at a $685M valuation, from investors including Google Ventures, TQ Ventures, Mitch Rales, Balderton Capital and Premier League footballers Harry Maguire and Reece James. In the last few years we've hit milestone after milestone, raising over $110M in funding. Today, we're on track to exceed $100 million in annual revenue, and we have offices in London, New York, Austin, and Phoenix.

So if you want your work to have real, tangible impact as we redefine an entire industry, Lawhive is where you can make it happen.



THE ROLE

We're hiring our first Legal Engineer focused on immigration and removal defense in the US. You'll be a practicing (or previously practicing) deportation defense attorney who wants to build the tools, not just use them.

You'll work in two directions. With Product and Engineering, you'll shape deportation-specific functionality in Lawhive: how matters are opened, how deadlines and hearings are tracked, how filings are drafted and checked. With our partner firms, you'll configure Lawhive around how their attorneys and staff actually work, and keep tuning it until it saves them real time.

This is a hands-on role. You'll write workflows and prompts, test outputs against your own legal judgement, and decide what good looks like for a removal defense practice.

You'll start with an established immigration firm with offices and clients across the US. The firm handles much more than removal defense, so Lawhive needs to support its whole caseload.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Build with Product

 - Act as the subject-matter lead for removal defense: map the end-to-end matter lifecycle, from intake and NTA review through master and individual hearings, relief applications, BIA appeals and bond.

 - Turn that knowledge into product requirements, workflows and acceptance criteria that engineers can build against.

 - Design, test and refine the prompts, templates and checks our AI agent uses for immigration work (for example, EOIR filings, I-589 and cancellation of removal packages, evidence indexes, country conditions research).

 - Build evaluation sets from real matter types and judge output quality as a practitioner would.

 - Keep the product current as policy, EOIR practice and agency guidance change, aligning with our Legal Data librarian, maintaining the firm's context layer.

Work with partner firms

 - Spend time with attorneys, paralegals and intake teams to understand where time is lost, then fix it in the product or in their setup.

 - Run training and workshops so firms use more of the platform, and follow up on adoption.

 - Measure the effect: time per matter, filing turnaround, matters handled per attorney.

 - Bring firm feedback back to Product and help decide what gets built next.

Grow the function

 - Write playbooks for configuring and supporting immigration firms, so the next legal engineer can pick them up.

 - Help us decide how this model extends to other immigration practice areas.



 


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - JD and active admission to at least one US state bar.

 - 3+ years practicing removal defense, with your own caseload in immigration court: detained or non-detained, master and individual hearings, relief applications and appeals.

 - Familiarity with federal court work for immigration clients, such as habeas petitions and mandamus actions.

 - A clear view of where immigration practices lose time, and ideas for fixing it.

 - Hands-on comfort with technology. You've built workflows, templates or automations, set up a case management system or used generative AI seriously in your own practice. You don't need to be a programmer.

 - Good judgement on AI risk in a high-stakes practice area: what can be automated, what needs attorney review, and how to tell the difference.

 - Clear communication with both attorneys and engineers. You can explain a cancellation of removal standard to a developer and a data model to a managing partner.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and with setting your own priorities in a fast-moving team.

 


INTERVIEW PROCESS

 - Introductory call with our Talent team

 - 1:1 with your hiring manager

 - Practical skills assessment

 - Values interview with one of our Founders

 - We offer!

 


BENEFITS

 - 🩺 Healthcare benefits: 'Premium' plan with 100% employee cover and 50% dependent cover

 - ✈️ Vacation: 20 days + 11 Federal holidays + 1 day of Birthday leave

 - 💰 401k: Matching contribution up to 2% of salary

 - 💰 Meaningful early-stage share options

 - 🌍 Work from anywhere for a month

 - 💻 Top-spec Macbook

 - ⛳️ Regular team building activities and socials!

 


DIVERSITY AT LAWHIVE

At Lawhive we know that diversity of thought is critical to delivering outlier outcomes. As such, we’re always working hard to ensure we build a diverse, inclusive team. We’re not yet where we want to be but as we scale we’ll only ever increase the focus we apply to this.

The Feinberg Mezzanine Observation Unit is a 43-bed unit falling under the umbrella of the Emergency Department. The Clinical Nurse reflects the mission, vision, and values of NM, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

Based on the NMH framework for practice, the registered professional clinical nurse (RN) is accountable and responsible for the provision and coordination of clinically competent, evidence-based care for an assigned group of patients that includes diagnosis, outcome identification, planning, implementation and evaluation. The nurse adheres to the ANA Scope and Standards of Professional Nursing, the Code of Ethics, and the Nursing Social Policy Statement.   As a member of the clinical care and unit team, the RN participates in decision-making, teaching, mentoring, and collaboration with the multidisciplinary team to advance the patient plan of care, achieve exceptional outcomes and enhance unit operations.  The RN exemplifies the components of what it means to be an NMH nurse, reflects the Mission, Vision, and Values of Northwestern Memorial, adheres to the organization’s Code of Ethics and Corporate Compliance Program, and complies with all relevant policies, procedures, guidelines and all other regulatory and accreditation standards.

Responsibilities:

The role of the professional clinical nurse is unique and essential to the care of the patient.  The nurse demonstrates that unique and essential function through the framework for nursing practice.

Advocate:

• Practices in accordance with the patient centered care model
• Develops an individualized age-specific culturally sensitive nursing plan of care for the patient that is based on the nursing process
• Incorporates the role of patient advocate into the plan of care
• Uses a team approach to develop and achieve daily patient-centered individualized care goals
• Acknowledges and values the contributions of the patient’s significant others as an integral part of the plan of care
• Identifies potential conflict situations and facilitates resolution using established communication channels

Clinical Expert:

• Identifies situations that require further intervention and escalates appropriately; Consults appropriate experts and resources when needed
• Participates in the formation, implementation and evaluation of team goals
• Appropriately delegates and supervises interventions to implement the plan of care
• Conveys complete, timely and accurate information at hand off at the bedside or any hand off
• Adheres to ethical standards of practice

Community Volunteer:

• Participates in one or more volunteer initiatives annually, Northwestern Memorial organized or on his/her own

Compassionate:

• Proactively responds to patient concerns such as speaking to patients about possible/expected delays in plan of care
• Treats patients, families, visitors and staff in a caring manner with respect and dignity

Required:

jobs.title: Embryologist
jobs.description:
Who is Spring Fertility?

We are a passionate, dedicated team of leading physicians and scientists who have trained at some of the world’s top research hospitals and fertility centers. Together, we are building the fastest-growing fertility group in the country, grounded in clinical excellence and innovation. We deliver deeply patient-centric, individualized, and compassionate care, recognizing that every journey is unique. Our mission is to partner with patients to help them achieve their goals, whatever those may be. We believe everyone deserves the opportunity to build a family if they choose, and our team is committed to guiding and supporting patients every step of the way.

Why should you join our team?

We are a mission-driven organization seeking motivated, high-performing professionals who are eager to innovate and make an impact. As we build a first-class fertility practice, we balance excellence with a culture that values collaboration, positivity, and enjoyment in the work we do. We are growing rapidly and are deeply committed to the professional and personal development of our team. Guided by optimism, compassion, and teamwork, we are united by a shared dedication to putting patients first.

Role Summary

This position is responsible for performing high quality IVF laboratory medical procedures. The embryologist consults and advises other staff groups/members regarding IVF laboratory procedures and outcomes, and human assisted reproductive techniques (ART). The embryologist works in a collaborative relationship with the IVF Laboratory Supervisor and other team members, as well as with other Spring Fertility departments as needed. The Embryologist are required to rotate in Andrology/Endocrinology laboratory as needed to cover or help as needed. The Embryologist position requires the candidate to be proficient and independent in all basic and advanced IVF laboratory procedures.

Day to day duties include:

• Provide high quality service to couples seeking treatment for infertility, including diagnostic and therapeutic services.

• Conducts the full range of basic and advance ART laboratory procedure under the direction of the Laboratory Director

• Works together with Laboratory Director to coordinate work for an effective use of resources.

• Works collaboratively with the IVF Laboratory Director and the IVF team to proactively identify evolving “best practices” as well as area of improvement in the Laboratory process and department operations.

• Complies with regulations and laws for human ART in U.S. and California, adheres to the policy and rules of SPRING Fertility, and assures that works is performed in accordance with ASRM standards.

• Scrupulously follows laboratory and clinic SOPs as well as comply with all safety policies and standards.

• Meets quality standards and numerical goals for laboratory procedures, as set by Laboratory Director.

• Conducts at required standards all the ART tasks, including but not limited to the following procedure: ICSI (be at same level with other embryologist for fertilization rate 90%), biopsy (70% implantation rate and <3% no call rate), eggs vitrification (about 4 years of experience required to be independent on full case), and embryos vitrification (about 4 years of experience required to be independent on full case), eggs warming (about 4 years of experience required to be independent on full case, goal is 94% survival rate) and embryo warming (goal is >95% survival rate), media and dishes set up, eggs retrievals, sperm preparation, eggs inseminations, fertilization checks, stripping of cumulus cells for ICSI procedure, embryo grading (Gardner grading), participates in PT external and internal, successfully performs embryo transfers of fresh and frozen embryos.

• Communicate effectively and compassionately with patients and other SPRING Fertility team members.

• Conducts daily quality control activities

• Performs all ancillaries’ duties as request to maintain a clean and operating laboratory, including cleaning, equipment maintenance and inventory control.

Education, Licenses, Certifications

• Bachelors in Science in Biological or Chemistry required; degree in reproductive Biology preferred

• Technical Supervisor certification from the American Board of Bioanalysis (ABB) within two years from when eligible.

• Minimum of 5 years of experience in embryology field.

• Good command of written and spoken English.

Employment Type

This is a full time exempt onsite position that requires early hours, rotating weekends and holidays.

Compensation

The salary range for this role is 70,000-150,000. Salary is based on several factors including job related knowledge and skill set level for embryology, depth of experience, certifications and/or degrees.

Benefits

Investing in You Today and Tomorrow

Supporting your well-being

• Competitive medical, dental, and vision plans

• Paid time off to recharge and enjoy personal time

• Access to BetterHelp therapy sessions for mental and emotional wellness

• Commuter benefits and discounted rates on home, auto, and pet insurance

Investing in your future

• 401(k) with up to a 4% company match

• Comprehensive fertility and parental leave benefits

• Career development opportunities in a fast-growing organization

• Employer-paid life and disability insurance

*Temporary and contract roles may not be eligible for all benefits listed above

Don’t have it all? We still welcome you to apply!

At Spring Fertility, we believe that everyone who wants a family deserves to have one, regardless of gender, sexual orientation, race, ethnicity, or religion. Just as we acknowledge and value the diversity of goals, life experiences, and unique paths to parenthood among our patients, we also actively celebrate diversity within our organization. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to a safe and inclusive work environment for all. We recognize that diversity among our team allows us to not only more effectively serve our patients, but also to advance innovation and opportunity within our field. We encourage qualified applicants of every background, ability, and life experience to apply to our employment opportunities.

We are scientists. We are humanists. We are passionate about fertility.

Spring Fertility will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or to receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please give us a call.

More than 1,500 firms in 60 countries use Addepar to manage and advise on nearly $10 trillion in assets. Its open platform integrates with 650 software, data and consulting partners to power end-to-end investment operations across firms of all sizes and levels of complexity. Addepar supports clients worldwide with offices in New York City, Salt Lake City, São Paulo, London, Edinburgh, Geneva, Warsaw, Dubai, Pune and Singapore.

The Program

We are currently seeking a Data Engineering Intern to join our Portfolio Data Engineering team in New York City for Summer 2027.

Being a part of the AddeU Internship Program, you will be working on meaningful project(s) that you can feel proud of and present back to the company at the end of the experience. In addition to having a supporting manager and mentor, we have a fantastic onboarding program to get you acclimated and ready for your time with us. Fun events and super cool swag are also included!

Our Portfolio Data Engineering team builds and maintains the data pipelines that bring portfolio data into Addepar's platform for our Enterprise and Hyperscaler clients. With enterprise project volume expected to grow significantly over the next year, we are looking for a Data Engineering Intern to help keep those pipelines running smoothly while improving the tooling behind them. If you are excited about working with complex financial data at scale and building more reliable, efficient data pipelines, we want to hear from you!

As a Data Engineering Intern, you will split your time between supporting day-to-day feed maintenance and working on tooling improvements, contributing to the next-generation data pipeline while gaining significant exposure to production data systems.

This role is based full-time in our New York office and requires in-person attendance for the duration of the internship. Dates are currently set for June - August 2027 but please advise your recruiter if you have any timing constraints. Relocation assistance is not offered. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States for any employer without requiring current or future visa sponsorship (for example, employment-based visas such as H-1B, F-1/OPT, or similar), and must be authorized to begin work in the U.S. on their first day of employment.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis between November 2026 and March 2027. We encourage you to apply early, as we may close the posting once the program is filled.

What You'll Do

• Support day-to-day maintenance of portfolio data feeds and reconciliation workflows for Enterprise and Hyperscaler clients

• Work on tooling improvements that increase pipeline reliability, data quality, and operational efficiency

• Contribute to the next-generation data pipeline on well-scoped deliverables

Who You Are

• Able to commit to the full 12-week program, June 7th, 2027 - August 27th, 2027

• Proficiency in Python and SQL

• Strong problem-solving skills and attention to data quality

• Ability to work collaboratively in a team-oriented environment
